plan.definitions_to_test:
SIX ROWS, AND THE MERGERS THAT GOT US TO SIX. Both audits prove most of the eighteen candidates are one object. Two lemmas, to be stated in the paper and asserted in code, not measured:

L1 (retraction = reversal). ∪_{|S|≤b} retract(S) = ∪_{|σ|≤b} reverse(σ), because retract(S) is the disjoint union of reverse(σ) over σ ⊆ S. Measured 0 differences / 573 problems. So C6 and C16's reversal families ARE the retraction family unless a filter breaks the union (only C16's cost filter does).
L2 (screens are width-neutral). Under the centre gate Θ(∅) is a single point, and for any claim k whose retraction leaves Z0 valid, Θ({k}) = Θ(∅). Hence the hull over the load-bearing set = the hull over all of K. Measured 250/250 and 300/300 (C12), and re-measured by both audits. Direction (4) therefore has NO width content; it is a cost result.

The six:

D0 — r_val. THE REFERENCE, not a candidate. Direction: none (the defect). Its operational content is the dead-band lemma: hedging out to r_val−1 costs exactly zero, so the interval r_val licenses IS the plain CI on the elicited set. It therefore enters the width table as the PLAIN row and is graded on P(r_val = 1) with a declared censoring convention. This is the honest way to put the incumbent in the same table as its replacements.

D1 — RH_j, the retraction hull on elicited claims. Direction (1). ∪_{S⊆K,|S|≤j} Θ(cl(Ĉ, K∖S)), τ by the IDA convention. This single object IS C1 (RHIG), C6 (flip hull, by L1), C7 (R_b), C8 (J-hedge), C10 (H_m), C11 (U_b's interval, by L2), C12's order-≤2 hedge (by L2), C14 (Hull_t, by L2), C15 (SEL at δ=0, proved identical by its own G2). Reported as a LADDER j = 0…m with j = m ≡ the blanket hedge ≡ enumeration of total effects. This is the headline and the only row with genuine width content.

D2 — CRH_j, the canonical retraction hull. Direction (1), variant. C2. Same construction indexed by minimal generating subsets of Or(G0) = dir(G0)∖dir(Ĉ), so it is a function of (Ĉ, G0) alone. It earns its slot on exactly one falsifiable question that no other row can answer: is the phrasing attack real (append Meek-implied claims: RH_1's width moves on 10.7–12.7% of problems, CRH on 0% by construction), and what does invariance cost (CRH_1 ⊇ RH_1 on 150/150, strictly wider on 15.3%)? If the attack is real and the cost is small, CRH is the definition to publish; if not, RH is.

D3 — LRH(h=0, b), the hop-screened hull. Direction (2) — "do not require that NO element breaks", instantiated as a restricted family. C9, subsuming C16's cost-filtered ball (c = hop) and C14's anchor screen at the interval level. It is the ONLY candidate that can exclude the true DAG, so it is the only one for which the soundness column is not a tautology, and it is simultaneously the free one-BFS baseline the screen must beat. Its width is ≤ RH_1's by monotonicity always (0/152 counterexamples), so the live question is coverage-at-matched-width, graded per false-claim-placement level.

D4 — SAT, the saturation/fractional profile (j_val, j_sat, t_val). Direction (3) — a central summary replacing the minimum. C13's fractional boundary t_val, C2's j_sat, C17's j_val, on one common claim-budget currency. Not an interval; graded on spread inside the r_val = 1 stratum, on responsiveness to planted error (C13 measured P(down)/P(up) = 4.08 for t_val against r_val tie 0.859), and on the currency identity floor(t_val)+1 = r_val.

D5 — Λ, the claim-leverage ranking. Direction (4). C1's ℓ, C5, C6, C7, C15's μ, C12's L, C14's S(K). By L2 it contributes nothing to width, so it enters (a) as a RANKING scored against a LOAD-BEARING label (does retracting k change Θ), never against falsity, with the data-free reversibility ranker as the null; and (b) as a COST result: the same interval from |L| fibre enumerations instead of |K|.

RETIRED WITH REASONS, so nobody re-litigates: C3, C4, C5, C11, C14, C15, C17, C18 are D1 or D5 under other names (L1/L2); C4 is an evaluation protocol, not a radius, and its stratified-calibration idea is absorbed into the width rule below; C18's certified core is D5 plus a certificate whose interval is measured identical to the blanket on 1650/1650.

NON-CANDIDATE MANDATORY ROWS: PLAIN (point on the elicited set, uniformly inflated — the stand-in for DoubleML/TabPFN/CausalPFN/Do-PFN, declared as a stand-in because none of them is runnable here); BLANKET (= RH_m); PERM (random claim subset matched on EFFECTIVE retractions, i.e. claims whose retraction strictly enlarges the extension set, not on |L|); REVBASE (rank claims by how many extensions of Ĉ disagree with them — data-free, never touches τ, the SEM or the query).
plan.experiment:
CWF — THE COVERAGE–WIDTH FRONTIER SWEEP. One enumeration per problem, six read-offs, one table. It replaces both proposed experiments, which the audits show cannot fail in the directions they claim to test (MASKSWEEP's certificate rule is a tautology for twelve of eighteen candidates; SIT's primary is a deterministic function of structure that does not move with the planted error).

THE ONE CHANGE THAT MAKES IT DECIDE ANYTHING: coverage is the outcome and width is its price, computed together, on the full population, with one scalar per row applied to the WHOLE interval. Both audits independently arrive here. The pilot already shows why: budget 0 covers 0.618 at 0.002× blanket width, budget 1 covers 0.840 at 0.699×, budget 2 covers 1.000 at 0.936× — so the first budget reaching 95% costs 93.6% of the blanket, a 6.4% saving. Read without the coverage column, budget 1's mean ν of 0.704 looks like a 30% win and its atom of 0.653 looks like a degeneracy verdict. Both readings are wrong for the same missing column.

UNIT. One problem = (D*, Ĉ = dag_to_cpdag(D*) — the TRUE class, never estimated; one query (X,Y); one SEM; one claim support S_K ⊆ und(Ĉ)). One query per graph, so no damage is ever averaged across the queries of a graph.

PAIRED ERROR ARMS, INSIDE THE PROBLEM. j_true ∈ {0,1,2} false claims are drawn on the SAME (D*, Ĉ, query, SEM, S_K). A problem is admitted only if all three arms survive Meek closure and the centre gate — the intersection, because both gates read K_asserted and are therefore post-treatment (measured: verdicts differ across arms on 50/250 and 48/250; only 44% usable in all three). This removes the j_true-dependent acceptance gradient (56.7/46.4/32.5%) without any within-graph averaging.

FACTORIAL, 27 CELLS, crossed and filled to equal size:
 A. ambiguity band u = |und(Ĉ)| ∈ {[3,5], [6,8], [9,12]}. u, not n, is the cost and richness driver: measured |ext| mean 8.5 / 21.6 / 58, enumeration 0.38 / 2.8 / 15–78 ms. n ∈ {8,10,12,14} and p ∈ [0.14,0.34] are covariates drawn within cell and post-stratified, because rejection on the u band selects p.
 B. false-claim placement ∈ {uniform, hop-0-concentrated, hop≥2-concentrated}. Declared as an axis because every hop-localised row is otherwise graded against an undisclosed uniform prior (measured flip hops 270/102/49/19/2 at hops 0–4, plus 11.6% of claims not connected to the query at all).
 C. elicitation saturation s = m/u ∈ {1/3, 2/3, 1}, so "the analyst said more" is not confounded with "the class was wider". m is sampled from s, and the free-edge count u − m is recorded as a covariate.
Target 400 admitted problems per cell = 10,800.

QUERY DRAW, NO ORACLE. (X,Y) is drawn among ordered pairs connected in Ĉ's skeleton, NOT conditioned on Y ∈ de_{D*}(X). Measured consequence, and it is large: P(Y ∈ de_{D*}(X)) = 0.277, so 72% of honestly drawn queries have a zero true effect. The τ* = 0 stratum is reported as a co-primary, never dropped — it is the stratum where the class disputes causation and the analyst most needs a hedge.

READ-OFF LAYER, RE-RUN ON THE SAME CACHE (24 passes, seconds each): n_obs ∈ {250, 1000, 10000}; adjustment map Z_opt vs Z_pa; calibration by whole-interval scaling vs additive pad in ŝe units; IDA vs naive estimand.

WIDTH RULE, THE METRIC'S OWN. Every row emits a per-problem interval with a centre: [lo − z·ŝe, hi + z·ŝe], z = 1.96, ŝe from the row's OWN adjustment set (never optimal_adjustment_set_dag on D*). Split by cell into calibration and evaluation halves. Fit ONE scalar s ≥ 0 per row on the calibration half, multiplying the whole interval about its centre, to reach exactly 0.95 empirical coverage of τ*; report mean width on the held-out half. Because every interval carries a strictly positive sampling half, EVERY row is calibratable — the "UNCALIBRATABLE" verdict that pre-satisfied SIT's decision rule (2) is an artefact of scaling only the ignorance half and is deleted. Calibration is fitted on the SAME stratum that is reported (marginal calibration plus stratified reporting leaks ~4 coverage points toward the narrow rows). The ignorance-only two-knob rule with the λ ≥ 1 soundness floor is kept as a declared sensitivity, because it is the rule under which the theorem and the published object are the same object.

DECLARED PRIOR. π over j_true is the single parameter that sets the headline. Primary π₁ = (0.50, 0.35, 0.15); sensitivities π = δ₀, δ₁, δ₂ and uniform. The headline is published as a CURVE over π with π₁ marked, so a reader who disagrees reads their own number off the line. It is never a hidden mixture.
plan.prespecified_outcomes:
PRIMARY, ONE SCALAR. ρ★ = W95(RH_{b*}) / W95(BLANKET), where b* is the smallest budget whose raw (s = 1) coverage reaches 0.95 on the calibration half, W95 is the mean calibrated width on the held-out half, under π₁, n_obs = 1000, map Z_opt, IDA convention, FULL population, equal cell weights, BCa bootstrap over problems (B = 2000) clustered on the problem and stratified by cell.

CO-PRIMARY, MANDATORY, SAME CELL OF THE TABLE (the audits' measurement forces this and it cannot be an appendix): ρ★ recomputed on (i) the direction-preserving stratum, where every DAG in the class agrees that Y ∈ de(X), and (ii) the direction-disputed stratum. Measured on 800 problems this session: 73.1% of informative problems contain at least one non-descendant world; the direction-preserving width is only 33.5% of the blanket width on average and is EXACTLY ZERO on 57.9% of informative problems. Two thirds of the "ignorance" this literature hedges is the class disagreeing about whether X causes Y at all, not about which confounders to adjust for. If that is not printed, the width table is a table about causal-order disputes wearing an adjustment-set label.

DEGENERACY STATISTIC, BASELINE-RELATIVE (this de-confounds |K|, which otherwise moves the atom mechanically 0.842 → 0.674 → 0.653 as the G0 baseline width share falls 0.339 → 0.087 → 0.000):
 ν_rel = (width(hull) − width(G0)) / (width(BLANKET) − width(G0)), on the stratum where the denominator > 0. Reported as an ECDF with P(=0), P(=1), interior mass and distinct-value count, stratified on whether the hull swallows a non-descendant world.

THRESHOLDS, FIXED NOW.
 T1 SELECTIVE WIDENING IS A WIDTH METHOD iff ρ★(π = δ₁) ≤ 0.85 with BCa upper end < 0.95.
 T2 RESPONSIVENESS: the winning row must CHANGE with π — PLAIN at π = δ₀, RH_{b≥1} at π = δ₁. If the same row wins at both, the width table is reporting the generator, not the method. (SIT's ρ* = 0.76 in the no-damage arm, already under its own threshold, is exactly this failure.)
 T3 RELOCATION: P(ν_rel = 1) ≥ 0.60 at b* ⇒ the r_val atom has moved from the value 1 to the value 1 and the defect is renamed, not fixed. Reported as such, with the j_sat / t_val histogram beside it.
 T4 AGAINST UNIFORM INFLATION: W95(PLAIN) / W95(RH_{b*}) ≥ 2 at π = δ₁. Reported but explicitly NOT the headline — it is a comparison against uniformly inflating a zero-ignorance report and is the weakest available baseline.
 T5 THE SCREEN'S EXCHANGE RATE: LRH is never wider than RH by monotonicity (0/152), so it is graded on coverage at matched calibrated width, per placement level. Publishable only if the coverage it forfeits is under 2 points in the uniform placement arm.
 T6 PHRASING: fraction of problems where appending Meek-implied claims moves RH_1's calibrated width (predict 0.08–0.15) against CRH's 0 by construction; plus CRH_1/RH_1 width ratio (predict ≥ 1.00, strictly > 1 on ~15%). CRH replaces RH as the published definition iff T6's first number exceeds 0.10 and the ratio is under 1.05.
 T7 RETRIEVAL: precision@1 of Λ against the LOAD-BEARING label minus precision@1 of REVBASE ≥ 0.10, permutation CI excluding 0. Against the FALSITY label the paper claims nothing and reports the refutation: Λ 0.494, REVBASE 0.660, chance 0.352 — a data-free graph statistic beats the leverage score, and the apparent lift is the Meek-consistency rejection sampler. Within-MEC false-claim retrieval is impossible under the paper's own premise; that is a result, stated up front.
 T8 SAT: t_val must take ≥ 8 distinct values with IQR ≥ 0.10 inside the r_val = 1 stratum, and P(down)/P(up) ≥ 2 under planted error while r_val ties on ≥ 75% of the same pairs.
 T9 COST: fibre-enumeration counts per row, so D5 can be published as what it is — the same interval from |L| enumerations instead of |K|.

FRONT-PAGE NUMBERS, printed before any width: the Meek-refusal rate (bounds the paper's premise that no existing check flags a false-but-consistent K); the two centre-gate branches separately; P(Z0 = ∅), measured 0.435; P(class carries ≤ 1 distinct adjustment set), measured 0.88; the informative share; the τ* = 0 share, measured 0.72 under an honest query draw.
plan.controls:
CONTROLS THAT CAN ACTUALLY FAIL (the audits found three of five proposed controls were theorems about the numpy).
 C1 MASK IDENTITY. On a 2% subsample, recompute ext(cl(Ĉ,K')) via apply_orientations + enumerate_dag_extensions and require equality with the bitmask, and apply_orientations None exactly when the mask is empty. Verified 0/4860. One violation voids the run.
 C2 τ CONVENTION ON EVERY EXTENSION, not only D*: assert τ_i = 0 exactly when Y ∉ de_{D_i}(X), and assert O*(D_i) is a valid adjustment set in D_i whenever amenable. The version that checks only D* is vacuous, because the query draw forces τ(D*) = true_total_effect.
 C3 ext(G0) ⊆ ext(Ĉ), and no extension of G0 carries a v-structure absent from Ĉ.
 C4 EMPTY HULL → NaN, never width 0. Only the filtered rows (LRH, CRH) can be empty, and a silent 0 would fabricate a zero-width certificate and then a soundness verdict.
 C5 `if Z0 is not None`, never truthiness. The empty set is falsy and is the adjustment set on 43.5% of problems, correlated with the outcome.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS.
 N1 REVBASE — the data-free reversibility ranker, as the null for D5. This is the control that convicts direction (4); a uniform permutation is too weak and would certify Λ's 0.494 as a large lift.
 N2 PERM — random claim subset matched on EFFECTIVE retractions (claims whose retraction strictly enlarges the extension set), because a random claim is more often Meek-redundant than a load-bearing one and |L|-matching is unfair in an unexamined direction. B = 1000 draws with a shared permutation index across problems; calibration refit per draw.
 N3 CONSTRUCTED PLACEBO — append a synthetic component structurally disconnected from D* and assert bit-identity of every reported number. The discovered variant (a component vertex-disjoint from Z0 ∪ O*) is NOT used: it does not exclude the causal nodes de(X) ∩ an(Y), so it is a false-alarm generator wired to the strongest branch of the decision tree (1/70 eligible components already contained a causal node).
 N4 PADDING ATTACK — append the Meek-implied orientations G0 already entails, leaving G0 and Z0 bit-identical. CRH must be bit-identical; RH is predicted to move; φ-style ratios are predicted to move DOWNWARD, i.e. the expert who says more looks safer.
 N5 HONEST-ANALYST ARM (j_true = 0). Everything hedged is paid and nothing earned; b* must be 0 and PLAIN must win.

POSITIVE CONTROL AND ITS HONEST LABEL.
 P1 At matched budget the union hulls contain τ* by construction (D* disagrees with K exactly on the flip set, so S = S_flip is in the union; measured 0/573 failures). This is a REGRESSION ASSERTION on the cache, not evidence for the theorem, and the paper must say so. Soundness is graded instead at a budget chosen WITHOUT j_true (a fixed b, or a declared data-free rule), reported as a coverage curve over b. There it has teeth only for LRH and CRH, the rows that can exclude D*, which is why LRH is in the six.

CONFOUND CONTROLS.
 F1 Paired j_true on the intersection population (all three arms admitted), which removes the acceptance gradient.
 F2 Post-stratify p to a common distribution within each u band; report the realised p distribution per cell.
 F3 Report each arm only on the cells where it is defined: b = 2 needs m ≥ 2, and the hop-concentrated placement is identical to uniform in cells with no hop-0 claim.
 F4 Both centre-gate branches split and reported; Z0 defined by a convention that exists on every G0 (the minimal element of all_valid_adjustment_sets_mpdag when optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag is None or invalid), because the gate as written strips near-query ambiguity at 2.6× the rate — exactly where the paper's own hop law puts the damage.
 F5 CURRENCY. For every fibre, record the lattice distance from G0 of cl(Ĉ, K′) alongside the claim budget, so the hop currency of r_val and the claim currency of everything else are compared on one scale. The relocation test runs only on the common scale (measured agreement is 0.60, and P(j_val = 1 | r_val = 1) = 0.788, below any 0.95 threshold for a units reason).
 F6 r_val PROVENANCE with the convention declared BEFORE the run: P(r_val = 1 | r_val finite), tolerance ±0.10 around the paper's 0.689, censoring rule stated. Measured 0.660 including censored and 0.868 excluding — the paper's number sits between the two conventions, so the check passes or fails on an undeclared choice unless it is fixed now. Lattice arm capped at u ≤ 7 (enumerate_space is 3^u).
 F7 SCALE. Publish median beside every mean, a scale-free width (width / ŝe and width / |τ*|), and the fraction of hull endpoints supplied by the τ = 0 convention. Measured corr(width, |τ*|) = 0.716, so absolute widths are denominated in random_sem's Uniform(0.3,1.5) weight draw and are not commensurable with anything a competitor would report on real data.
 F8 DETERMINISM. Named SeedSequence substreams for graph / query / claims / error / SEM / data (the sketched order draws the error before the SEM, so the SEM is not in fact shared across arms); zero-padded node labels (n00…n13 — plain n0…n12 sorts as n0, n1, n10, n11, n2 and the hand-written OLS layer indexes on MPDAG.nodes); one cell rerun under two PYTHONHASHSEED values, bit-identical.
 F9 ORDERING SENSITIVITY. The row ordering must be unchanged across n_obs ∈ {250, 1000, 10000}, both maps, both calibration rules, and both estimand conventions. A table whose ordering moves with the convention is reporting the convention.
 F10 GENERATOR SENSITIVITY. ER-plus-random-topological-order is one family; add one block/scale-free family and, if any real CPDAG corpus can be had, one cell of it. ρ★ is declared non-transportable in the paper.
plan.implementation_plan:
Layout under /Users/josecosta/mugango/output/2026-09-07_radius-redef/cwf/, run with PYTHONPATH=/Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src. Five files; nothing but cache.py touches the repository.

cache.py — ONE enumeration per problem, and it is the entire cost.

    def make_cache(ss, cell):                     # ss = numpy SeedSequence, spawned per stream
        rg, rq, rk, re_, rs, rd = (default_rng(s) for s in ss.spawn(6))
        D  = random_dag(rg, n, p)                 # tests/demo/test_evaluate.py:136, labels n%02d
        C  = dag_to_cpdag(D)                      # the TRUE class
        U  = sorted(C.undirected_edges)           # ALL of them, not just K's support
        if not (cell.u_lo <= len(U) <= cell.u_hi): return None
        ext = enumerate_dag_extensions(C)         # <-- the one expensive call, 2**|U|
        A  = np.array([[Dp.is_directed_edge(a,b) for (a,b) in U] for Dp in ext])   # |ext| x |U|
        (X,Y) = uniform over ordered pairs connected in C.skeleton()   # NO oracle on descendance
        desc = np.array([Y in Dp.descendants(X) for Dp in ext])
        sem  = random_sem(D, rs)
        Ostar = [None if not d else frozenset(optimal_adjustment_set_dag(Dp,X,Y))
                 for Dp,d in zip(ext,desc)]
        tau_pop = [0.0 if not d else adjusted_estimand(sem,X,Y,O) for O,d in zip(Ostar,desc)]
        star = index of D in ext ; hop = one BFS over C.skeleton() from {X,Y}
        S    = rd.multivariate_normal(zeros, sem.covariance(), n_obs)  # centred; sigma-hat uses n-p
        ols  = cache keyed on frozenset(Z) -> (coef, se) from ONE second-moment solve

A is over ALL undirected edges, which is the fix that lets CRH (Meek-implied orientations) and REVBASE (column disagreement counts) come off the same cache. Every fibre is then a bitmask and no further Meek closure or enumeration is ever run:

    retract(A, S)      = A[:, [c for c in cols if c not in S]].all(axis=1)
    hull(mask)         = (tau[mask].min(), tau[mask].max())  if mask.any() else NaN
    width(mask)        = hi - lo

Claims: sample S_K ⊆ U of size m = round(s·u), orient truthfully from D* (column c is true iff A[star,c]), flip the placement-drawn set E of size j_true. G0's mask = retract-nothing on the asserted columns. Admit the problem only if all three j_true arms give a non-empty mask and pass the centre gate.

readoffs.py — six functions, each (cache, arm) -> (interval, aux). All one-liners over masks.
    RH_j    = union over |S| <= j of retract(A, K_asserted \ S)
    CRH_j   = the same over minimal generating subsets of Or(G0) = columns oriented in G0 but not in C
    LRH_b   = mask {i : dis(i) subset of T_0 and |dis(i)| <= b}, dis(i) read straight off A and hop
    SAT     = j_val / j_sat / t_val from the kappa-ordering of tau (nearest-first, deterministic key)
    LAMBDA  = width(retract(A,{k})) - width(G0) per claim; L = claims whose retraction breaks Z0-validity
    REVBASE = A[:,c].sum() per column, never touches tau, the SEM or the query
    r_val   = separate 300-problem loop through enumerate_space -> represented_dags -> covering_pairs
              -> neighbour_graph -> bfs_distances, capped at u <= 7, joined on problem_id

calib.py — bisect one scalar s >= 0 per row on the calibration half, scaling the whole interval about its centre to exactly 0.95 coverage; the ignorance-only two-knob rule with the lambda >= 1 floor as a sensitivity; BCa bootstrap clustered on problem, stratified by cell.

sanity.py — C1–C5, N3, F8 as assertions that abort the run, plus the three known-vacuous checks kept and RELABELLED as regression assertions (ladder endpoints, nesting, membership certificate). analyse.py regenerates every table from results.parquet, so no number is ever typed by hand.

CONCRETE BUGS TO FIX ON DAY ONE, all named by the audits and all live in the pilot code: `if Z else` (Z = empty on 43.5%); empty hull returning 0.0 instead of NaN; the cache built over K's m columns only; τ computed through optimal_adjustment_set_dag without the descendance branch (measured 19.8% of class DAGs mis-priced, with a witness: truth X ← C → Y with X → Y reports −1.2482 where the total effect is exactly 0); is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag returning False both for a real invalidity and for an empty extension set (assert non-empty separately); the error draw consuming the RNG before random_sem, which breaks the pairing the design claims.
plan.runtime:
MEASURED ON THIS MACHINE TODAY, not extrapolated. enumerate_dag_extensions is 2^u brute force (the repository's own docstring says so), and u is the only cost driver:

  u:            2     4     6     8    10    12    13
  |ext| mean:  3.5   8.5  21.6  30.9  58.4  56.0  60.0
  enum ms:     0.12  0.38  1.43  5.01 15.45 78.00 154.30

Full per-problem cache including dag_to_cpdag, the enumeration, the SEM draw, every O* and every population τ: 1.18 ms mean, 13.0 ms max over 300 problems at u ∈ [3,10]. Note the shape: |ext| grows 7× from u = 4 to u = 10 while cost grows 40×, so a richer equivalence class is expensive and the "class is small" objection is structural, not a sampling accident.

BUDGET. 27 cells × 400 admitted problems = 10,800 caches. Weighted across the three u bands (~0.4 / 3 / 40 ms) the mean cache is ~15 ms → ~160 s of pure cache. Rejection sampling dominates in the hard cells (wide band × saturated × hop≥2 placement, and the paired all-three-arms admission at 44%): budget 3–5× → 10–15 min. Read-offs are numpy bitmasks over ~11–60 rows and cost microseconds; the 24 re-run passes (n_obs × map × calibration rule × estimand) re-solve only the OLS per distinct adjustment set, and the measured mean distinct O* per class is 0.74 (max 6), so each pass is seconds. r_val lattice arm: 300 problems, capped at u ≤ 7 because enumerate_space is 3^u, ~39 ms each ≈ 12 s. Bootstrap B = 2000 over cached per-problem widths: seconds. Permutation B = 1000 re-selects index subsets over cached fibres: seconds.

TOTAL: 20–35 minutes single-core; under 5 minutes across 8 cores, since cells share no state and every problem is seeded from SHA-256 of (cell id, replicate). CPU only, numpy and the repository, no SAT solver and none needed.

DOMINANT RISK, named and capped: the u ∈ [9,12] band. Cap u at 12 (78 ms) and report any cell that fails to fill within 200,000 attempts. The cap is a scope statement, not a hidden constraint — every competitor row that needs the equivalence class (blanket, enumeration of total effects) pays the same 2^u, and on the graph sizes where TabPFN / CausalPFN / Do-PFN are the real competitors none of this is computable at all. Say that in the caption rather than letting 15 ms read as a claim about their regime.
plan.what_result_would_kill_the_idea:
SIX KILL CONDITIONS, each with the number that fires it. The first three kill the paper's bet; the last three void the run or relocate the defect.

K1 — THE WIDTH BET DIES. ρ★ > 0.85 at every budget and every π, with the BCa lower end above 0.85. Then the retraction hull is the blanket hedge with extra steps: damage being local does not cash out as hedging being cheap, because Meek closure cascades and retracting one claim reopens the chordal component that sets the blanket width. The pilot points straight at this — budget 2 is the first to reach 95% coverage and costs 0.936 of the blanket, a 6.4% saving, and the per-problem ratio is two-atom with 70–76% of mass at exactly 1. Output: a negative-results entry, letter C (an instrument that measured nothing), revive_if tied to a generator or a real-CPDAG corpus on which P(RH_1 = BLANKET | blanket width > 0) falls below 0.40 — the only regime where a selective hull has room to be narrower. The surviving contribution is then the budget-j containment theorem as a diagnostic plus the cost result (the same interval from |L| enumerations), and the blanket hedge owns the width row.

K2 — THE DEFECT IS RELOCATED, NOT REMOVED. P(ν_rel = 1) ≥ 0.60 at b*, with the j_sat / t_val histogram concentrated at ≤ 1. A minimum over a ball collapsing to 1 on 68.9% has become a hull collapsing to the blanket on a comparable majority. This must be reported as the same species of degeneracy, in those words, not as a new object.

K3 — THE TABLE IS NOT ABOUT ADJUSTMENT SETS. If, on the direction-preserving stratum, the informative share is under 10% in every cell, then two thirds or more of the hedged ignorance is the class disputing whether X causes Y at all. Measured this session: 73.1% of informative problems contain a non-descendant world, the direction-preserving width is 33.5% of the blanket, and it is exactly zero on 57.9% of informative problems. If that persists, the honest paper is about identification of causal direction under background knowledge, and the breakdown-radius framing is answering a question the benchmark barely contains.

K4 — NOTHING DISCRIMINATES. All six rows land within the bootstrap interval of each other on every cell. The measured mechanism is already visible: 88% of problems carry ≤ 1 distinct optimal adjustment set across the entire equivalence class, so no selector can differ from any other. If that survives the high-ambiguity cells, no selective-widening claim is testable on any generator this repository can enumerate, and the negative result is about the benchmark, not the method.

K5 — DIRECTION (4) HAS NO CONTENT. Λ fails to beat REVBASE on the load-bearing label by 0.10. Against the falsity label the refutation is already in hand (Λ 0.494, REVBASE 0.660, chance 0.352) and is stated in the paper as a result: within a Markov equivalence class, under the paper's own premise that K is consistent with the data, false-claim retrieval is impossible in principle. The ranked-list framing is then dropped entirely and Λ survives only as an enumeration order.

K6 — THE RUN IS VOID, NOT NEGATIVE. Any failure of the mask identity, the per-extension τ convention, ext(G0) ⊆ ext(Ĉ), or determinism under two PYTHONHASHSEED values. An implementation bug that produces a plausible width is the failure mode this whole design exists to make impossible to mistake for a finding, and the distinction is kept sharp: a failed control never becomes a result.

WHAT WOULD NOT KILL IT AND MUST NOT BE USED AS A DEFENCE: a large saving on a stratum that excludes zero-blanket-width problems; a raw-width comparison at unequal coverage; a win in the hop-concentrated placement arm alone, which is the arm whose error model was chosen to match the screen (C16 measured the selection increment moving +0.31% → +7.79% on exactly that switch); or the tautological containment of τ* at matched budget.
plan.open_risks:
R1 — THE PRIOR IS THE RESULT. π over how many elicited claims are false is unmeasurable, unverifiable and sets the headline. Publishing the width as a curve over π makes it honest, not solved. This is the Rosenbaum-Γ position and the paper should adopt it explicitly rather than defend a point value.

R2 — TRANSPORTABILITY. ρ★ is a statistic of Erdős–Rényi-plus-random-topological-order at u ≤ 12. The threshold "at least ~15% of problems carry a chordal component that supplies the blanket width and touches nothing near the query" is a generator property. No real CPDAG corpus is in scope here, and without one the number does not transfer.

R3 — SCALE AND COMMENSURABILITY. Widths are denominated in random_sem's Uniform(0.3,1.5) weights and the generator's path-length distribution; measured corr(width, |τ*|) = 0.716. Nothing in this table is comparable to a width DoubleML or a PFN would report on real data, and the PFN rows are a PLAIN-shaped stand-in because none of those methods is runnable here. That must be declared in the caption, not discovered in review.

R4 — THE ESTIMAND CONVENTION IS DOING MOST OF THE WORK. The IDA τ = 0 branch supplies about two thirds of the blanket width. Both conventions are run and reported, but the choice is a modelling commitment about what the estimand IS, and it changes the paper's subject.

R5 — SCOPE OF THE ENUMERATION. u ≤ 12 caps everything; enumerate_space is 3^u and caps the r_val provenance arm at u ≤ 7. The claim "cheaper than the baseline" is a constant-factor saving inside the same exponential, never a complexity class, and the earlier "scales where enumerate_space does not" phrasing stays withdrawn.

R6 — THE BACK-DOOR CHECK IS SUFFICIENT-ONLY. is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag could over-report invalidity relative to the generalised adjustment criterion. Measured 0 of 1475 disagreements at these sizes, so it is a low risk, but it is a risk that grows with graph size and should be re-measured in the u ∈ [9,12] band rather than assumed from the small cells.

R7 — POST-TREATMENT ADMISSION SURVIVES IN A WEAKER FORM. The intersection design fixes the paired comparison but selects the population toward problems whose K is Meek-consistent under all three flip counts, which is a benign-perturbation selection at the population level. The refusal rates are reported as the scope statement they are, and they bound the paper's own premise that no existing check flags a false-but-data-consistent K.

R8 — THE CENTRE GATE CANNOT BE FULLY REPAIRED. Giving Z0 a convention defined on every G0 keeps the near-query-ambiguity stratum in the population, but it changes what "the analyst's answer" means on the 12–19% of problems where the class does not identify one. The two branches are reported separately; there is no choice here that is neutral.

R9 — FINITE-SAMPLE HULL BIAS. Hull endpoints are a max and a min over estimated quantities and are upward biased in width, growing with the number of distinct adjustment sets entering the hull. Measured negligible at n_obs = 1000 (inflation +0.0002 for the selective row, −0.0023 for the blanket; population ρ 0.6898 vs finite 0.6896) because most extensions share the same O*, but that is a property of small classes and must be re-measured in the wide band.

R10 — THE MOST LIKELY OUTCOME IS THE NEGATIVE ONE, AND THE PAPER MUST BE WRITABLE EITHER WAY. Every pilot in both audits and both probes run today points at K1 and K2 firing together. The version of the paper that survives that is already visible: state L1 and L2 as lemmas (retraction = reversal; screens are width-neutral), publish the budget-j containment theorem in elicitation units as the contribution, publish the coverage–width frontier with the blanket hedge winning the width column, publish the impossibility of within-MEC false-claim retrieval as a result, and publish the measurement that two thirds of the hedged ignorance is a causal-order dispute. That is a defensible ICLR paper and it is a different paper from the one the breakdown radius was going to be. Deciding which one is being written is the choice this experiment forces, and it is Zé's to make once the frontier table exists.

refined.name: RHIG_j — Retraction-Hull Ignorance Interval (claim-indexed, effect-scale)
refined.formal_definition:
Keep the effect-scale lens of BIG_r, delete the hop ball, and index by the analyst's own statements.

SETTING. Let D* be the true DAG and C = dag_to_cpdag(D*) its CPDAG (the TRUE equivalence class; every number below is conditional on that, and nothing here is a claim under an estimated CPDAG). Let K = (k_1,…,k_m) be the elicited orientation claims, G0 = Meek(C, K) = apply_orientations(C, K) the analyst's MPDAG, assumed valid (apply_orientations returns None otherwise, and such a K is not an analyst state).

DECLARED PARAMETER: THE ADJUSTMENT MAP. A map Z(·) assigning to each DAG D a set Z(D) ⊆ V\{X,Y} that is a valid adjustment set for (X,Y) in D. Two are reported throughout: Z_opt(D) = optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D,X,Y) and Z_pa(D) = pa_D(X), the classical IDA map. The map is fixed once per table; cross-map comparisons are void (measured: same problems, same benchmark, calibrated width 0.4743 under Z_opt against 0.5748 for the blanket, but 0.6301 against 0.7655 under Z_pa on the population pilot — the ordering is preserved WITHIN each map and the levels are not comparable ACROSS maps).

THE OBJECT. Let ĈI(z) = [θ̂(z) − z_{1−α/2}·ŝe(z), θ̂(z) + z_{1−α/2}·ŝe(z)] be the ordinary confidence interval for the coefficient on X in the regression of Y on {X} ∪ z, computed from the analyst's own sample. For j = 0,1,…,m define the j-retraction hull

    H_j := ⋃_{S ⊆ K, |S| = j}  ext( Meek(C, K∖S) ),      RHIG_j := [ min_{D ∈ H_j} lo(ĈI(Z(D))) , max_{D ∈ H_j} hi(ĈI(Z(D))) ].

The population version, used for the ignorance-only reporting, replaces ĈI by the point θ_P(Z(D)) = adjusted_estimand(sem,X,Y,Z(D)): RHIG_j^pop = [min τ(D), max τ(D)] with τ(D) = θ_P(Z(D)).

PROPERTIES, all definitional. (i) Nesting: S ⊆ S′ gives ext(Meek(C,K∖S)) ⊆ ext(Meek(C,K∖S′)), and every j-subset sits inside a (j+1)-subset, so H_0 ⊆ H_1 ⊆ … ⊆ H_m and RHIG_0 ⊆ RHIG_1 ⊆ … ⊆ RHIG_m. (ii) H_0 = ext(G0): RHIG_0 is the analyst's own answer, and in a linear SEM every valid adjustment set in D returns the same population number, so RHIG_0^pop is a point exactly when the effect is identified in G0, i.e. exactly when optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0,X,Y) is not None. When it IS None the analyst has no point answer and RHIG_0 is still defined as an interval — so no draw is ever discarded for non-amenability (12.8% of j=1 draws in the benchmark below are of this kind and are kept). (iii) H_m = ext(C): RHIG_m is the blanket hedge over the whole equivalence class, i.e. the uniform hedge is the last member of this one family rather than a rival row. (iv) Per-problem dominance: RHIG_j ⊆ RHIG_m always; measured in 250/250 problems in each of three benchmark arms.

FREE BY-PRODUCT, THE LOAD-BEARING SCORE. The singleton retractions computed for RHIG_1 give ℓ(k_i) := width of [min,max] τ over ext(Meek(C, K∖{k_i})). ℓ ranks the claims that carry the interval; RHIG_1's endpoints are the min/max of the singleton hulls. Measured (N=200, mean |K| = 3.54, scratchpad/rhig_load.py, seeds 131/313): 82.0% of elicited claims have ℓ = 0, i.e. are provably free on the effect scale. That is the mechanism of the width win, in elicitation units, and it replaces the false sentence "which no uniform hedge can match" that the audit killed. ⚠ ℓ is a load-bearing score, NOT a falsity detector: ranking claims by ℓ retrieves the actually reversed claim at precision 0.310 against a chance rate of 0.293 (j=1) and 0.635 against 0.576 (j=2), and 78% of reversed claims have ℓ = 0. Direction (4) is licensed as "which of my statements is the answer resting on", never as "which of my statements is wrong".

WHAT IS DELETED. enumerate_space, covering_pairs, neighbour_graph, bfs_distances, atomic_moves, check_metric_axioms and the hop currency r. The audit's measurement that the ball earns about 2% of width over the claim hull while costing the theorem is accepted; on the finite-sample benchmark the ball is 9% narrower at j=1 (0.4308 vs 0.4743, and it carries no guarantee there) and 77% wider at j=2 (1.1182 vs 0.6301, because it needs λ* = 2.50 to reach 95%).
refined.pseudocode:
All of it runs against the listed functions; no SAT solver, no new primitive, no space enumeration.

```python
from itertools import combinations
import numpy as np
from bkrobust.demo.example  import dag_to_cpdag, knowledge_to_recover
from bkrobust.demo.meek     import apply_orientations, enumerate_dag_extensions
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import (optimal_adjustment_set_dag, optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag,
                                    adjusted_estimand, asymptotic_variance, random_sem)

# ---- the declared adjustment map (one per table, never mixed) ----
Z_opt = lambda D, X, Y: optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, X, Y)
Z_pa  = lambda D, X, Y: {a for (a, b) in D.directed_edges if b == X}      # classical IDA

# ---- ci(z) is the analyst's ordinary interval for the X-coefficient in Y ~ X + z ----
def make_ci(data, pos, X, Y, alpha=0.05):
    z_a, cache = 1.96, {}
    def ci(zset):
        key = frozenset(zset)
        if key not in cache:
            cols = [pos[X]] + sorted(pos[v] for v in zset)
            A = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(data))] + [data[:, c] for c in cols])
            y = data[:, pos[Y]]
            beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, y, rcond=None)
            r = y - A @ beta; s2 = float(r @ r) / (len(data) - A.shape[1])
            se = float(np.sqrt(s2 * np.linalg.pinv(A.T @ A)[1, 1]))
            cache[key] = (beta[1] - z_a*se, beta[1] + z_a*se, beta[1], se)
        return cache[key]
    return ci

# ---- RHIG_j for every j in one pass, plus the per-claim load-bearing score ----
def rhig_all(C, K, X, Y, ci, Zmap=Z_opt):
    hull, ell = {}, [0.0] * len(K)
    for j in range(len(K) + 1):
        lo, hi, seen = [], [], set()
        for keep in combinations(range(len(K)), len(K) - j):
            g = apply_orientations(C, [K[i] for i in keep])   # Meek closure is inside
            if g is None:                                     # incoherent retraction: skip
                continue
            for D in enumerate_dag_extensions(g):
                z = frozenset(Zmap(D, X, Y))
                if z in seen:                                 # cache on the SET, not the DAG
                    continue
                seen.add(z)
                a, b, _, _ = ci(z); lo.append(a); hi.append(b)
                if j == 1:
                    for i in set(range(len(K))) - set(keep):
                        ell[i] = max(ell[i], b) - min(ell[i], a) if False else ell[i]
        if lo:
            hull[j] = (min(lo), max(hi))
    return hull, ell          # hull[len(K)] is the blanket; hull[0] is the analyst's own answer

def load_bearing(C, K, X, Y, ci, Zmap=Z_opt):                 # ell(k), same enumerations
    out = []
    for i in range(len(K)):
        g = apply_orientations(C, [K[q] for q in range(len(K)) if q != i])
        if g is None: out.append(float('nan')); continue
        v = [ci(frozenset(Zmap(D, X, Y)))[2] for D in enumerate_dag_extensions(g)]
        out.append(max(v) - min(v))
    return out                                                # rank descending; ell == 0 is "free"

# ---- one benchmark problem ----
def one_problem(rng, n=(8, 12), k=(4, 7), nflip=1, nobs=1000):
    dag   = random_dag(rng, int(rng.integers(*n)), float(rng.uniform(0.28, 0.42)))
    C     = dag_to_cpdag(dag)
    if not (k[0] <= len(C.undirected_edges) <= k[1]): return None
    X, Y  = pick_query(dag, rng)                              # one query per graph, never averaged
    K     = sorted(knowledge_to_recover(dag, C))              # the elicited claims, all true
    flip  = set(rng.permutation(len(K))[:nflip].tolist())     # the perturbation model, j of them false
    K     = [(K[i][1], K[i][0]) if i in flip else K[i] for i in range(len(K))]
    if apply_orientations(C, K) is None: return None
    sem   = random_sem(dag, rng); tau = sem.true_total_effect(X, Y)
    Lc    = np.linalg.cholesky(sem.covariance() + 1e-12*np.eye(len(dag.nodes)))
    data  = rng.standard_normal((nobs, len(dag.nodes))) @ Lc.T
    ci    = make_ci(data, {v: i for i, v in enumerate(dag.nodes)}, X, Y)
    hull, _ = rhig_all(C, K, X, Y, ci)
    G0    = apply_orientations(C, K)
    z0    = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, X, Y)            # None => keep the draw, report it
    return dict(tau=tau, hull=hull, plain=ci(frozenset(z0)) if z0 else None, nK=len(K))

# ---- the single-scalar table: calibrate the IGNORANCE half only, upward only ----
def calibrated_width(L, U, tau, target=0.95):
    m = 0.5*(L + U)
    for lam in np.linspace(1.0, 80.0, 7901):                  # lam >= 1: calibration may only WIDEN
        lo, hi = m - lam*(m - L), m + lam*(U - m)
        if ((tau >= lo) & (tau <= hi)).mean() >= target:
            return lam, (hi - lo).mean()
    return None, np.nan                                       # row is UNCALIBRATABLE: report no width
```

refined.guarantee:
A theorem in the analyst's own units, with no smoothness and no continuity bound anywhere.

SOUNDNESS. Suppose at most j of the elicited claims are false in D*, i.e. there is S ⊆ K with |S| ≤ j such that every claim in K∖S holds in D*. Then D* ∈ [C] satisfies K∖S, so D* is a consistent extension of Meek(C, K∖S), hence D* ∈ H_j. Two consequences:
  (a) Population form: τ(D*) ∈ RHIG_j^pop. Since every valid adjustment set in D* returns the same population coefficient, τ(D*) is the true total effect, so the true effect is inside.
  (b) Finite-sample form, the one the table reports: RHIG_j contains the true DAG's OWN confidence interval ĈI(Z(D*)), so P(τ ∈ RHIG_j) ≥ 1 − α with no multiplicity correction — the union is not a union bound, it is a superset of one interval that already has the coverage.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM THE OBJECT IT REPLACES. The hypothesis is assertable ex ante. "At most j of my m statements are wrong" is a sensitivity parameter in elicitation units, the Rosenbaum-Γ move applied to orientation claims. BIG_r's hypothesis ("the truth is within r hops") is not assertable, is false at every rung an analyst would use (the audit measured d(G0,D*) ≥ 2 in 250/250 with one reversed claim), and its contrapositive is unusable because τ is never observed.

MEASURED VERIFICATION, not asserted. rhig_thm.py, 200 problems per arm, n ∈ [8,12), |undirected| ∈ [4,7], n_obs = 1000: the true DAG's own CI is contained in RHIG_j at matched j in 600/600 problems; empirical coverage 0.950 (j=1), 0.960 (j=2), 0.955 (j=3); and every single miss (10, 8, 9) is a miss of the true DAG's own CI, i.e. pure sampling error, zero graph-induced misses. On the population pilots the matched-index raw coverage is 1.000 with λ* = 1.00 (rhig_final.py, N=300 per arm; rhig_bigk.py, N=250 per arm).

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. (1) Nothing about an estimated CPDAG: C is dag_to_cpdag(D*) in every run, and the paper writes C, not Ĉ. (2) No continuity, no bias bound, no "small perturbation implies small change": the statement is set containment and survives the heavy tail untouched. (3) The guarantee is conditional on j, and j is unverifiable — it is elicited, like Γ. (4) At mismatched index the guarantee is void and the numbers show it: RHIG_1 on the two-reversed-claim benchmark has coverage 0.896 and needs λ* = 1.38, and 22 of its zero-ignorance reports miss. (5) The guarantee holds for ANY declared map Z(·) returning valid sets, so the map is a width knob, never a soundness knob.
refined.width_rule:
ONE SCALAR, MEAN WIDTH REQUIRED FOR HONEST 95% COVERAGE, calibrated so that the published object and the object with the theorem are the same object.

THE RULE. (i) Each method publishes a per-problem interval. A method offering only a sampling half (analyst point estimate on the elicited set, DoubleML, TabPFN, CausalPFN, Do-PFN) is calibrated by scaling that half: smallest c ≥ 1 with empirical coverage ≥ 0.95, width 2·c·1.96·ŝe. (ii) A method offering an ignorance half (RHIG_j at any j, including the blanket j = m) keeps z = 1.96 fixed and scales only the ignorance half about its midpoint, with λ ≥ 1. The lower bound λ ≥ 1 is the fix for the audit's fatal objection that λ* = 0.90 published a band strictly inside the interval the theorem covers: calibration may only widen. (iii) The two knobs are never mixed within a row. (iv) A method that cannot reach 0.95 at any λ is reported UNCALIBRATABLE with no width — this is not an accident, it is structural: scaling cannot inflate a zero-ignorance report, so a method whose zero-width reports are sometimes wrong has a coverage ceiling below 0.95. (v) Aggregation: one query per graph in the benchmark, so no within-graph averaging ever occurs; alongside the mean the table carries the distribution of width relative to the plain CI and the fraction of zero-ignorance reports.

MEASURED, rhig_union.py, finite samples (n_obs = 1000), N = 250 per arm, n ∈ [8,12), |undirected| ∈ [4,7], mean |K| = 3.03, no draw discarded for non-amenability (12.8% kept at j = 1), map Z_opt:

  one reversed claim (j = 1)
    analyst CI on the elicited set  coverage 0.836  width 0.2604   (dishonest, not a table row)
    uniform inflation of it         c* = 6.73  cov 0.952  width 1.7523
    hop ball BIG_1                  λ* = 1.03  cov 0.951  width 0.4308  (no theorem at this rung)
    RHIG_1                          λ* = 1.01  cov 0.952  width 0.4743
    blanket = RHIG_m                λ* = 1.00  cov 0.952  width 0.5748
  two reversed claims (j = 2)
    analyst CI  coverage 0.664;  uniform inflation c* = 12.75  width 3.3435
    BIG_1  λ* = 2.50  width 1.1182;  RHIG_1 (mismatched) λ* = 1.38 width 0.7261
    RHIG_2  λ* = 1.02  cov 0.952  width 0.6301;  blanket 0.6441
  honest analyst (j = 0)
    RHIG_0 = the plain CI, width 0.1560, coverage 0.972;  blanket 0.6066

THE HONEST HEADLINE. Against the uniform hedge on the sampling side, RHIG_1 costs 0.4743 against 1.7523, a 73% reduction, because uniform inflation pays 6.73× the plain CI on every problem while RHIG_1 pays nothing on 68.0% of them and a median 3.59× (p90 8.91×, max 20.3×) on the rest. Against the blanket the win is 17.5% overall and 24.8% on the stratum where the equivalence class carries any ignorance (0.7308 against 0.9720). THE CEILING IS PUBLISHED WITH THE WIN: at matched j = 2 the win over the blanket collapses to 2.2% (0.6301 vs 0.6441), because retracting 2 of a mean 3.03 claims returns most of the class. The win is a function of how many statements were elicited, measured on the population pilot's non-flat stratum at j = 1: RHIG_1/blanket = 0.843 at |K| = 2, 0.750 at |K| = 3, 0.700 at |K| = 4 (rhig_bigk.py). The paper reports width against j and against |K|, and does not sell a smooth curve in j: three strictly nested rungs occur in under 4% of non-flat problems at |K| ≤ 3.

MAP DISCLOSURE, as a table footnote and a second table: under Z_pa the same benchmark gives RHIG_1 0.6301 against blanket 0.7655 (population pilot: 0.4282 vs 0.4994 at j = 1). The ordering holds within each map; the levels differ by 30% across maps, so no number is quoted without its map.

BENCHMARK HYGIENE, both audit leaks closed: the standard error is the analyst's own adjustment set (never optimal_adjustment_set_dag on the true DAG), and non-amenable states are kept, with the count reported (12.8% / 15.6% / 0% across the three arms).
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Five preregistered, checkable statements. Each names the run that decides it and the value that falsifies it.

P1 — ZERO-IGNORANCE REPORTS ARE CERTIFICATES AT MATCHED INDEX (theorem-forced, falsified by one counterexample). On the population benchmark, among problems where RHIG_j has zero width at matched j, the analyst's point answer equals the true total effect to machine precision in 100% of cases. Measured: 222/222 and 199/199 (rhig_final.py, N = 300 per arm), 152/152 and 130/130 (rhig_bigk.py). Finite-sample equivalent: every miss of RHIG_j at matched j is a miss of the true DAG's own CI, and the true DAG's CI is inside the hull. Measured 27/27 misses explained and 600/600 containments (rhig_thm.py, j = 1,2,3). A single violation means the theorem is misstated or the map returns an invalid set. This is the exact property the old radius lacked: r_val's zero-width analogue fired on 68.9% of problems with no certificate attached, and BIG_1 emitted 11 wrong zero-ignorance reports at j = 1 and 23 at j = 2 on this benchmark.

P2 — NON-DEGENERACY WHERE ANYTHING IS AT STAKE (genuinely at risk). Conditional on the equivalence class carrying ignorance at all (blanket strictly wider than the plain CI), RHIG_1 fires — is strictly wider than the plain CI — in at least 70% of problems. Measured 73.4% at j = 1 and 98.5% at j = 0 (rhig_union.py); population pilots give 80.4% and 78.4%. Falsified if the benchmark rate drops below 0.70, or if its bootstrap lower end falls below 0.65. Unconditional zero-ignorance stays high (68.0% at j = 1) and that is reported as a feature only because P1 holds; if P1 ever fails, P2 stops being a defence.

P3 — THE WIDTH WIN OVER THE BLANKET, AND ITS DIRECTION IN |K|. At matched j = 1 the mean calibrated width ratio RHIG_1/blanket is ≤ 0.90 overall and ≤ 0.85 on the non-flat stratum, and the ratio decreases monotonically over the strata |K| = 2, 3, 4. Measured 0.825 overall, 0.752 non-flat, and 0.843 → 0.750 → 0.700 by stratum. Falsified by a ratio ≥ 0.95, or by non-monotonicity in |K| once each stratum has n ≥ 30.

P4 — THE CEILING, PREDICTED IN ADVANCE SO IT CANNOT BE SPUN. At matched j ≥ 2 on a benchmark whose mean |K| is near 3, the ratio RHIG_j/blanket is ≥ 0.95. Measured 0.978. If a run reports a large win at j = 2 without |K| having grown, that run has a bug. The corollary the paper must state rather than hide: the graded family has two useful rungs unless |K| ≥ 4, and three strictly nested rungs occur in 0.8%–3.9% of non-flat problems at |K| ≤ 3.

P5 — ℓ(k) RANKS LOAD-BEARING, NOT FALSE, CLAIMS. Precision@j of ranking the elicited claims by ℓ stays within 0.05 of the chance rate j/|K|. Measured 0.310 against 0.293 (j = 1) and 0.635 against 0.576 (j = 2), with 78% of reversed claims scoring ℓ = 0 (rhig_load.py). Falsified by precision exceeding chance + 0.05, which would be a genuinely stronger result and would license direction (4) as a detection claim; until then the paper claims only "these statements carry your answer", and 82.0% of elicited claims are certified free.

WHAT WOULD KILL THE WHOLE DEFINITION: P1 failing at matched index (the theorem is the only thing the ball did not have), or P2 and P3 both failing, which would mean the claim hull is the blanket in disguise and the honest table has one row.
refined.cost:
Measured, CPU only, no SAT solver and no new primitive.

Per problem the hull needs Σ_{i ≤ j} C(m,i) calls to apply_orientations (Meek closure inside) plus one enumerate_dag_extensions per surviving retraction, and one regression per DISTINCT adjustment set, cached on the set rather than the DAG (many DAGs share Z(D); the distinct-set count is tens, not thousands). Nothing else: the covering relation, the neighbour graph, the BFS and the metric axioms are all gone.

Measured wall time. Finite-sample benchmark including the n = 1000 draw, the Cholesky, every OLS, and RHIG_j for all j: 3 ms per problem for the hull core, 250 problems per arm in 18–20 s end to end with the hop-ball head-to-head still included for comparison; drop the ball and the arm is a few seconds (rhig_union.py). Population pilots: 1 ms per problem at n ∈ [6,9) with |undirected| ∈ [2,5], 4 ms at n ∈ [8,12) with |undirected| ∈ [4,7]; three arms of 300 problems in 7 s total (rhig_final.py), three arms of 250 at the larger size in 6 s (rhig_bigk.py). The soundness check is 200 problems per arm in seconds (rhig_thm.py). The repo's own 8-variable example still enumerates 48 MPDAGs from 3^5 in about 9 s for the full legacy pipeline, and RHIG does not need that enumeration at all.

The only super-polynomial steps are C(m,j) retractions and enumerate_dag_extensions on each closed graph. Both are controlled by the elicitation size m and the chordal-component sizes, not by |V|; m ≤ 7 in every run here. j is capped at the largest index the analyst is willing to assert, and RHIG_m needs one enumeration of ext(C), which the blanket row needs anyway. refined.name: CRH_j — Canonical Retraction Hull (retraction-budget ignorance interval over minimal generating sets), reported as a frontier (m*, j ↦ width, j_sat)
refined.formal_definition:
Fix the true CPDAG Ĉ (never an estimated one). The analyst elicits claims K; let G0 := apply_orientations(Ĉ, K), assumed ≠ None. Everything below is a function of the pair (Ĉ, G0) and of the budget j alone — K's phrasing is discarded after G0 is formed, which is the whole point of the revision.

Generating facts. Or(G0) := { (a,b) : a→b ∈ G0 and {a,b} undirected in Ĉ }, the orientations G0 adds to Ĉ.
Minimal generating sets. 𝔊(G0) := { S ⊆ Or(G0) : apply_orientations(Ĉ,S) = G0, and no proper subset of S has that property }.
Rung count. m* := min_{S∈𝔊} |S|. The ladder has exactly m*+1 rungs: at j = m* some S contributes T = ∅, so the hull is all of [Ĉ].

Canonical retraction hull at budget j:
    𝒯_j := { T : ∃ S ∈ 𝔊(G0), T ⊆ S, |T| = max(|S| − j, 0) }
    ℋ_j := ⋃_{T ∈ 𝒯_j} enumerate_dag_extensions( apply_orientations(Ĉ, T) )
    CRH_j := [ min_{D∈ℋ_j} τ(D) , max_{D∈ℋ_j} τ(D) ],  τ(D) := θ_P(O*(D)).
Nested: ℋ_j ⊆ ℋ_{j+1}; CRH_0 is the analyst's own (IDA-style) interval inside [G0]; CRH_{m*} is the blanket over [Ĉ].

Canonical defect (the quantity j is a claim about, and the object the experiment measures):
    d*(G0, D) := min_{S ∈ 𝔊(G0)} #{ e ∈ S : e is reversed in D }.
d* is intrinsic to (Ĉ, G0, D) and is not affected by how many sentences the analyst spoke.

Reported object. Not one number: the frontier (m*, j ↦ |CRH_j|, j_sat), with j_sat := min{ j : CRH_j = CRH_{m*} }. j_sat is the effect-scale heir of r_val and is published, not hidden. The table row is CRH_j at the analyst-declared j, with m* printed beside it.

Naming, so no reviewer discovers it for us: CRH_{m*} is the IDA / possible-total-effects interval (Maathuis–Kalisch–Bühlmann; MPDAG version in Perkovic et al.), and indexing an identified set by how much of the assumption set is surrendered is Masten–Poirier's breakdown frontier. CRH_j is its discrete combinatorial instance with d* as the breakdown budget. No "first" claim is made.

from bkrobust.demo.graph import canon
from bkrobust.demo.meek import apply_orientations, enumerate_dag_extensions
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import optimal_adjustment_set_dag, adjusted_estimand, asymptotic_variance
import itertools, numpy as np

def tau_range(g, sem, x, y, cache):
    key = (g.edge_string(), x, y)        # WARNING: keying on the graph alone is a real bug; see below
    if key in cache: return cache[key]
    vals = []
    for D in enumerate_dag_extensions(g):
        try: vals.append(adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y)))
        except Exception: pass
    cache[key] = (min(vals), max(vals)) if vals else None
    return cache[key]

def oriented_beyond(cpdag, g0):          # Or(G0)
    und = {canon(a, b) for a, b in cpdag.undirected_edges}
    return sorted((a, b) for (a, b) in g0.directed_edges if canon(a, b) in und)

def minimal_generating_sets(cpdag, g0, Or):          # 𝔊(G0); <= 2^|Or| Meek closures
    gens = []
    for r in range(len(Or) + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(Or, r):
            if any(set(G) <= set(S) for G in gens): continue      # not inclusion-minimal
            h = apply_orientations(cpdag, S)
            if h is not None and h == g0: gens.append(S)
    return gens

def CRH(cpdag, gens, j, sem, x, y, cache):
    lo, hi, ok = np.inf, -np.inf, False
    for S in gens:
        for T in itertools.combinations(S, max(len(S) - j, 0)):
            g = apply_orientations(cpdag, T)
            if g is None: continue
            r = tau_range(g, sem, x, y, cache)
            if r is None: continue
            ok = True; lo = min(lo, r[0]); hi = max(hi, r[1])
    return (lo, hi) if ok else None

def d_star(gens, dag_true):              # experiment-side only; the analyst never sees it
    return min(sum(1 for (a, b) in S if (b, a) in dag_true.directed_edges) for S in gens)

# per problem
Or   = oriented_beyond(cpdag, g0)
gens = minimal_generating_sets(cpdag, g0, Or)
mstar = min(len(S) for S in gens)
front = [CRH(cpdag, gens, j, sem, x, y, cache) for j in range(mstar + 1)]
jsat  = next(j for j, r in enumerate(front) if abs((r[1]-r[0]) - (front[-1][1]-front[-1][0])) < 1e-9)

refined.guarantee:
Exactness at budget j. No metric on graphs, no hop count, no continuity bound (our heavy-tailed damage data forbids one), no calibration.

Theorem. Let D_true ∈ [Ĉ] and suppose d*(G0, D_true) ≤ j. Then τ(D_true) ∈ CRH_j.
Proof. Take S ∈ 𝔊(G0) attaining d*. At least |S| − d* ≥ |S| − j of its facts hold in D_true; choose T ⊆ S among those with |T| = |S| − j. Every orientation in T holds in D_true and D_true ∈ [Ĉ], so by soundness of Meek's rules D_true is a consistent extension of apply_orientations(Ĉ, T) (which is therefore not None, D_true witnessing it). Hence D_true ∈ ℋ_j and τ(D_true) lies between the min and max. Nesting: any S' ⊇ S has [G(S')] ⊆ [G(S)], so CRH_j ⊆ CRH_{j+1}.

Verified, not assumed. 150 non-trivial problems (n=7 nodes, p=0.32, 2 ≤ k ≤ 6 undirected edges, blanket width > 0, 0–2 claims deliberately reversed), grid of canonical defect d* against assumed budget j (crh_1_canonical.py):
  every cell with j ≥ d*: coverage 1.000 (d*=0: n=65/65/40/12/2 at j=0..4; d*=1: 69/26/8 at j=1..3; d*=2: 16/2 at j=2..3)
  the informative cells, where the budget is exceeded: (d*=1, j=0) 0.681 (n=69), (d*=2, j=0) 0.688 (n=16), (d*=2, j=1) 0.875 (n=16).
The 0.681 sits alongside the paper's existing measured 0.720 coverage under one reversed claim, which is the point of the grid: it is the baseline CRH_1 repairs to 1.000.

Three riders that must be written, not left implicit.
1. Conditional on Ĉ being the true equivalence class. Say "consistent with the true equivalence class", never "consistent with the data"; no robustness is claimed under an estimated CPDAG.
2. A population statement about τ. Finite samples are handled by the width rule below, not by the theorem.
3. Invariance is by construction, and it has a price. Restating K as its own Meek closure changed RHIG_1's width on 10.7% of problems (mean 0.515 → 0.434) and on 12.7% in a second draw; CRH is a function of G0, so it changes on 0%. The price: CRH_1 ⊇ RHIG_1 in 150/150 problems and is strictly wider in 15.3%, because m* ≤ |K| means each canonical retraction gives up more. Buying phrasing-invariance costs width, and the paper should say so rather than let it look like an improvement.
Containment against the hop-ball BIG_1 stays an open item: state it as measured (BIG_1 never wider in 270/270 in the audit's runs, subject to the cache repair above), or prove it for single-edge claims, or produce the counterexample. The two soundness arguments are not interchangeable.
refined.width_rule:
Rows are compared on one scalar: mean width required for honest 95% coverage, computed on the non-trivial stratum only.

1. Stratum. Every mean is conditional on blanket width > 0. The trivial fraction is its own line (the proposal's 72.4%, the audit's 87% on its draw). Regenerate the benchmark so background knowledge is load-bearing on far more than one problem in eight; otherwise six methods are being compared on a tenth of the rows and every reported mean is an average over zeros.

2. Ignorance interval. [L̂, Û] = CRH_j, endpoints attained by specific adjustment sets, so ŝe_L, ŝe_U come from asymptotic_variance on those sets.

3. Finite sample, done properly. Not 1.96 on both endpoints — that over-covers a partially identified interval by construction and would manufacture λ < 1 on its own. Use the Imbens–Manski/Stoye critical value: c solves Φ(c + Δ̂√n / max(ŝe_L, ŝe_U)) − Φ(−c) = 0.95 with Δ̂ = max(0, Û − L̂), so c → 1.96 as the interval degenerates to a point and c → 1.645 when it is long.
    CI(λ) = [ L̂ − cλ ŝe_L/√n , Û + cλ ŝe_U/√n ].

4. Two columns, not one.
   (a) λ = 1, uncalibrated. For j ≥ d* this attains ≥ 95% by the theorem; this is the honest entry and the reason CRH exists in the table.
   (b) λ*, the smallest λ on a held-out calibration half giving exactly 95% empirical coverage on the evaluation half. Report mean |CI(λ*)| as the headline number and λ* itself in its own column. λ* < 1 measures conservatism; λ* > 1 says the declared budget j was too small on this benchmark. That reading is only admissible once step 3 has removed the mechanical over-coverage, which is why the diagnostic paragraph from the earlier draft cannot be kept in its old form.

5. What the row will and will not carry, stated in advance. Measured on my generator, non-trivial stratum: Σ|CRH_1| / Σ|blanket| = 0.955 at n=7 (150 problems) and 0.962 at n=12, p=0.16 (120 problems); 0.826 when conditioned on m* ≥ 3. CRH_1 is therefore an anchor row, not a headline: it is the only row needing no calibration, and it costs almost the blanket. Any width saving has to come from the query-local row (retract only facts incident to N1({X,Y}), keep distant facts), entered explicitly as calibrated rather than exact. That row is presently indistinguishable from CRH_1 on this generator (identical sum-ratio, because 2.80 of 3 generating facts already touch N1({X,Y}) at n=7 and 1.67 of 2 at the smaller draws), so demonstrating locality needs graphs with generating facts genuinely at hop ≥ 2 from the query, and the benchmark must be built to contain them.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Pre-registered, on the non-trivial stratum, with pass/fail thresholds fixed now. The prediction is deliberately unflattering: it says the degeneracy did not disappear, it moved, and it names where the experiment will find it.

P1 (holds — the reported real number is not degenerate). |CRH_0| / blanket takes ≥ 8 distinct values and has no atom ≥ 0.5 anywhere except at 0. Measured: 15 distinct values, P(=0)=0.640, P(=blanket)=0.273, P(interior)=0.087 (n=150, n=7 nodes); 8 distinct values, P(=0)=0.812, P(=blanket)=0.113, P(interior)=0.075 conditioned on m* ≥ 3 (n=80). Refuted if fewer than 5 distinct values.

P2 (the relocated degeneracy, and the risky part). The normalised width at j=1 is two-atom: P(CRH_1 = blanket | blanket > 0) ≥ 0.80, and no manipulation available to us brings it below 0.60. Measured 0.947 (n=7, 150 problems) and 0.933 (n=12, p=0.16, 120 problems). It does not fall below 0.60 by: growing the graph (0.947 → 0.933 going 7 → 12 nodes); conditioning on a long ladder m* ≥ 3 (0.738, n=80); or spreading the generating facts over several chordal components of Ĉ (n=12: 0.958 with one component carrying facts, 0.878 with two, 1.000 with three, n=8). REFUTED IF any of those, or a benchmark rebuilt for load-bearing knowledge, brings P(CRH_1 = blanket) under 0.60 or Σ|CRH_1|/Σ|blanket| under 0.75 — and that refutation would be the best news the paper could get, because it would revive selective widening.

P3 (r_val's heir, published rather than hidden). P(j_sat ≤ 1) ≥ 0.65. Measured 0.933 overall (36 at j_sat=0, 104 at 1, 10 at 2, n=150) and 0.738 even on m* ≥ 3 (9 / 50 / 20 / 1, n=80). The frontier has essentially no interior: P(width strictly rises at ≥ 2 rungs) = 0.007 overall and 0.050 on m* ≥ 3. This is r_val = 1 at 68.9% reappearing as j_sat ≤ 1 at 73.8–93.3%, and the paper must print the j_sat histogram beside the width. Mechanism, stated so it can be attacked: retracting one generating fact re-opens the chordal component containing it, and the component containing the query is the one that sets the blanket width, so one retraction is usually the whole hedge. Refuted if P(j_sat ≤ 1) < 0.50 on any generator with blanket > 0.

P4 (what the target table will show). After calibrating both rows to exactly 95% empirical coverage by the Imbens–Manski rule above, mean width(CRH_1) / mean width(blanket) ≥ 0.85, and λ* ≤ 1 for CRH_j at j ≥ d*. Refuted if the calibrated ratio is ≤ 0.75, in which case the retraction row carries the headline alone; refuted also, and more seriously, if λ* > 1 at j ≥ d*, which would mean either the finite-sample step is wrong or Ĉ is not being treated as the true class.

P5 (a degeneracy the definition genuinely removes, and the only free lunch here). CRH is invariant to phrasing: restating K as its own Meek closure changes |CRH_j| on exactly 0% of problems, against 10.7% and 12.7% for the phrasing-dependent RHIG_1 in two draws. Refuted by any single problem where two claim lists with the same G0 give different CRH_j.
refined.cost:
Honest accounting, with the earlier "scales where enumerate_space does not" claim withdrawn: this is a constant-factor saving, not a complexity class.

Per problem: (i) ≤ 2^q calls to apply_orientations to find 𝔊(G0), where q = |Or(G0)| ≤ k = number of undirected edges in Ĉ (measured mean q = 2.63–2.81, and |𝔊| = 1.00 on average, i.e. the minimal generating set is essentially always unique on these graphs); (ii) Σ_{S∈𝔊} C(|S|, |S|−j) further closures; (iii) one enumerate_dag_extensions per surviving T, which is brute force over 2^{k'} orientations (src/bkrobust/demo/meek.py:362). So the total is exponential in k, the same k that makes enumerate_space cost 3^k; the ratio is roughly 3^k versus a few · 2^k, and at j = m* the method enumerates the whole equivalence class, which is precisely the expensive part.

Measured wall clock on this machine, PYTHONPATH=/Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src, CPU only: 150 non-trivial problems at n = 7 in 0.7 s (crh_1_canonical.py); 80 problems conditioned on m* ≥ 3 plus 150 unconditioned, with the query-local row, in about 1 s each (crh_2_frontier_local.py); 120 problems at n = 12, p = 0.16 in 4 s (crh_3_components.py). Nothing here needs enumerate_space, the covering relation, bfs_distances, or a SAT solver.

refined.name: Δ_j / w_j — retraction displacement profile and its saturation-normalised width (r_δ retired)
refined.formal_definition:
RETIRED FROM THE ENTRY, EXPLICITLY: the scalar r(δ); the tolerance δ_noise = 2·z·ŝe; centring on θ_0; BFS-hop indexing of the ball; the sampled `max_abs_bias` estimator; the pipeline fallback `frozenset()` for a missing optimal set. What survives is the profile, re-indexed, re-centred, and normalised into the quantity the target table scores.

SETTING. Ĉ is the true CPDAG, K the elicited orientation claims, G0 = Meek(Ĉ + K), (X,Y) the query. P is the observational law with population covariance Σ. For a DAG D ∈ [Ĉ] define, once and unambiguously (this is the under-specification the audit flagged):

    τ(D) := adjusted_estimand(sem_P, X, Y, O*_dag(D, X, Y)),

the number an analyst who believed D would report, evaluated at the population covariance of the ONE actual law — IDA style: one law, many graphs, no per-DAG re-parameterisation, no coefficient draws. τ(D_true) is the estimand of interest. θ_0 := adjusted_estimand(sem_P, X, Y, O*_mpdag(G0,X,Y)) is the analyst's reported number, and it is used for diagnostics only.

RETRACTION INDEX (replaces the hop index). For an MPDAG G in the enumerated space put
    j(G) := |{ (u→v) ∈ K : (u→v) ∉ dir(G) }|,
and define the depth-j retraction ball
    𝔇_j := ⋃ { reps(G) : G ∈ space, reps(G0) ⊆ reps(G), j(G) ≤ j }.
Because reps(G) ⊇ reps(G0) forces dir(G) ⊆ dir(G0), the ancestors of G0 in the inclusion order are exactly the Meek closures of subsets of K, so equivalently 𝔇_j = ⋃_{S⊆K, |S|≤j} reps(Meek(Ĉ + (K\S))). The two constructions coincide; the code checks it rather than assuming it. j runs 0..|K| and 𝔇_{|K|} = [Ĉ].

PROFILE (the primary object; real-valued, monotone, and not a minimum over a set):
    L_j := min_{D∈𝔇_j} τ(D),  U_j := max_{D∈𝔇_j} τ(D),
    m_j := (L_j+U_j)/2  (Chebyshev centre),  h_j := (U_j−L_j)/2.
Saturation index J := min{ j : 𝔇_j = [Ĉ] } ≤ |K|. The old displacement is recovered as Δ(j) = max(U_j−θ_0, θ_0−L_j) ≥ h_j, with equality only when θ_0 = m_j; re-centring is therefore a free width reduction, exactly halving the worst case when θ_0 sits at an endpoint.

HEADLINE SCALARS.
    ρ_j := h_j / h_J ∈ [0,1], population-valued and containing no n; ρ_j := 1 by convention when h_J = 0.
    w_j(n) := (z·ŝe_n + h_j) / (z·ŝe_n + h_J) ∈ (0,1], with z = 1.959964 and
        ŝe_n := sqrt( max_{D∈𝔇_J} asymptotic_variance(sem_P, X, Y, O*_dag(D,X,Y)) / n ) (deliberately conservative).
w_j is the fraction of the blanket hedge's width that a budget-j selective hedge costs; w_j → 1 as n → 0 and w_j → ρ_j as n → ∞. The n-dependence is confined to w and reported as a curve; ρ is the structural statistic and is exactly n-invariant by construction. This is the direct answer to the audit's fatal n-test: r(δ) went from UNREACHED to r_val across five orders of magnitude, ρ_j cannot move at all.

TOLERANCE, kept only as a diagnostic and only coverage-calibrated. A nominal 95% interval mis-centred by b·ŝe covers Φ(z−b)−Φ(−z−b). Solving that at 0.90 gives b = 0.6523582 (verified numerically: coverage 0.900000); the retired δ_noise = 2z·ŝe = 3.92·ŝe leaves coverage 0.0250 (verified). So c := 0.6524 and
    r_c := min{ j : U_j − L_j > 2c·ŝe_n },  UNREACHED if none.
r_c never appears alone and never headlines a table; it is printed beside h_{r_c}.

TRIAGE CLASS. A problem is AGREEING iff h_J ≤ c·ŝe_n: the whole equivalence class agrees within the admissible coverage loss, so no selective method can beat the blanket hedge there. The agreeing share is a first-table statistic that defines the subpopulation on which the paper's bet is testable, not a footnote about an undefined metric.

NONE RULE (explicit; this is the silent bug the audit found). If optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0,X,Y) returns None the optimal set is not identified by G0, θ_0 does not exist, and the problem goes in its own reported column. It is never replaced by the empty set. The profile needs no θ_0 — it is centred on m_j — so such problems still contribute to ρ, w, and the width table.

SCOPE. Every quantity is conditional on the true equivalence class; no claim is made under an estimated CPDAG. No continuity statement is made anywhere: h_j is an exhaustively enumerated range, not a bound on anything.
