refined.guarantee:
BUDGET-b SOUNDNESS (exact; the only statement the paper prints).
If at most b of the elicited claims are false in D*, then θ_{D*} ∈ R_b.

Proof. Let S ⊆ K be the false claims, |S| ≤ b. Every claim in K∖S holds in D*, so D* is a consistent extension of cl(K∖S), so θ_{D*} ∈ Θ(cl(K∖S)) ⊆ R_b. ∎

It is structural, not asymptotic: no continuity clause, no bound on damage, no sample size. The heavy tail of damage (median relative bias 0.59, up to 128×) is harmless because R_b CONTAINS the tail's endpoint rather than bounding the distance to it. Nothing here transfers to an estimated CPDAG and the paper must not say it does.

Measured (final_rh_1_ladder.py plus a 900-problem run, seed 20260907, regime-filtered, exactly b_true claims reversed):
  b_true=0  n=900  coverage at b=0,1,2,3 = 1.0000 / 1.0000 / 1.0000 / 1.0000
  b_true=1  n=626  0.6821 / 1.0000 / 1.0000 / 1.0000
  b_true=2  n=438  0.3379 / 0.8562 / 1.0000 / 1.0000
  b_true=3  n=247  0.1943 / 0.6761 / 0.9109 / 1.0000
Coverage is exactly 1.0000 on the whole upper triangle b ≥ b_true and never above it. This closes the audit's kill shot: at budget 2 the old fibre hull covered 0.72–0.76; the pairwise retraction hull covers 1.0000.

Two endpoints, both verified rather than asserted: R_0 = Θ(G_0), and R_m = Θ(Ĉ) exactly on 160/160 problems. The family therefore interpolates between the analyst's point and the blanket hedge, which is what makes it calibratable at all.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. λ carries no guarantee and is not scored as retrieval against "which claim is false" — it gets top-1 0.521 and leaves 53.4% of actually-reversed claims at λ=0 (audit). Direction (4) survives only as a width decomposition with a histogram, not as a ranked-retrieval table.
refined.width_rule:
PROTOCOL FOR THE SINGLE-METRIC TABLE. Every method supplies a nested family of intervals indexed by one monotone knob. Split the problems into a calibration half and an evaluation half. Take the smallest knob value whose empirical coverage on the calibration half is ≥ 0.95, and report the MEAN WIDTH it produces on the evaluation half.

For DoubleML / TabPFN / CausalPFN / Do-PFN the knob is the usual multiplicative scale. FOR US IT IS THE RETRACTION BUDGET b, NOT A SCALE, and that substitution is the point:

  W(ours) = mean_i w(R_{b*}(i)),   b* = min{ b : coverage_cal(R_b) ≥ 0.95 }.

Why the knob must change. Scaling a zero-width interval leaves it zero-width, so any hull-valued method that returns a point and misses can never be calibrated — the audit's structural kill shot. The budget ladder has no such hole: it is nested, non-decreasing, and terminates at R_m = Θ(Ĉ), which covers by construction under the true-CPDAG assumption. b* therefore always exists, and W(ours) ≤ W(blanket) with equality only when b* = m. Measured zero-width-and-wrong at the calibrated budget: 0.4% / 1.2% / 0.0% at q = 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.35.

MEASURED ROW (final_rh_6_qboundary.py, 400 problems per cell, regime-filtered, per-claim elicitation error rate q, seed 20260907):
  q=0.05  b*=0  cov 0.968  width 0.0338  blanket 0.6357  saving 94.7%
  q=0.10  b*=1  cov 0.997  width 0.4932  blanket 0.6321  saving 22.0%
  q=0.15  b*=1  cov 0.994  width 0.4909  blanket 0.6310  saving 22.2%
  q=0.20  b*=1  cov 0.991  width 0.4622  blanket 0.6188  saving 25.3%
  q=0.25  b*=1  cov 0.983  width 0.4568  blanket 0.6147  saving 25.7%
  q=0.30  b*=1  cov 0.978  width 0.4659  blanket 0.6183  saving 24.7%
  q=0.35  b*=1  cov 0.962  width 0.4399  blanket 0.6270  saving 29.8%
  q=0.45  b*=2  cov 0.991  width 0.5910  blanket 0.6364  saving  7.1%
Three seeds × four q (final_rh_5_verify.py, 200 problems/cell) reproduce b*=1 in 11 of 12 cells with savings 17.4–33.1% and coverage 0.966–1.000.

TWO SWEEP HYGIENE RULES THE AUDIT DEMANDED, ADOPTED. (1) |K| is held fixed across methods within a cell, or width is reported against |K|, because at a constant per-claim error rate width falls as claims are added and an unpenalised claim count is a free width knob. (2) Every cell states the regime filter w(Θ(Ĉ)) > 0 and the fraction of draws it keeps.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
STATISTIC. ν(i) := w(R_{b*}(i)) / w(Θ(Ĉ)(i)) ∈ [0,1] per problem, plus the aggregate saving σ := 1 − mean w(R_{b*}) / mean w(Θ(Ĉ)). Degenerate means either σ ≈ 0 (we are the blanket with extra steps) or b* pinned at an endpoint. Unlike r_val, ν cannot saturate at a floor by construction, but it CAN pile up at 1, and it does — so the prediction is about where the mass sits, not about whether it exists.

PREDICTION, on ≥2,000 regime-filtered problems, per-claim error rate q ∈ [0.10, 0.35]:
  P1  b* = 1 strictly interior (mean |K| ≈ 3.4), in ≥ 10 of 12 seed × q cells.
  P2  σ ∈ [0.15, 0.35].
  P3  ν is BIMODAL, not uniform: mass at 0 in [0.20, 0.32], mass at 1 in [0.60, 0.80], interior mass in [0.05, 0.10]. Measured 21.1–31.4% / 61.5–69.5% / 5.9–9.4% across three seeds and four q.
  P4  the ν=1 mass RISES with the free ambiguity f := |undirected(Ĉ)| − |K|: 63.5% at f=0.5 rising to 79.0% at f=3.7 (final_rh_4), while σ stays ≥ 0.15 (measured 0.31, 0.17, 0.22).
  P5  the bet expires in q: σ ≥ 0.20 for q ≤ 0.35 and σ ≤ 0.10 at q ≥ 0.45, because the singleton tier's coverage crosses 0.95 there (0.962 at q=0.35, 0.919 at q=0.45) and b* jumps to 2. Measured σ = 7.1% at q = 0.45.
  P6  LOCALITY OF DAMAGE DOES NOT BECOME LOCALITY OF WIDTH, and this is the prediction most likely to embarrass the paper's bet if stated the other way round. At fixed b=1, ν is LARGER where no claim touches X or Y (0.979, n=200) than where every claim does (0.780, n=200) — because far claims were never buying precision, so R_0 is already 79% of the blanket and there is nothing to save. The hedging tax (w(R_1) − w(R_0)) / (w(Θ(Ĉ)) − w(R_0)) is 0.93 far vs 0.77 near (final_rh_3).

FALSIFIERS, any one of which kills the selective-widening bet and should be written into wiki/activities/active-claims.md before the sweep runs:
  F1  σ < 0.05 at q ≤ 0.20 → R_b is the blanket hedge with extra steps; report it and let the blanket own the row.
  F2  b* = m at q ≤ 0.20 → same conclusion, reached through the ladder instead of the width.
  F3  coverage of R_1 < 0.95 at q = 0.20 → single-claim retraction does not carry the error model; the paper's budget-1 scope is wrong.
  F4  ν=1 mass > 0.85 → the hull equals the blanket on nearly every problem and the mean saving is carried by a minority; that is degeneracy of the same species as r_val = 1, relocated, and must be reported as such.
  F5  σ at f ≈ 6 falls below 0.05 while σ at f ≈ 0 stays above 0.20 → the method only works on graphs whose ambiguity the claims nearly exhaust, which is not the applied setting.
refined.cost:
MEEK CLOSURES. Σ_{j ≤ b*} C(m, j). At the calibrated b* = 1 this is m closures plus the base: measured mean 3.4 (final_rh_5_verify.py). At b* = 2 with m = 3 it is 7. The reversal branch is gone, which halves the audit's stated 2m.

θ EVALUATIONS. With a cache keyed on D.key(), the cost is |⋃_{|S| ≤ b*} [cl(K∖S)]| distinct DAGs. Every such DAG is a consistent extension of Ĉ, so this is bounded by the blanket hedge's own extension count — a containment, not the sum-of-smaller-terms non-sequitur the audit shot down. Measured at b* ≤ 1: mean 0.563 of the blanket's count, max ratio 1.000, exceeds the blanket on 0 of 160 problems. The ranking and the interval together are strictly cheaper than the single baseline they compete against, and now for a reason that is true.

WALL CLOCK, this machine, CPU. A 400-problem cell including generation, all four budget tiers, coverage and widths: about 3 s. The eight-point q sweep (3,200 problems): 25 s. The 900-problem budget-soundness table: about 20 s. The 8-variable demo's Θ(G) is well under a millisecond per graph.

WHAT DOMINATES. enumerate_dag_extensions is the only exponential term, 2^{|undirected|} candidates filtered to consistent extensions; the sweeps here run at |undirected| ≤ 9 (mean blanket extension count 6.6 to 28.4). No SAT solver, no encoding, nothing beyond numpy and the repository.

refined.name: Audit-budget frontier: hitting recall over retraction fibres, reported against the width it buys
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING. Ĉ is the true CPDAG (never an estimated one). K = (k_1,…,k_m) are elicited orientation claims on undirected edges of Ĉ. cl(·) is Meek closure; G_0 = cl(K); Z_0 = O*(G_0). For an MPDAG G with [G] ≠ ∅ let Θ(G) := { τ_D : D ∈ [G] }, τ_D the effect identified by adjusting on O*(D). Θ is finite; write its hull as an interval.

RETRACTION FIBRES. For A ⊆ K put G_{−A} := cl(K \ A) and I_A := hull( Θ(G_0) ∪ Θ(G_{−A}) ). Write I_∅ = hull Θ(G_0) and I_k = I_{{k}}.

COLLAPSE OF THE STATE MAP (this replaces σ ∈ {retract,reverse}^A in the earlier draft). Meek closure is sound and complete, so [cl(K')] = { D ∈ [Ĉ] : D agrees with K' }. Hence [cl(K[σ])] ⊆ [cl(K \ A)] for every σ, and hull(Θ(G_0) ∪ ⋃_σ Θ(G[σ])) = I_A. Reversal is dominated by retraction and is dropped. Consequence: the family is monotone, A ⊆ A′ ⟹ I_A ⊆ I_{A′}, so the repair family is upward closed and the non-submodularity the earlier version conceded is gone.

HAZARD (oracle-free, deployment side). λ(k) := |I_k| − |I_∅| ≥ 0, an excess width in effect units. H := { k : λ(k) > 0 }. Since I_k ⊇ I_∅ are nested intervals, λ(k) = 0 ⟺ I_k = I_∅.

THE TWO AUDIT INTERVALS. For an audit set T ⊆ K,
  U-hedge  I^∪(T) := I_∅ ∪ ⋃_{k∈T} I_k   ("at most one claim in T is wrong")
  J-hedge  I^∩(T) := I_T                  ("any subset of T may be wrong")
Every I_k contains the nonempty I_∅, so the union is an interval and hull = union. I_∅ ⊆ I^∪(T) ⊆ I^∩(T) ⊆ hull Θ(Ĉ). T = ∅ gives the unhedged estimand range; T = K with the J-hedge gives the blanket. The construction is a ladder between them, indexed by (T, b), not a minimum over a ball.

BENCHMARK GROUND TRUTH (needs τ*, synthetic only). M_b := { A ⊆ K : |A| ≤ b, τ* ∈ I_A }; r_rep := min{ |A| : τ* ∈ I_A }, ∞ if none. r_rep = 0 ⟺ no damage. Damage event D := { τ* ∉ I_∅ } = { r_rep ≥ 1 }.

METRICS, ALL CONDITIONAL ON D (this is fix 1: unconditionally, ∅ ∈ M_b on every undamaged instance and the mean is a prevalence number).
 • Audit-budget curve  t ↦ E[ HR@t | D ],  HR@t := 1{ top-t ∩ M_1 ≠ ∅ } = 1{ τ* ∈ I^∪(top-t) }. HR@0 | D = 0 by construction.
 • Ceiling row  R_1 := P(M_1 ≠ ∅ | D) = P(r_rep ≤ 1 | D). No ranking exceeds it; it is a graph property, not a method property, and it is where r_val's degeneracy is quarantined.
 • Ranking efficiency  E@t := E[HR@t | D] / R_1, and MRR of the first repairing claim (misses score 0).
 • J-ladder  HR^∩@t := 1{ τ* ∈ I_{top-t} }, which by upward closure equals 1{ ∃A ⊆ top-t : A ∈ M_{|A|} }. This is how the residue 1 − R_1 is bought, at a width that is reported.
 • Silent-failure row  S := P( D ∧ H = ∅ ) — told nothing is load-bearing while the answer is wrong.
 • False-alarm row  P( ¬D ∧ H ≠ ∅ ) — width paid where nothing was wrong.
 • Base-rate row  P(¬D) = P(∅ ∈ M_b), reported separately and never folded into the headline.
 • WIDTH IS THE SECOND AXIS, replacing PR@T. W@t := mean |I^∪(top-t)| over all instances. The metric is the frontier t ↦ (W@t, HR@t), plotted against |I_∅| and the blanket |hull Θ(Ĉ)|. The old PR@T = Σ_{k∈T}λ / Σ_K λ is deleted: it is monotone in T and equals 1 at T = K, i.e. hazard-mass recall wearing precision's name. If a precision scalar is still wanted it is Σ_{k∈T} λ(k) / max(|T|,1), a per-item denominator, or the marginal width W@t − W@(t−1).

b IS FIXED AT 1 FOR THE DEPLOYMENT OBJECT AND REPORTED AS SUCH; b > 1 appears only as the J-hedge on the same T, so the benchmark and the deployment side are never at different orders (fix 4).
refined.pseudocode:
PYTHONPATH=/Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src. Every call below is a verified function of the repo.

from bkrobust.demo.meek import apply_orientations, enumerate_dag_extensions, is_consistent_extension
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import optimal_adjustment_set_dag, adjusted_estimand, random_sem
from bkrobust.demo.example import dag_to_cpdag, knowledge_to_recover

def theta(g, sem, x, y):                      # Θ(G) as an interval; None if unusable
    if g is None: return None
    exts = enumerate_dag_extensions(g)        # cap |undirected| <= 9, else subsample
    if not exts: return None
    vals = []
    for D in exts:
        z = optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y)
        if z is None: return None
        vals.append(adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, z))
    return (min(vals), max(vals))

def hull(a, b): return (min(a[0], b[0]), max(a[1], b[1]))
def wid(iv):    return iv[1] - iv[0]

# ---------- DEPLOYMENT SIDE: no τ*, no true DAG ----------
def audit(cpdag, K, sem, x, y):
    G0 = apply_orientations(cpdag, K)         # = Meek closure of Ĉ + K
    I0 = theta(G0, sem, x, y)
    I, lam = [], []
    for i in range(len(K)):
        Gi = apply_orientations(cpdag, [k for j, k in enumerate(K) if j != i])
        Ii = hull(I0, theta(Gi, sem, x, y))   # I_k, the retraction fibre
        I.append(Ii); lam.append(wid(Ii) - wid(I0))
    order = sorted(range(len(K)), key=lambda i: -lam[i])
    H     = [i for i in range(len(K)) if lam[i] > TOL]
    return dict(I0=I0, I=I, lam=lam, order=order, H=H)

def U_hedge(a, T):                            # I^∪(T): "at most one of T is wrong"
    iv = a['I0']
    for i in T: iv = hull(iv, a['I'][i])
    return iv

def J_hedge(a, cpdag, K, T, sem, x, y):       # I^∩(T): "any subset of T is wrong"
    if not T: return a['I0']
    g = apply_orientations(cpdag, [k for j, k in enumerate(K) if j not in set(T)])
    t = theta(g, sem, x, y)
    return a['I0'] if t is None else hull(a['I0'], t)

# ---------- BENCHMARK SIDE: τ* known ----------
def label(a, cpdag, K, sem, x, y, tau):
    damaged = not (a['I0'][0] - TOL <= tau <= a['I0'][1] + TOL)
    M1 = [i for i in range(len(K)) if a['I'][i][0] - TOL <= tau <= a['I'][i][1] + TOL]
    r_rep = 0 if not damaged else (1 if M1 else None)
    if r_rep is None:                          # order-2 probe, C(m,2) closures, retraction only
        for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(len(K)), 2):
            iv = J_hedge(a, cpdag, K, [i, j], sem, x, y)
            if iv[0] - TOL <= tau <= iv[1] + TOL: r_rep = 2; break
    return dict(damaged=damaged, M1=M1, r_rep=r_rep)

# instance generator (the repo's own primitives)
#   dag = random DAG (tests/demo/test_evaluate.py::_random_dag), cpdag = dag_to_cpdag(dag)
#   K_min = knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag); K = K_min + a random subset of the remaining
#          true orientations of cpdag.undirected_edges  (redundancy r = |K|/|K_min|)
#   plant 1–2 reversals in K; sem = random_sem(dag, rng); tau = sem.true_total_effect(x, y)
#   sanity: is_consistent_extension(dag, cpdag) must hold; τ* is never used before `label`.

# ---------- AGGREGATION ----------
#   dmg   = [r for r in rows if r.damaged]
#   curve = [ mean(1{set(order[:t]) & set(M1)}) for t in 0..max_m ]  over dmg   # audit-budget
#   R1    = mean(1{M1 != []}) over dmg                                          # ceiling row
#   S     = mean(damaged and H == []) over ALL rows                             # silent failure
#   W[t]  = mean(wid(U_hedge(a, order[:t]))) over ALL rows                      # width axis
#   ranking baselines on the same rows: random permutation, adversarial (repairs last).
# Calibration to the single-metric table: for each method m and instance i,
#   c_i = |τ*_i − centre(I_i)| / halfwidth(I_i)   (0 if τ* = centre; ∞ if halfwidth = 0 and miss)
#   s* = the ⌈0.95 N⌉-th order statistic of c;  reported width = 2 · s* · mean(halfwidth)
#   count(c_i = ∞) is printed: those instances cannot be calibrated by ANY finite scalar.
refined.guarantee:
LEMMA 1 (fibres are nested, unions are intervals). Θ(G_0) ⊆ Θ(G_{−A}), so I_∅ ⊆ I_A, and every I_k contains the nonempty I_∅; hence ⋃_{k∈T} I_k is an interval and equals its hull. Consequence, the identity that licenses the whole direction: HR@T = 1{ τ* ∈ I^∪(T) } exactly, not up to an inequality. E[HR@T | ·] is the structural coverage of the reported interval computed a second way; the retrieval column and the coverage column of the table are the same number. The corresponding statement for the J-ladder is HR^∩@T = 1{ τ* ∈ I_T }, which by upward closure equals "some subset of T repairs".

LEMMA 2 (λ-soundness at b = 1). λ(k) = 0 ⟹ I_k = I_∅ (nested intervals of equal length) ⟹ (τ* ∈ I_k ⟺ τ* ∈ I_∅ ⟺ no damage). Hence on damaged instances M_1 ⊆ H. Verified without exception in every damaged instance I generated in-session: 89/89 (w4_cal, N=300), 50/50 + 56/56 + 54/54 (w4_final, three redundancy arms), and the audit's earlier 51/51 and 119/119.

THEOREM (selective soundness with a deployment-checkable antecedent). If H ⊆ T then I^∪(T) = I^∪(H) ⊇ I_k for every k, so { r_rep ≤ 1 } ∩ { H ⊆ T } ⊆ { τ* ∈ I^∪(T) }. Equivalently P(τ* ∈ I^∪(H)) ≥ P(r_rep ≤ 1). The antecedent H ⊆ T is checkable without τ*; the antecedent r_rep ≤ 1 is not, and it is exactly the ceiling row R_1. Stating the theorem without that conditional is the error the audit caught, so it belongs in the theorem line, not a footnote.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, said plainly. This is not an unconditional coverage guarantee. The residue 1 − R_1 must be bought by climbing the ladder — the J-hedge at b = 2 on the same audit set, whose width is measured and reported — and never absorbed into the calibration scalar, because a scalar is uniform widening, the competitor the paper exists to beat. Measured in-session (w4_join, N=300, independent seed): union top-1 covers 0.960 at 0.599 of the blanket width; joint retraction on top-2 covers 0.977 at 0.780; blanket covers 1.000 at 1.000. The ladder buys the residue at a stated price.

NO CONTINUITY IS CLAIMED ANYWHERE. λ(k) = 0 is an exact identity of intervals, not a smallness statement, and nothing here asserts that small λ implies small bias. The heavy tail of damage-conditional bias is untouched by this metric and is priced only through the width axis.

THE ONE STRUCTURAL FAILURE EVENT IS NAMED AND MEASURED: D ∧ H = ∅, the analyst told that no claim is load-bearing while the estimate is wrong. Measured 6/89 damaged, 2.0 per cent unconditional (w4_cal, N=300). It does not go to zero and it is a row of the table.
refined.width_rule:
THE RULE. Report CI(T) = the interval I^∪(top-t*) (or I^∩ if the ladder was climbed), widened for sampling by the same protocol every competitor gets: scale about the centre by the scalar s* that brings empirical coverage to 95 per cent on held-out synthetic instances, then report mean width. Operating point t*: the smallest cutoff whose structural coverage P(¬D) + P(D)·E[HR@t | D] meets the structural share of the 95 per cent target. If no t reaches it because R_1 caps it, climb to the J-hedge at b = 2 on the same T rather than inflating s*, and report which was used, the structural coverage attained, and the scalar separately. A row whose 95 per cent is bought mostly by s* is a uniform hedge with an audit list stapled to it, and the table must show that.

MEASURED IN-SESSION under exactly this protocol (population estimands, 6–8 node DAGs, |U| ≤ 9, 1–2 planted reversed claims, mixed redundancy; w4_cal.py, N = 300, damage rate 0.297):
  method                 raw cov   mean W    s*      uncoverable   calibrated W   vs blanket
  Θ(G_0), no hedge        0.703    0.0342    ∞        86/300            ∞             —
  hedge on a random claim 0.803    0.1099    ∞        48/300            ∞             —
  union hedge, top-1 λ    0.970    0.2350    1.000     6/300          0.2350        0.615
  union hedge, T = H      0.973    0.2422    1.000     6/300          0.2422        0.634
  blanket over Ĉ          1.000    0.3820    1.000     0/300          0.3820        1.000
Replication, independent seed (w4_join.py, N = 300): union top-1 coverage 0.960 at 0.599 of blanket; T = H 0.970 at 0.622; joint retraction top-2 0.977 at 0.780.

TWO CONSEQUENCES THE PAPER MUST STATE RATHER THAN HIDE.
(i) The unhedged estimand and a random-claim hedge cannot be calibrated to 95 per cent by ANY finite scalar: on 86 and 48 of 300 instances the interval has zero half-width and misses. Honesty here is not purchasable by uniform inflation; it has to be bought in the right direction. That is the strongest argument the direction has, and it is a table row, not a sentence.
(ii) WHERE THE WIN COMES FROM. The median ratio of selective to blanket width is exactly 1.000, with 52.8 per cent exact ties (and 31.8 per cent below 0.5); the audit's finding replicates, and redundancy in K does not repair it — median 1.000 at redundancy 1.0, 1.41 and 1.66, only 0.954 above 2.0 (w4_final.py, 200 instances × 3 arms). Split by hazard: where H = ∅ (58.7 per cent of instances) the selective width is 0.0345 against a blanket 0.1881; where H ≠ ∅ it is 0.5195 against 0.6571, a ratio of 0.79. So "damage is local" cashes out as MOST QUERIES HAVE NO LOAD-BEARING CLAIM AT ALL, and there the interval collapses to the point estimate. It does not cash out as "hedging a load-bearing claim is cheap" — Meek closure cascades, and retracting one claim reopens most of the class. Write the mechanism that way, report the mean because the target metric is a mean, and report the median tie in the same table so no reader discovers it in review.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Registered before the 2,087-problem sweep runs; every number below is from this session's probes on 6–8 node DAGs and is predicted to hold at the sweep's scale.

PREDICTED NON-DEGENERACY.
P1. Ranking resolution, conditional on damage: E[HR@1 | D] ≥ 0.80 for the λ-ranking and ≤ 0.45 for a random permutation, gap ≥ 0.30. Probes: 0.899 vs 0.315 (n = 89, w4_cal/w4_an; a second RNG draw gave 0.292), 0.960 vs 0.460, 0.982 vs 0.339, 1.000 vs 0.352 (three arms, w4_final). Adversarial ranking 0.022. MRR 0.904.
P2. No prevalence dilution: E[HR@0 | D] = 0.000 exactly, and the unconditional curve starts at exactly 1 − P(damage) (0.703 measured). If the paper ever prints the unconditional number as the headline it is reporting a base rate.
P3. The min-over-a-set that killed r_val survives ONLY as the flat right endpoint: E[HR@t | D] is constant for t ≥ 2 at R_1, and R_1 is a graph property no ranking touches. Predicted R_1 ≥ 0.85 with one planted flip (measured 0.910 and 1.000 in separate arms) and R_1 ≤ 0.80 with two (the audit's probe measured 0.714). Ranking efficiency E@1 = HR@1 / R_1 ≥ 0.95 (measured 0.988).
P4. The honest failure row does not vanish: P(D ∧ H = ∅) ∈ (0, 0.05], measured 0.020 (6/300); false alarms P(¬D ∧ H ≠ ∅) ≈ 0.19 of undamaged instances (41/211).
P5. Width, the prediction that decides the paper: calibrated mean W(selective top-1)/W(blanket) ∈ [0.55, 0.75] as long as P(H = ∅) ≥ 0.5 (measured 0.615 and 0.599 on two seeds at P(H = ∅) = 0.587), and it rises toward 1 as P(H = ∅) → 0 — denser graphs, longer K, elicitation concentrated on the query neighbourhood. The MEDIAN ratio stays at 1.000 in every configuration, including every redundancy bucket below 2.0. The ratio is therefore predicted to track P(H = ∅) and not to track the ranking's quality.

KILL CONDITIONS — any one fires and this becomes a negative-results entry (letter C, an instrument that measured nothing) with a revive_if, not a paper section.
K1. E[HR@1 | D] − E[HR@1 | D, random ranking] < 0.15 at the sweep's scale: the ranking carries no information the space did not already have, and the metric is r_val renamed after all.
K2. R_1 < 0.5 with a single planted false claim: the b = 1 object is the wrong order and the deployment side must move to pair hazards before anything is claimed.
K3. Calibrated W(selective)/W(blanket) > 0.90 while P(H = ∅) ≥ 0.5: the ranking is real and cannot be cashed into the column the paper is judged on.
K4. The width ordering reverses once DoubleML, TabPFN, CausalPFN, Do-PFN and the total-effect enumeration are calibrated by the identical order-statistic rule.
K5. P(D ∧ H = ∅) > 0.10: the audit list is silent too often for the soundness theorem's antecedent to be worth checking.

The prediction I would most expect to lose is P5 at the sweep's graph sizes, since P(H = ∅) falls as the undirected component grows and as K is elicited near the query — and the sweep's own measurement (568 of 1,266 perturbations damaging when a claim touches the treatment or outcome) says elicitation near the query is the regime that matters.
refined.cost:
DEPLOYMENT (no τ*, per query): m + 1 Meek closures, each followed by one enumeration of [G] and one O*-plus-adjusted-estimand evaluation per extension. Measured on this machine: mean 0.5 ms, median 0.4 ms, max 1.7 ms per query at n = 6–8 nodes, |U| ≤ 8, |K| ≈ 2–4, over 40 queries (w4_time.py). The audit is free relative to enumerating the class once, which every baseline row in the table also pays.

BENCHMARK, order 2: an extra C(m,2) closures — retraction only, since the 2^|A| state-map factor was proved redundant — so 28 at m = 8, against the 4·C(m,2) the earlier draft budgeted. Order-b in general is Σ_{j≤b} C(m,j), no 2^j factor.

FULL SWEEP: 300 instances with the complete fibre, labelling, calibration and ranking baselines ran in under three minutes of wall clock in each of the three probes; the three-arm redundancy sweep (200 instances × 3 elicitation regimes) ran in the same order. 2,087 problems is minutes, not hours, on CPU.

SCALING DRIVER, and it is not the metric: |[Ĉ]|, exponential in the undirected component. The repo's enumerate_dag_extensions is the bottleneck and it is shared with the blanket baseline, so the comparison stays fair. Cap at |U| ≤ 9 as the probes do, or subsample extensions and report the Monte-Carlo error on Θ's endpoints; the endpoints are order statistics, so the error is reportable rather than hidden.

refined.name: Localized revision hull (LRH)
refined.formal_definition:
LRH(h, b). Fix the CPDAG Ĉ, the elicited orientation claims K, the query (X, Y), and the closed MPDAG G₀ = Meek(Ĉ + K) with Z₀ = O*(G₀).

PRECONDITION (analyst-checkable, no oracle): G₀ is a valid MPDAG, Z₀ exists, and Z₀ is a valid adjustment set in G₀.

SCREEN (no estimand is evaluated to compute it). Let d(·) be the skeleton hop distance in Ĉ from {X, Y}, and for a claim k = (u→v) let d(k) = min(d(u), d(v)). The query-local claims are T_h := { k ∈ K : d(k) ≤ h }. Default h = 0.

ADMITTED FAMILY (DAG-level, which is what removes the Meek-no-op problem: a "retraction" that Meek re-derives simply contributes no new DAG).
  𝔇(h, b) := { D ∈ ext(Ĉ) : dis(D) ⊆ T_h and |dis(D)| ≤ b },  where dis(D) := { k ∈ K : D contradicts k }.
Equivalently, and this is how it is computed without ever enumerating ext(Ĉ):
  𝔇(h, b) = ⋃_{A ⊆ T_h, |A| ≤ b} ext( Meek(Ĉ + K[A reversed]) ),  the A = ∅ term being ext(G₀).
b is an elicitation error budget declared by the analyst, not a discovered radius; h is fixed a priori.

ESTIMATES. On one dataset of size n, θ̂_D := OLS coefficient on X in Y ~ X + O*(D) for each D ∈ 𝔇(h, b), with its standard error ŝe_D. Write ŝe := max_D ŝe_D.

REPORTED INTERVAL.  I(h, b, c) := [ min_D θ̂_D − c·ŝe , max_D θ̂_D + c·ŝe ], with 𝔇 empty replaced by the singleton {(θ̂_{Z₀}, ŝe_{Z₀})}. c > 0 is the single calibrated scalar. The reported number is the width |I| = (max θ̂ − min θ̂) + 2c·ŝe.

What is deleted relative to the audited draft: λ, δ, the prefix, the "selective completeness theorem", and all retrieval language. λ was provably void (λ(k) ≤ δ bounds the width it can add by δ, so the threshold's saving is bounded by the threshold), circular (defined through the estimand it is meant to protect), unsound at b = 2, and measurably more expensive than the blanket. The hop screen is none of those: it is computed from the skeleton of Ĉ alone, it is not defined through θ, and it strictly reduces the number of DAGs scored.

  /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josecosta-mugango/1cbd3bff-6ceb-4991-8a2a-b20d5a3f01d3/scratchpad/w5f/lrh3.py       (dense/large regime)
  /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josecosta-mugango/1cbd3bff-6ceb-4991-8a2a-b20d5a3f01d3/scratchpad/w5f/sound.py      (population soundness check)

def hop_screen(chat, x, y, K, h):                      # zero estimand evaluations
    adj = defaultdict(set)
    for u, v in chat.skeleton(): adj[u].add(v); adj[v].add(u)
    d = {x: 0, y: 0}; q = deque([x, y])
    while q:
        c = q.popleft()
        for nb in adj[c]:
            if nb not in d: d[nb] = d[c] + 1; q.append(nb)
    return [k for k in K if min(d.get(k[0], INF), d.get(k[1], INF)) <= h]

def lrh_interval(chat, K, x, y, data, h=0, b=1, c=None):
    g0 = apply_orientations(chat, K)                    # meek_closure inside; None => K inconsistent
    if g0 is None: raise Inconsistent
    z0 = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(g0, x, y)
    if z0 is None or not is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(g0, x, y, z0): raise PreconditionFailed
    T = hop_screen(chat, x, y, K, h)

    fam = {frozenset(D.directed_edges): D for D in enumerate_dag_extensions(g0)}
    for j in range(1, b + 1):
        for A in combinations(T, j):
            Krev = [ (k[1], k[0]) if k in A else k for k in K ]
            gA = apply_orientations(chat, Krev)         # None => that revision is inconsistent, skip
            if gA is None: continue
            for D in enumerate_dag_extensions(gA):
                fam.setdefault(frozenset(D.directed_edges), D)

    S = np.cov(data, rowvar=False); idx = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(nodes)}
    def ols(reg):                                       # theta-hat and se on the SAME data
        r = [idx[v] for v in reg]; Srr = S[np.ix_(r, r)]; Sry = S[r, idx[y]]
        Si = np.linalg.inv(Srr); beta = Si @ Sry
        rv = float(S[idx[y], idx[y]] - Sry @ beta)
        return float(beta[0]), float(np.sqrt(max(rv, 1e-12) * Si[0, 0] / len(data)))

    pts = [ols([x, *sorted(set(optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y)) - {x, y})]) for D in fam.values()]
    if not pts: pts = [ols([x, *sorted(set(z0) - {x, y})])]
    lo = min(t for t, _ in pts); hi = max(t for t, _ in pts); se = max(s for _, s in pts)
    return (lo - c * se, hi + c * se)

# Oracle / population mode (no data): swap ols(...) for
#   adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, Zd)  and  sqrt(asymptotic_variance(sem, x, y, Zd) / n).

def calibrate_c(problems, h, b, target=0.95):           # bisection, the ONLY knob, same for every row
    def cov(c):
        return mean(abs(tau - ctr) <= half + c * se
                    for ctr, half, se, tau in centers_halfwidths_ses(problems, h, b))
    lo, hi = 0.0, 400.0
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if cov(mid) >= target: hi = mid
        else: lo = mid
    return hi
refined.guarantee:
CONDITIONAL SOUNDNESS (this replaces the promissory "selective-completeness theorem", which had no theorem and used the wrong word).

Let D* be the true DAG, Ĉ its CPDAG, and F := { k ∈ K : D* contradicts k } the set of false claims. Assume the precondition above, and amenability of the query (Y ∈ de(X) in D*, so O*(D*) is a valid adjustment set in D* and θ_{D*} = τ*). If
  (i) every k ∈ F satisfies d(k) ≤ h, and (ii) |F| ≤ b,
then D* ∈ 𝔇(h, b), hence τ* ∈ [min_D θ_D, max_D θ_D] at the population level, and the reported interval fails only through sampling error, which is what c·ŝe is for.

Measured (sound.py, 600 problems, nodes 6–9, seed 424242, population estimands): the antecedent holds in 0.698 of problems; containment there is 419/419 = 1.0000 with zero violations; where the antecedent fails, containment drops to 169/181 = 0.9337. The theorem is exactly as strong and exactly as weak as that.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, and must not be written.
- No completeness. The hull can be strictly wider than the identified set of the truth, and nothing bounds the excess.
- No continuity bound. Damage conditional on Z moving is heavy-tailed; the interval is sound by membership, so it is indifferent to the tail, but "small structural error implies small width" is false and is never claimed.
- No robustness under an estimated CPDAG. Every run uses the true equivalence class; under an estimated Ĉ the truth can leave the family for reasons that have nothing to do with h or b, and no row of the table may be labelled otherwise.
- The antecedent is unverifiable in practice, and its screen half of it is weak: measured (lrh2.py, regime A) P(the single false claim is query-local | exactly one false claim) = 0.483, P(all false claims query-local | at least one) = 0.440. So the honest reading of direction (4) is that the hop screen ranks by proximity to the query, not by falsity; it is a locality prior on where damage lands, and its miss rate is reported, not bounded.
- Consequently the row is not sound at ≥ 2 planted false claims: measured coverage (lrh.py, regime A, c frozen at its marginal calibration) 0.788 for LRH(h=0,b=1) against the blanket's 1.000 on that stratum. That failure must appear in the table as its own row, not be absorbed into a marginal 0.95.
refined.width_rule:
THE CONVERSION TO THE SINGLE SCALAR.
1. Split the synthetic benchmark once into a calibration half and an evaluation half.
2. For every method in the table, including the baselines, fit its one scalar c by bisection to empirical coverage of τ* equal to 0.95 on the calibration half, then freeze it. One knob per row, same procedure for every row, no second tuning parameter: h and b are declared before the sweep and are properties of the method, not fitted.
3. Report on the evaluation half: mean |I|, and beside it median and 90th-percentile |I|, because the damage distribution is heavy-tailed and one tail problem moves a mean.
4. Report the row stratified, never as one number alone: by whether an elicited claim touches X or Y, and by the number of planted false claims (0 / 1 / ≥2), with the coverage each stratum actually gets at the frozen c.

refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Four predictions, each with the measurement that would kill it. They are stated so the planned sweep can refute them without re-deriving anything.

D1 — the row sits strictly between the two endpoints. On the paper's grid, LRH(h=0, b=1) will have calibrated mean width in [0.70, 0.90] of the blanket's, and 2.0 to 3.0 times better than the point estimate on the elicited set. Measured across three regimes: 0.770, 0.832, 0.732 (split-calibrated 0.782); point/blanket 2.258, 2.255, 2.708. FALSIFIED by any regime giving a ratio ≥ 0.95 (the method has collapsed into the blanket and the paper's selectivity bet is dead) or ≤ 0.40 (the screen is discarding real damage and coverage is being bought entirely by c, which the per-stratum coverage will show).

D2 — the honest degeneracy, disclosed rather than hidden. The structural half-width max θ̂ − min θ̂ is exactly zero on 0.60 to 0.80 of problems, and that zero mass coincides with the no-damage stratum. Measured: 0.710, 0.733, 0.700; distinct values 117/400 and 81/300, so the width distribution is continuous where it is non-zero (median 0.0000, p90 0.3210, max 1.5135 in regime A). This is not the r_val collapse: r_val collapsed to its minimum, this is a maximum over the admitted family and it moves toward over-width. FALSIFIED if the zero mass exceeds 0.90 (the row is DoubleML with extra machinery and should be withdrawn) or falls below 0.40 (damage is not concentrated near the query, which refutes the locality premise the whole paper rests on).

D3 — the saving comes from the locality screen, not from the budget. The unscreened hull at b = 2 will be within 5 per cent of the blanket, while the screened LRH(h=0, b=2) stays below 0.90 of it. Measured: unscreened b = 2 at 0.954, 0.995, 0.967; screened b = 2 at 0.817, 0.886, 0.748. FALSIFIED if an unscreened b = 2 row beats the blanket by more than 5 per cent in any regime, in which case the screen is decorative and only b matters.

D4 — the kill condition, named in advance. LRH degenerates to the blanket as T_h → K together with b → |K|, and to the point estimate when T_h = ∅ (measured 0.282 and 0.497 of problems in regimes A and B, where the row is literally the DoubleML endpoint at zero structural width). The audit's claim that the gap shrinks with graph size does not reproduce for this screen: the ratio went 0.770 → 0.832 → 0.732 as the mean class size went 6.0 → 8.1 → 15.4, so the sentence "nine nodes is the least favourable case" stays deleted and no monotone size story is claimed in either direction. refined.name: Endpoint provenance for the order-m retraction hull
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING. Chat is the true equivalence class (never an estimated one). K = (k_1,...,k_q) are the elicited orientation claims, held as SENTENCES, not as edges. G0 := cl(K) = apply_orientations(Chat, K). Z := O*(G0) = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, x, y), assumed to exist; theta_hat := adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, Z). For a DAG D write theta_D := adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y)).

RETRACTION FIBRE. For S subset of K, F(S) := cl(K \ S) = apply_orientations(Chat, K \ S), and Theta(S) := { theta_D : D in enumerate_dag_extensions(F(S)) }. "rev" is fixed here once and for all as RETRACTION (drop the sentence), not flip. Retraction is the primitive because it is the only elementary move guaranteed to contain the truth when the sentence is false; the flip fibre cl(K \ {k} + reverse(k)) is a strict subset of F({k}). Measured on this machine: the flip-fibre range equals the retraction-fibre range on 100.0% of non-silent instances at 9, 11 and 13 nodes (ep.py, "flip-fibre lemma holds : 1.0000"), so the two coincide empirically, but the definition uses retraction and the coincidence is reported as measured, never assumed.

ORDER-m HULL. H_m := [ min_{|S| <= m} min Theta(S) , max_{|S| <= m} max Theta(S) ], with H_0 = {theta_hat} (a singleton, because O*(G0) exists means every extension of G0 agrees on O*, so every extension gives theta_hat) and H_q = the blanket hedge over the whole class. m is a DECLARED assumption on the number of simultaneously false sentences, printed with the interval, never tuned on the evaluation split.

ENDPOINT PROVENANCE (this is a reporting layer on H_m, not a replacement for r_val and not itself the non-degenerate quantity). Define S+ := the minimal-cardinality, then lexicographically first, S attaining max H_m, and D+ := an argmax of theta_D over enumerate_dag_extensions(F(S+)); symmetrically S-, D-. The upper endpoint carries provenance ONLY if max H_m > theta_hat + tol; an endpoint equal to theta_hat is the analyst's own number and is reported with no sentence attached. (This clause is load-bearing: without it every fibre attains the theta_hat-side endpoint and the provenance names 99.06% of all elicited sentences, measured, which is a label that says nothing. With it, provenance names a mean of 1.12 sentences out of a mean |K| = 3.67.) The reported card for each end is ( S+, Delta+ := O*(D+) sym-diff Z, theta_{D+}, theta_{D+} - theta_hat ). Delta+ is well defined even when D+ is not: across all four sweeps, every DAG tied at an endpoint argmax yielded the same O*, 100.0% of instances.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a claim that the named sentence is false, and the plain reading must say "a world, admissible on the data, in which the answer differs", never "the world in which it is wrong".
refined.pseudocode:
```python
# runs as written against the listed functions; PYTHONHASHSEED-independent because every
# set that feeds the RNG or the argmax is sorted first (the cert.py defect the audit found).
from itertools import combinations
from math import sqrt
import numpy as np
from bkrobust.demo.meek import apply_orientations, enumerate_dag_extensions
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import (optimal_adjustment_set_dag, optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag,
                                    adjusted_estimand, asymptotic_variance)

TOL = 1e-9

def theta(sem, x, y, D):
    return adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y))

def endpoint_provenance(chat, K, x, y, sem, m=1):
    """Order-m retraction hull with provenance on each endpoint. K is a LIST of sentences."""
    K = sorted(K)
    G0 = apply_orientations(chat, K)
    if G0 is None:
        return None                      # elicited claims inconsistent with the class
    Z = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, x, y)
    if Z is None:
        return None                      # O* not identified by G0: object does not apply
    Z = frozenset(Z)
    hat = adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, Z)
    lo = hi = hat
    up = dn = None                       # (S, D, theta)
    for r in range(1, m + 1):            # minimal-cardinality S wins ties by construction
        for S in combinations(K, r):
            G = apply_orientations(chat, [k for k in K if k not in S])
            if G is None:
                continue
            for D in enumerate_dag_extensions(G):
                t = theta(sem, x, y, D)
                if t > hi + TOL: hi, up = t, (S, D, t)
                if t < lo - TOL: lo, dn = t, (S, D, t)

    def card(rec):
        if rec is None:
            return None                  # endpoint == theta_hat: no sentence is responsible
        S, D, t = rec
        return dict(sentences=list(S),
                    delta=set(optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y)) ^ set(Z),
                    theta=t, moves_by=t - hat)

    return dict(order=m, hat=hat, hull=(lo, hi), width=hi - lo,
                upper=card(up), lower=card(dn),
                se_unit=sqrt(asymptotic_variance(sem, x, y, Z)))

def calibrated_width(recs, taus, n_obs, alpha=0.05):
    """Single scalar gamma fit on a CALIBRATION split; report mean width on the held-out split."""
    se  = np.array([r["se_unit"] / sqrt(n_obs) for r in recs])
    lo  = np.array([r["hull"][0] for r in recs])
    hi  = np.array([r["hull"][1] for r in recs])
    tau = np.asarray(taus)
    need = np.maximum(np.maximum((lo - tau) / se, (tau - hi) / se), 0.0)
    gamma = float(np.quantile(need, 1 - alpha, method="higher"))
    cov   = float(np.mean((lo - gamma*se <= tau + 1e-12) & (tau - 1e-12 <= hi + gamma*se)))
    return gamma, cov, float(np.mean(hi - lo + 2*gamma*se))
```

refined.guarantee:
TWO STATEMENTS, KEPT APART.

1. HULL SOUNDNESS, indexed by m (this is the theorem; it belongs to H_m, not to the provenance card). If Chat is the true equivalence class, and at most m of the q elicited sentences are false, then letting S* be the set of false sentences (|S*| <= m), every remaining sentence is true of D*, so D* is a consistent extension of cl(K \ S*) = F(S*), hence tau = theta_{D*} lies in Theta(S*) and therefore in H_m. Population coverage 1. Measured, 300 instances per cell, 9 nodes, p = 0.26, 3-8 undirected edges (ep2.py): with one false sentence H_1 covers 1.0000, H_2 1.0000, H_3 1.0000, blanket 1.0000; with two false sentences H_1 covers 0.9500 and H_2 1.0000; with three, H_1 0.8333, H_2 0.9667, H_3 1.0000. The guarantee is indexed by a count the analyst does not observe, so m must be printed in the row label and the failure below m must be printed in the same paragraph as the coverage.

THE FAILURE IS SILENT, and that is the fact the paper exists to expose. At 9 nodes with two false sentences, H_1 has zero width on 67.67% of instances and is zero-width-AND-wrong on 4.00%; at three false sentences, zero-width-and-wrong on 15.00%. The blanket hedge covers all of those.

2. PROVENANCE: EXHIBITION ONLY. The card ( S+, Delta+, theta_{D+} ) proves that a DAG admissible on the data, reachable by retracting exactly the sentences in S+, assigns theta_{D+} to the query and adjusts on a set differing from Z by Delta+. It does not claim that world is likely, that S+ is false, that theta_{D+} is the worst value outside the enumerated fibres, or anything about several sentences being wrong at once beyond the declared m. No continuity bound is asserted anywhere: damage conditional on Z moving is heavy-tailed and the object never uses a small-perturbation-implies-small-bias step.

PROVENANCE IS LEVERAGE, NOT FALSITY, and the number goes in the same sentence as the ranking, always. Measured (ep3.py, 9 nodes, one false sentence, 149 fired of 400): P(the named sentence is the actually false one | provenance fired) = 0.3893 +/- 0.0399, against 0.2880 for naming a sentence of K uniformly at random - a lift of 1.35, about 2.5 sigma. Weakly informative, nowhere near a detector. Consistent with the audit's finding that the leverage score ranks below chance (AUC 0.4106) among already-certified claims.

THE REFUTATION LOOP IS KILLED. The card is display-only. An expert may not see a witness and then remove its sentence from the audit: the audit measured that one adaptive round moves hull coverage 1.0000 -> 0.6226, and 1.0000 -> 0.0000 on the stratum where the witness named the genuinely false sentence. If expert refutation appears in the paper at all it is pre-registered - worlds ruled out BEFORE any endpoint is computed - and the adaptive variant is reported with those numbers, not hedged in prose.
refined.width_rule:
ROW CONSTRUCTION. For a declared order m, the reported interval is I_m = [ lo_m - gamma * se_hat , hi_m + gamma * se_hat ] with se_hat = sqrt(asymptotic_variance(sem, x, y, Z) / n) and a single scalar gamma fit on a held-out calibration split as the smallest value reaching 95% empirical coverage; the table reports the mean width of I_m on the evaluation split. The structural hull and the sampling term are separate terms, not one scaled object, for a reason the metric would otherwise punish arbitrarily: a singleton hull scales to itself, so a method that is silent everywhere would be uncalibratable rather than merely wide. Under this rule silence is priced - it is paid for in gamma, uniformly, on every instance including the ones with zero structural width.

MEASURED (ep2.py, 9 nodes, p = 0.26, 300 instances per cell, n = 500; gamma fit in-sample here and declared as such - the manuscript version fits it on a calibration half):

  one false sentence : point-on-elicited-set 1.3861 (gamma 13.22, oracle coverage 0.8567)
                       ours m=1  0.2191 (gamma 0)   m=2 0.2805   blanket 0.2875
  two false          : point 1.6317 (gamma 15.68)
                       ours m=1  0.5920 (gamma 3.87, coverage bought by inflating every
                       instance)   m=2 0.2896   blanket 0.3014
  three false        : point 2.1587    m=1 1.5559   m=2 0.3128   m=3 0.3632   blanket 0.3647

THE CLAIM THE TABLE LICENSES, AND NO MORE. The selective saving over the blanket hedge is 23.8% at m=1, 3.9% at m=2, 0.4% at m=3. "Damage is local" pays at order one and is essentially exhausted by order two, because cl(K \ S) collapses toward Chat as |S| grows. Say that; do not say the method beats the blanket in general. At 11 and 13 nodes the m=1 saving is 18.8% (0.1689 vs 0.2079) and 25.1% (0.0975 vs 0.1301), so the effect is stable in graph size at one false sentence.

AND THE ROW THAT MUST APPEAR BESIDE IT. The naive point estimate is not always the loser: at 13 nodes / p = 0.16 / one false sentence its oracle coverage is already 0.9533, so its calibrated width is 0.0000 and it wins the table outright. A width table without the silent-failure rate printed next to it is uninterpretable, and the headline configuration must be chosen and declared by that rate rather than by the width it yields.

WHERE m COMES FROM. m is an assumption, so the honest presentation is the whole ladder m = 0, 1, 2, ..., q as rows, with the crossing visible: the width-minimising honest rung is the smallest m whose empirical miss rate is under 5%, and choosing it on the evaluation split would be cheating. Report the ladder, not the winner.

ONE ACKNOWLEDGED APPROXIMATION. Every number above is population arithmetic with oracle access to the SEM. A deployed hull is a max and a min over ESTIMATED quantities and is therefore upward biased in width, which is exactly what this metric scores; the bias grows with the number of distinct adjustment sets entering the hull (the audit measured a mean of 2.12, max 4, at this scale). The estimated version must be run before the table is final, and the gap reported.
