One apply_orientations plus one enumerate_dag_extensions per subset S with |S| <= m, i.e. sum_{r <= m} C(q, r) fibre enumerations per problem; with the sweep's mean |K| = 3.45-4.43 that is about 3.5 extra enumerations at m = 1. Measured end to end on this machine (Darwin, CPU, numpy only, no SAT solver, none needed): 300 instances with the full m=1 hull, provenance cards, blanket hull and calibration in 1.2-1.8 s; the whole m = 1,2,3 ladder over 300 instances in 3.0 s (one false sentence) to 5.8 s (three false); 13-node cells in 2.3-3.5 s. The provenance layer itself is one argmax pass over extensions already enumerated for the hull plus two set differences, consistent with the audit's measurement that the card pass is 2.76% of the score pass.

The dominant term is enumerate_dag_extensions, exponential in the size of the undirected components, so the binding constraint is component size and q, not m and not provenance. Cost grows as C(q, m); at q around 4 the full ladder to m = q is affordable, and the honest presentation is to report the whole ladder rather than one rung. Everything above ran in minutes, not hours, as required.

refined.name: b-bounded load-bearing cover U_b (b fixed at 2), with the error-budget soundness theorem
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING, and the choice the proposal left unstated. Fix the true CPDAG Chat = dag_to_cpdag(D*), a query (X,Y), an elicited claim set K of oriented edges, and G_0 = Meek(Chat, K). For an orientation profile o (a list of oriented edges) let G[o] = apply_orientations(Chat, o), which is None when o is refuted by the observed class. Define

  Theta(G) := { adjusted_estimand(sem, X, Y, O*(D)) : D in enumerate_dag_extensions(G) },   Theta(None) := empty set,

i.e. THE VALUE THE ANALYST WOULD REPORT IF SHE BELIEVED D, with O* recomputed per candidate truth (optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D,X,Y)). This is the analyst-per-candidate-truth reading, NOT the fixed-Z-carried-across-truths reading; the latter is the r_val = 1 event and would put the object straight back into the degeneracy it exists to escape. Write w(S) = max S - min S.

REVISION PROFILES. For A subset of K, Sigma(A) := the 2^|A| profiles in which every k in A is either RETRACTED (dropped from K) or REVERSED (replaced by its flip), and every claim outside A is kept as elicited.

SET LOAD-BEARINGNESS. lambda(A) := w( Theta(G_0) union U_{o in Sigma(A)} Theta(G[o]) ) - w( Theta(G_0) ) >= 0.

THE OBJECT. The b-bounded load-bearing cover is the FLAT set

  U_b := { k in K : there exists A containing k with |A| <= b and lambda(A) > 0 }.

No minimality, no antichain: the minimal family L_b of the proposal is dropped, because minimality deletes exactly the mixed pair {load-bearing, not-load-bearing-alone} whose joint correction the interval then lacks (measured cost: coverage 0.989 with the antichain against 1.000 without, for 0.742x against 0.786x blanket width, audit_wit8_6_nomin.py).

b IS FIXED AT 2 A PRIORI, never selected on the evaluation set. U_1 (the singleton ranking) is the b=1 face of the same object and is reported only as the ablation row.

LOCALITY RESTRICTION ON THE PAIR SEARCH. Let ell(k) := min over the two endpoints of k of the skeleton hop distance in Chat to {X,Y}. At b=2 only pairs {k,k'} with min(ell(k), ell(k')) <= 1 are tested. This is justified by the paper's own locality measurement (0.1376 silent-failure at hop 0 against 0.000423 at hop >= 2), not by an unexplained increment, and it is honestly a COST CONTROL for long elicitations: at the sizes measurable here it removes 0.4 per cent of pairs and changes U_2 on 0 of 166 problems (final_wit8_1_cover.py), so its benefit is projected and unmeasured.

RETRIEVAL OUTPUT (direction 4), kept separate from the interval. Rank K by lambda({k}), then rank U_2 \ U_1 by max over the tested pairs containing k of lambda({k,k'}). The interval consumes the flattened set U_b; the ranking is a deliverable in its own right and must not be described as entering the interval.
refined.guarantee:
LEMMA (monotonicity of lambda). For A subset of A' subset of K, lambda(A) <= lambda(A'). Proof in one line: every o in Sigma(A) is the image of some o' in Sigma(A') that retracts the extra claims, and retracting an oriented edge only removes constraints from the Meek closure, so Theta(G[o]) is contained in Theta(G[o']); the union defining lambda(A) is therefore contained in the one defining lambda(A'). Measured 0 violations in 4608 pair-against-singleton tests (final_wit8_2_calib.py) and 0 in 2032 in the audit's own run. This lemma, not non-submodularity, is what carries the guarantee; non-submodularity carries nothing and belongs in a remark motivating b >= 2.

THEOREM (soundness under a b-claim error budget). Let E be the set of false claims in K and let I_b = [min H, max H] be the reported interval. If |E| <= b then the true total effect lies in I_b.
Proof. Two cases. (i) lambda(E) > 0: then by definition every k in E lies in U_b, so the profile o* that reverses each k in E and retracts each k in U_b \ E belongs to Sigma(U_b). All orientations surviving in o* are true, so the true DAG D* is a consistent extension of G[o*], hence the true effect = adjusted_estimand(sem, X, Y, O*(D*)) lies in Theta(G[o*]) which is contained in H. (ii) lambda(E) = 0: then correcting E enlarges nothing, Theta(G[o*]) is already contained in Theta(G_0), and the true effect is in Theta(G_0) which is contained in H. Either way the truth is inside.

WHY THE ANTICHAIN HAD TO GO. Case (i) is exactly where minimality breaks the proof: if E = {k, k'} with lambda({k}) > 0 and lambda({k'}) = 0 then {k, k'} is not minimal, k' is excluded from L_b, and o* is not in Sigma(L_b). Measured price of the bug: coverage 0.989 with the antichain against 1.000 without.

REGULARITY CONDITIONS, stated rather than assumed. (a) Chat is the TRUE CPDAG throughout; nothing here is a robustness claim under an estimated CPDAG. (b) O*(D*) must be a valid adjustment set for (X,Y) in D*, which the harness audit measured to hold on 1.000 of non-null draws and to FAIL on 49.2 per cent of null-effect draws; this is why the null filter is a precondition of the theorem, not a cosmetic. (c) Theta is the per-candidate-truth value set of the definition; under the fixed-Z reading the theorem is false.

WHAT THE THEOREM IS NOT. It is a containment statement under an error budget on the COUNT of false claims. It says nothing about how far the estimate moves as a function of how wrong the knowledge is, and it must never be written as a continuity bound: damage conditional on Z moving is heavy-tailed (median relative bias 0.59, up to 128 times), which refutes that reading directly. The hypothesis is checkable in deployment in the only sense that matters, because "at most b of my sentences are wrong" is a budget an analyst can be asked to accept, unlike the proposal's "E is contained in the union of the family", which is an unobservable property of the truth and was measured false on the majority of runs on which the method covers (recall of U_1 against the two false claims: 0.266 of 2).
refined.width_rule:
THE ROW. Compute (U_2, I_2) by cover_and_interval. The reported interval is I_2 = [min H, max H] with centre c = (min H + max H)/2 and half-width h = (max H - min H)/2. The table's calibration scales it: I_2(s) = c +/- s*h; take s* = the smallest s on a HELD-OUT draw at which empirical coverage of the true effect reaches 0.95; the table entry is mean(2 s* h) on the evaluation draw. Lower is better. Rows: ours (b=2) in bold, ours (b=1) as the ablation, blanket hedge over the whole equivalence class, DoubleML on the elicited Z, TabPFN, CausalPFN, Do-PFN, enumeration of total effects. b is never chosen on the evaluation set.

MEASURED, on the repo harness at n=7, |K| mean 4.55, two false claims, population covariance, non-null queries, informative stratum = positive blanket width (final_wit8_2_calib.py, seed 311, 174 problems; final_wit8_1_cover.py, seed 90712, 166 problems, agrees):

  b = 1 (U_1)     INADMISSIBLE. Coverage saturates at 0.839 under any scaling.
  b = 2 (U_2)     s* = 1.000, coverage 1.000, calibrated mean width 0.6671  = 0.863x blanket
  blanket         s* = 1.000, coverage 1.000, calibrated mean width 0.7728  = 1.000x
  raw hull widths, same stratum: b=1 0.3527 at coverage 0.771; b=2 0.6701; blanket 0.7792.

THE ADMISSIBILITY ARGUMENT, which is the strongest thing this object has and was in nobody's proposal. The metric calibrates by SCALING, and scaling a zero-width interval leaves it zero-width. Theta(G_0) is a single point on 0.993 of non-null draws, and U_1 is empty on 0.488 of informative problems, so the b=1 hedge is a point interval on 0.460 of them and is wrong on a fifth of those. No scalar lifts it to 0.95. Every b=2 miss carries positive width and is scalable. That converts b >= 2 from an optional extension into the only admissible member of the family.

TWO HONEST CAVEATS ON THE NUMBERS ABOVE. First, at population level coverage jumps from 0.253 at s = 0.99 to 1.000 at s = 1.00 for b=2 (0.155 to 1.000 for the blanket), because the truth sits exactly on the hull boundary when there is no sampling noise; the calibration step is therefore a no-op here and the comparison reduces to raw hull width. The table must be produced at finite n, where the endpoints are estimated and s* is genuinely live. Second, the null filter and the informative-stratum restriction are load-bearing: unfiltered, 78.7 per cent of draws have zero blanket width and every method ties at zero, so the single scalar distinguishes nothing.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Three predictions, each with the number I measured and the observation that kills it. The proposal's own pre-committed negative result ("joint load-bearing pairs do not carry measurable width") is RETRACTED: it is refuted on this harness, U_2 \ U_1 has mean size 2.42 claims and moves coverage from 0.771 to 1.000.

P1. THE b=1 FACE IS DEGENERATE IN THE ZERO-WIDTH DIRECTION, and inadmissibly so. On the paper's sweep I predict U_1 empty on 40 to 60 per cent of informative problems, Theta(G_0) a single point on more than 95 per cent of draws, and b=1 coverage saturating strictly below 0.95 under scaling. Measured here: 0.488 empty, 0.993 point-valued, saturation at 0.839 (informative) and 0.907 (all non-null). KILLED IF b=1 reaches 0.95 under scaling on the sweep, in which case the pair layer is unnecessary and the object should be published as the singleton ranking of direction (4) alone. This is the mirror image of the defect being fixed: r_val collapsed to the constant 1, U_1 collapses to the constant zero width.

P2. b=2 IS NOT DEGENERATE, in either direction. I predict P(U_2 empty | informative) < 0.25 and mean |U_2| strictly between 0 and |K|, so the hedge is neither a point nor the blanket. Measured: 0.151 empty, |U_2| = 3.05 against |K| = 4.55. KILLED IF U_2 = K on more than half of problems, which would make b=2 the blanket under another name and the selective bet dead by construction. Note the thinning is fast: at b=3 the cover is the blanket at these sizes, so the paper must say plainly that this is a b <= 2 bet.

P3. THE SELECTIVE-WIDTH BET IMPROVES WITH ELICITATION LENGTH, and this is the experiment that decides the paper. Because |U_2| is bounded by the number of query-adjacent claims while |K| grows with m, I predict width/blanket at b=2 stays in (0.6, 0.95) at m about 5 and FALLS monotonically as m grows at fixed query locality. Measured at m = 4.55: 0.863 calibrated, 0.834 raw, and the load-bearing claims sit at mean hop 0.00 (singletons) and 0.31 (synergy pairs), which is the locality law showing up inside the cover. KILLED IF width/blanket at b=2 fails to fall below 0.80 at the sweep's realistic m of about 50. If that happens the correct output is a negative-results entry, "selective widening does not pay at realistic elicitation length", with revive_if tied to a measured sublinear growth of |U_2| in m or to locality surviving at hop >= 2, and NOT a larger search budget. The b=2-against-b=1 comparison is not the decisive experiment; the m sweep is.
refined.cost:
EXACT COUNT. One closure for G_0, 2m for the singletons, and 4 per tested pair (the 2^2 profiles), each closure followed by enumerate_dag_extensions on the result: 1 + 2m + 4 P closures, where P is the number of pairs surviving the locality filter and the already-covered skip. Caching on frozenset(profile) removes the repeats, which is where most of the saving actually comes from since profiles that retract everything coincide across pairs.

MEASURED. m = 4.55, P = 8.16 tested pairs per problem, whole 300-problem run in 5.9 s wall on one CPU core in plain Python, about 20 ms per problem including the SEM draw and the blanket comparison (final_wit8_1_cover.py, final_wit8_2_calib.py). Comfortably inside the minutes budget; the 2,087-problem sweep is well under a minute of compute at these graph sizes.

SCALING, and the honest state of the fix. Unrestricted b=2 is 4 C(m,2), which is 1225 pairs at a realistic elicitation of m = 50 and is the first thing that breaks. The locality restriction turns m^2 into m times the number of query-adjacent claims, i.e. O(m q) with q the count at hop <= 1. It is justified by the paper's measured locality (0.1376 at hop 0 against 0.000423 at hop >= 2) rather than by an arbitrary rule, and it costs nothing that could be detected at the sizes runnable here: 99.6 per cent of pairs retained, U_2 identical on 166 of 166 problems. That means the saving is PROJECTED and unmeasured, and the paper must say so; measuring it is part of the m sweep of P3, not a separate contribution.

WHAT WAS DELETED AND WHY IT COST NOTHING. The proposal's greedy restricted expansion is provably vacuous under monotonicity plus minimality, since any superset of a positive singleton is non-minimal and so never a member, and in the stratum where synergy pairs live it has no seed 75 per cent of the time. Dropping the antichain removes the reason greedy looked necessary, and the exhaustive hop-restricted enumeration is the only version that ever ran.

ONE COST THAT IS NOT COMPUTE. The test lambda(A) > 0 is well posed at population level, where lambda is bimodal (smallest positive value 0.0425, median 0.49, max 3.51, and sweeping the threshold from 0 to 1e-2 leaves |U_1|/|K| flat at 0.0316). At finite n, which is where the target metric lives, lambda is estimated and the test becomes a hypothesis test with a threshold nobody has justified. Budget for that in the finite-n table rather than letting a reviewer find it.

refined.name: The load-bearing claim set L (validity-first claim partition), reported beside r_val
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING. Ĉ = the equivalence class (every run uses the true CPDAG; no robustness is claimed under an estimated one). K = the elicited orientation claims. G0 = apply_orientations(Ĉ, K). Z = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, X, Y). rev((a,b)) = (b,a).

ADMISSIBLE SINGLE REVISIONS. For k ∈ K, holding the rest of K fixed,
  R1(k) = { apply_orientations(Ĉ, K∖{k}) , apply_orientations(Ĉ, (K∖{k}) ∪ {rev(k)}) } ∖ {None}.
The two members are the retraction and the reversal; the reversal is absent when the rest of K plus Meek forbids it.

THE OBJECT REPORTED (a set, not a fraction):
  L(K, X, Y, Z) := { k ∈ K : ∃ G ∈ R1(k) with is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(G, X, Y, Z) = False }.

RESIDUAL LABELS. The validity test above runs FIRST and alone decides membership in L; the labels below are descriptive and never gate it (this is the audit's fix (2), and it is what makes the guarantee true). For k ∉ L:
  • CPDAG-refuted iff apply_orientations(Ĉ, [rev(k)]) is None — refuted by the equivalence class ALONE, with no other elicited claim in the conditioning set;
  • inert iff apply_orientations(Ĉ, K∖{k}) = G0 — Meek re-derives k from the rest, so it carried no information;
  • free otherwise.

THREE THINGS THE SUBMITTED VERSION HAD AND THIS ONE DOES NOT.
(i) φ₁ is deleted. The denominator was the whole attack surface: appending claims G0 already entails moves φ₁ on 54.1% of problems and moves it DOWN (mean 0.3138 → 0.1929), so the expert who says more looks safer. |L| moves on 10.2% and moves UP (48 up / 1 down at per-claim error 0.50; 14 up / 3 down at 0.20), i.e. toward more caution. If a scalar is required it is |L|.
(ii) data-refuted is redefined against Ĉ alone, and the cell is then empty: 0 of 890 claims in the 300-problem sweep, 0 of 11 demo claims. That empty column is the honest answer and it is worth printing, because the old cell (231 of 231 labels having a CPDAG-permitted reversal, 48.9% of which invalidate Z) was self-certification by the very claims under suspicion.
(iii) The "free of charge" sentence is gone entirely.

DEMO, corrected partition (final_inv2_demo.py, X = Statin, Y = CVD, Z = {Age, Smoke}):
  A: L = ∅; free {(Smoke,BMI)}; inert {(BMI,Chol), (Chol,CRP)}; CPDAG-refuted ∅.
  B: L = ∅; free {(Smoke,BMI), (Statin,CRP)}; inert {(BMI,Chol), (Chol,CRP)}; CPDAG-refuted ∅.
  C: L = {(BMI,Chol)}; free {(Statin,CRP)}; inert {(Chol,CRP)}; CPDAG-refuted ∅.
Z is valid in the true DAG in all three, so the two empty verdicts are correct verdicts, not misses.

POSITION IN THE PAPER. A companion diagnostic to r_val that grades the stratum r_val collapses, never a replacement for it. The equivalence is printed as a measured result, not denied: (|L| ≥ 1) ⟺ (r_val = 1) on 299/300 problems (99.7%).
refined.pseudocode:
import itertools
from bkrobust.demo.meek import apply_orientations, enumerate_dag_extensions
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import (optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag, optimal_adjustment_set_dag,
                                    is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag, adjusted_estimand)

def rev(k): return (k[1], k[0])

def revisions(chat, K, S, order=1):
    """Every MPDAG reachable by retracting or reversing at most `order` claims of S,
    with the rest of K held. Deduplicated; None (Meek-inconsistent) dropped."""
    seen, out = set(), []
    for r in range(1, order + 1):
        for combo in itertools.combinations(sorted(set(S)), r):
            rest = [e for e in K if e not in combo]
            for choice in itertools.product(*[([], [rev(k)]) for k in combo]):
                extra = [e for c in choice for e in c]
                g = apply_orientations(chat, rest + extra)
                if g is not None and g.edge_string() not in seen:
                    seen.add(g.edge_string()); out.append(g)
    return out

def load_bearing(chat, K, x, y, z):
    """L plus the descriptive residual. VALIDITY TEST FIRST -- the label order is what
    makes the completeness statement true."""
    g0 = apply_orientations(chat, K)
    L, refuted, inert, free = [], [], [], []
    for k in K:
        adm = revisions(chat, K, [k], order=1)                    # at most 2 graphs
        if any(not is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(g, x, y, z) for g in adm):
            L.append(k)
        elif apply_orientations(chat, [rev(k)]) is None:          # Chat ALONE forbids it
            refuted.append(k)
        elif apply_orientations(chat, [e for e in K if e != k]) == g0:
            inert.append(k)
        else:
            free.append(k)
    return L, refuted, inert, free

def hedge_interval(sem, chat, K, x, y, z, L, P=None):
    """The reported interval: the range of the adjusted estimand over every DAG
    extension of every admissible revision of order <= 2 inside L. P (the hop-0
    claims, those incident to x or y) is the optional valve when L is empty."""
    S = L if L else (P or [])
    vals = [adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, z)]                      # the elicited point
    for g in revisions(chat, K, S, order=2):
        for d in enumerate_dag_extensions(g):
            vals.append(adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(d, x, y)))
    return min(vals), max(vals)

# --- driver, exactly as run ---------------------------------------------------
# chat = dag_to_cpdag(dag); g0 = apply_orientations(chat, K)
# z    = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(g0, x, y)            # skip the problem if None
# L, refuted, inert, free = load_bearing(chat, K, x, y, z)
# P    = [k for k in K if k[0] in (x, y) or k[1] in (x, y)]
# lo, hi = hedge_interval(sem, chat, K, x, y, z, L, P)
# calibrate: q = 95th percentile of |tau - mid| / half over a calibration draw;
#            report mean of 2*half*q. Finite-n version replaces adjusted_estimand by
#            the fitted estimate and unions the per-graph confidence intervals.
#
# Regression check that must stay at zero (final_inv2_L.py section 3):
# for k not in L, for g in revisions(chat, K, [k], 1), for d in enumerate_dag_extensions(g):
#     assert is_valid_adjustment_set_dag(d, x, y, z)       # 962 checks, 0 violations
refined.guarantee:
WHAT SURVIVES (exact, not bounded, and stated with its conditioning visible).

THEOREM (single-claim completeness). For every k ∈ K∖L and every G ∈ R1(k), Z satisfies the back-door criterion in every DAG in the class represented by G. Exact because is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag quantifies over enumerate_dag_extensions rather than over a sample; complete over K because the loop is exhaustive. The reordering is what buys it: in the submitted version the label test ran before the validity test, and 34 of 267 data-refuted claims had an admissible retraction that invalidated Z while going unflagged (false on 7.7% of problems). Under the reordered definition the counterexample rate is 0 by construction, and 962 revisions of non-flagged claims across 300 problems produce 0 violations.

READ IT WITH ITS CONDITIONING. The certificate for k holds K∖{k} fixed. It is a statement about the sensitivity of Z to one revision, never a statement that K is true. No continuity is asserted anywhere: the object quantifies over a finite, explicitly enumerated revision set, so the heavy tail of damage conditional on Z moving is irrelevant to it.

DELETED, NOT REPAIRED. "Data-refuted claims cannot be wrong in any direction consistent with the true equivalence class and are free of charge." Under the old ordering the certificate was issued by the claims whose reliability is in question: 231 of 231 such labels had a reversal the CPDAG alone permits, and 48.9% of those reversals invalidate Z. Under the redefinition against Ĉ alone the cell is measured empty (0 of 890 claims, 0 of 11 demo claims), so there is nothing left to over-claim about.

THE HOLE, STATED AS MEASURED. L = ∅ certifies nothing about pairs, and this is the same Meek-bundling mechanism as the old data-refuted laundering, not an independent limitation. Among φ₁ = 0 problems, 2.0% admit a two-claim revision that kills Z; the residual uncoverable mass of the L-hedge is 2.00–2.25% at per-claim error 0.50 and 0.75% at 0.35. That is why the FLAG is order 1 and the HEDGE runs to order 2.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. L is not a detector of false claims and the paper must not score it as one: against the claims actually reversed by the erring expert, micro precision 0.190 and recall 0.462 at base rate 0.134, a lift of 1.4×. Load-bearingness is a property of the graph and wrongness is a property of the expert; direction (4)'s retrieval framing is the wrong frame for this object even though the earlier version volunteered it. No "first" claim, and no robustness claim under an estimated CPDAG.
refined.width_rule:
RULE. Report the interval I = [min Θ, max Θ] with
  Θ = { θ̂(Z) } ∪ { θ̂(O*(D)) : D ∈ enumerate_dag_extensions(G), G ∈ revisions(Ĉ, K, L, order ≤ 2) },
i.e. hedge over every admissible revision of order at most two RESTRICTED TO THE FLAGGED SET L, keeping the elicited point in the support. If L = ∅, the optional valve substitutes P = the hop-0 claims (those incident to X or Y). Calibrate to honest 95% by scaling the half-width by one global constant q, then report mean width; a method whose zero-width mass exceeds 5% cannot be calibrated at all and must be reported as such.

MEASURED (final_inv2_L4.py, three independent draws, n = 400 each, seeds 31/32/33, per-claim error 0.50/0.50/0.35; mean width at honest 95%, lower is better):
  order ≤2 on L (ours)          0.1081 / 0.1561 / 0.1121   raw coverage 0.978 / 0.970 / 0.988
  order ≤2 on P (proximity)     0.1374 / 0.1892 / 0.1473
  order ≤2 on all of K          0.1583 / 0.2061 / 0.1587
  blanket over the whole class  0.1844 / 0.2309 / 0.1682
L against the same-order all-claims hedge: −31.7% / −24.3% / −29.4%. Against the blanket: −41.4% / −32.4% / −33.4%. Against the proximity set alone: −21.3% / −17.5% / −23.9%, at a coverage cost of 0.5 to 1.75 points.

THE TWO HONEST COUNTERWEIGHTS, BOTH PRINTED IN THE SAME TABLE.
(1) At ORDER 1 the selection is a measured no-op, exactly as the audit found: hedging over L and over all of K give the identical interval on 300/300 problems and identical calibrated widths (0.1123 / 0.1566 / 0.3678 at per-claim error 0.20 / 0.35 / 0.50). The selective saving is quadratic in origin — it lives in which PAIRS get revised — and the paper must say so rather than sell an order-1 saving that does not exist.
(2) L is nearly a subset of the proximity set: the order-2 hedge on L∪P differs from the hedge on P alone on 0.0% (error 0.35) and 0.4% (error 0.50) of problems. So the measured locality law is doing much of the work, and what L adds on top of it is the 17–24% further narrowing obtained by dropping the hop-0 claims that are not load-bearing. Both rows belong in the table.

REGIME. In the exact-estimand setting the elicited point estimate covers 0.952 / 0.916 / 0.828 at per-claim error 0.20 / 0.35 / 0.50, so at 95% nominal the whole width question only bites once the expert errs enough that Z is invalid in the true DAG more than 5% of the time (measured 4.8% / 8.4% / 17.2%). Report the width table by regime rather than at one error rate, and state the crossover instead of hiding it: below it the point estimate needs no width at all.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Preregistered on the full sweep (the 2,087-problem draw, plus a fresh draw with |K| ≥ 4 and 7 nodes). Each is falsifiable by a number the existing harness already prints.

P1 — NON-DEGENERATE INSIDE THE COLLAPSED STRATUM. Restricted to problems with r_val = 1, |L| takes at least 4 distinct values and no single value holds more than 80% of the mass. Pilot: 4 values {1:152, 2:29, 3:10, 4:12}, max cell 74.9%, n = 203. FALSIFIED if the max cell exceeds 80%, or if {|L| = 0} ∪ {|L| = |K|} carries more than 90% overall.

P2 — THE INDICATOR DOES NOT ESCAPE r_val, AND WE PREDICT THAT. (|L| ≥ 1) ⟺ (r_val = 1) on at least 95% of problems. Pilot: 299/300 = 99.7%. This prediction is written to be confirmed, not dodged: the contribution is the conditional distribution of damage given r_val = 1, not a new indicator. FALSIFIED if agreement falls below 95%, which would mean the flag is finding breakers the ball does not contain, and would force a re-examination of the covering relation rather than of L.

P3 — THE MASS AT ZERO MOVES WITH THE EXPERT, NOT WITH n. P(|L| = 0) stays inside [20%, 50%] and decreases monotonically as the per-claim error rate rises through 0.20, 0.35, 0.50. Pilot: 40.8% → 32.4% → 28.8% (n = 250 each). FALSIFIED by non-monotonicity of more than 3 points, or by leaving the band — either would mean |L| is tracking graph shape rather than elicitation quality.

P4 — PADDING MOVES IT UPWARD OR NOT AT ALL. Appending claims that G0 already entails changes |L| on fewer than 15% of problems, and the "fewer flags" direction stays below 3%. Pilot: changed on 10.2%; up 14 / down 3 at error 0.20 and up 48 / down 1 at 0.50; φ₁ on the same draws changed on 54.1% and shrank on balance. FALSIFIED if the down direction ever exceeds the up direction, which would make |L| gameable in the dangerous direction and would retire the scalar entirely in favour of the set.

P5 — THE RETRIEVAL FRAME FAILS AND THE PAPER SAYS SO FIRST. Precision of L against the claims the expert actually reversed stays below 0.30 at a base rate near 0.13. Pilot: precision 0.190, recall 0.462, base 0.134. FALSIFIED if precision exceeds 0.30, in which case direction (4)'s scoring becomes admissible and the flag may be presented as a detector. Until then it may not be.

P6 — THE WIDTH ORDERING IS THE REAL BET. On a fresh draw in the regime where Z is invalid in the true DAG on more than 5% of problems, the order-≤2 hedge on L attains honest 95% coverage with mean width at least 15% below the same-order all-claims hedge, with uncoverable mass below 5%. Pilot: −31.7% / −24.3% / −29.4% at uncoverable 2.00% / 2.25% / 0.75%. FALSIFIED if the saving drops below 15%, or if the uncoverable mass reaches 5% and the method stops being calibratable — the latter is the sharpest failure available and it is one line of the harness away.
refined.cost:
FLAG. At most 2|K| calls to apply_orientations and at most 2|K| calls to is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag, plus |K| extra apply_orientations calls for the two residual labels. No enumerate_space, no covering_pairs, no bfs_distances: the flag never builds the model-inclusion space, which removes the 3^|und| MPDAG enumeration.

HEDGE. Adds at most 4·C(|L|,2) further graphs, and one enumerate_dag_extensions per graph. |L| is small in practice (mean 0.96 to 1.40 across the error regimes measured, against |K| mean 2.9), so the quadratic term is the reason the selective saving exists at all rather than a cost concern.

THE EXPONENTIAL THAT REMAINS, STATED PLAINLY. is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag still calls enumerate_dag_extensions, and it calls it on retraction graphs, which are coarser than G0 and therefore carry the largest undirected components. One of the two exponentials is removed, not both. The correct sentence is "the cheapest of the six by a large constant", never "the only one that scales past exhaustive enumeration". Measured on 7-node problems with 4 to 6 undirected edges: 13.3 DAG extensions against 242.6 for enumerate_space, 0.8 ms against 13.1 ms, a 17× constant.

WALL CLOCK, THIS MACHINE. 300 amenable problems with the flag, the full r_val ball for the cross-tab, the completeness regression, the padding attack and a five-method width table: 3.9 s (final_inv2_L.py). Three error regimes at n = 250: 9.5 s. Three seeds at n = 400 with order-2 hedges: 10.4 s. CPU only, no solver, nothing near the minutes budget.

refined.name: Fractional-budget hedging profile w(t), with the fractional breakdown boundary t_val (r_val = floor(t_val) + 1)
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING. CPDAG Chat (true equivalence class in every run), elicited orientation claims K, G0 = Meek closure of Chat + K, analyst's adjustment set Z = O*(G0). Space G_Chat with the covering relation and BFS hop distance d(G0, .); shells S_r of MPDAGs at distance r; eccentricity R. For a DAG e in the class, hop(e) := min{ d(G0, G) : e in [G] } (a DAG enters at the first hop that reaches it). Let D_r := {e : hop(e) <= r}; D_R is the whole class.

ESTIMAND (the audit's fix, non-negotiable). tau(e) := 0 if y is not in De_e(x), else beta_{yx.O*(e)}(P). This is the IDA total-effect convention. The repository violates it silently: optimal_adjustment_set_dag returns the empty set both when no adjustment is needed and when y is not a descendant of x, and adjusted_estimand then returns the raw confounded regression. Witness scratchpad/sk_tau_bug.py: truth x <- c -> y with x -> y, rival DAG y -> x, pipeline reports tau = -1.2482 where the total effect is exactly 0. On average 19.8 per cent of class DAGs per problem are mis-priced this way, at least one on 40.7 per cent of problems (reproduced here).

Let tau_0 := beta_{yx.Z}(P) be the analyst's own estimand. Inside each shell order the DAGs NEAREST-FIRST by the deterministic key kappa(e) := (hop(e), |tau(e) - tau_0|, e.edge_string()).

FRACTIONAL BUDGET. For real t in [0, R] write r = floor(t), f = t - r, and define
  D(t) := D_r  union  {the first ceil(f * |S^D_{r+1}|) DAGs of shell r+1 in kappa order},
where S^D_{s} := {e : hop(e) = s}. So D(t) = D_r exactly at integer t, and between integers it admits a deterministic, ranked prefix of the next shell: this is proposal (2) ("do not require that NO element breaks") applied to the SET being unioned, not to the definition of the radius.

REPORTED OBJECTS. Psi(t) := {tau(e) : e in D(t)}; the hedging width w(t) := max Psi(t) - min Psi(t), in effect units, is the primary reported quantity and the curve t -> w(t) is the definition. rho(t) := w(t)/w(R) is a derived figure only, never the headline: it is uncorrelated with scale (audit: spearman(rho(1), w(R)) = +0.017, p = 0.84) and dropping it also removes the only reason to enumerate the whole space.

FRACTIONAL BREAKDOWN BOUNDARY. Order the whole class by kappa into a sequence e_1, e_2, ...; let m := the index of the first e_i with |tau(e_i) - tau_0| > TOL (m := N if none). Let s be the shell containing index m and c the count of DAGs in shells strictly below s; then
  t_val := (s - 1) + (m - c)/|S^D_s|   (0 if m falls in shell 0),
i.e. t_val = inf{t : w(t) > 0}. LEMMA, one direction only, proved: if Z is a valid adjustment set in every e in D(t), then every such e is consistent with the same P, so tau(e) = beta_{yx.Z} = tau_0 for all of them, Psi(t) is a singleton and w(t) = 0. Hence w(t) = 0 for every t <= r_val - 1, so t_val >= r_val - 1. The converse is NOT proved; it needs the SEM parameters to be generic (an invalid Z can coincide with the truth on a null set). It is reported as a measured identity: floor(t_val) + 1 = r_val on 6200 of 6200 (problem, stratum, SEM) rows. The old radius is therefore not deleted and not renamed: it is recovered exactly as the integer part of a finer quantity, and the 68.9 per cent finding (81.6 per cent here) is reported unchanged as the statement that on most problems the FREE hedge does not survive a whole hop.

A useful side effect: w(.) and t_val are computed from tau alone and never call an adjustment-set criterion, so the audit's 12 per cent over-firing of the back-door test (79 of 660 pairs) is off the critical path; r_val is recovered from t_val and the two agreed on all 6200 rows.

EXCLUSIONS, COUNTED. A problem is excluded when the class is already point-identified (every DAG agrees on tau for every SEM draw) or when optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, x, y) is None. In the sweep: 120 problems kept from 1228 draws; filters k out of range 527, |K| out of range 128, y not a descendant of x 437, class already point-identified 16.

MEASURED, ON A GENERATOR WHERE K IS FALSE BY CONSTRUCTION (120 problems, 5-7 nodes, 2-5 undirected edges, j in {0,1,2} reversed elicited claims, 20 SEM draws each, corrected estimand; scratchpad/final_profile.py + final_report2.py, 8.3 s):
  r_val: 4 distinct values, P(r_val = 1) = 0.8161.
  t_val: 14 distinct values, mean 0.5188, median 0.5000. On the degenerate r_val = 1 stratum (n = 5060): 5 distinct values, mean 0.2892, P(t_val > 0) = 0.5415, and per stratum P(t_val > 0) = 0.924 (j=0), 0.314 (j=1), 0.210 (j=2).
  Paired within problem and SEM, j = 0 vs j = 2: t_val mean 0.667 -> 0.324, P(down) = 0.690, P(up) = 0.169, tie 0.141; the same pairs leave r_val at mean 1.141 -> 1.155 with P(tie) = 0.859. The fractional boundary moves when the elicited knowledge is falsified; the integer radius does not.
refined.pseudocode:
```python
# PYTHONPATH=$HOME/bkrobust/src ; every name below is a verified repo function.
import math, itertools, collections
from bkrobust.demo.meek     import apply_orientations
from bkrobust.demo.space    import (enumerate_space, represented_dags, covering_pairs,
                                    neighbour_graph, bfs_distances, atomic_moves)
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import (optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag, optimal_adjustment_set_dag,
                                    is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag, adjusted_estimand,
                                    asymptotic_variance)
TOL = 1e-9

def tau(P, e, x, y):                       # IDA convention -- the fix
    if y not in e.descendants(x):          # x has no causal path to y in this DAG
        return 0.0
    return adjusted_estimand(P, x, y, frozenset(optimal_adjustment_set_dag(e, x, y)))

def profile(cpdag, K, x, y, P, grid):
    G0 = apply_orientations(cpdag, K)                    # Meek closure; None -> K inconsistent: abstain
    Z  = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, x, y)          # None -> not identified by G0: EXCLUDE and COUNT
    if G0 is None or Z is None: return None
    Z = frozenset(Z)

    space = enumerate_space(cpdag)                       # cost is 3**k; see the cost field
    reps  = represented_dags(space)
    nbrs  = neighbour_graph(space, covering_pairs(space, reps))
    shells_mpdag = bfs_distances(nbrs, G0); R = max(shells_mpdag.values())

    hop = {}                                             # a DAG enters at its FIRST hop
    for G, s in shells_mpdag.items():
        for e in reps[G]:
            k = e.edge_string()
            if k not in hop or s < hop[k][0]: hop[k] = (s, e)

    tau_0 = adjusted_estimand(P, x, y, Z)                # the analyst's own estimand
    S = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for s, e in hop.values(): S[s].append(e)
    for s in S:                                          # NEAREST-FIRST, deterministic tie-break
        S[s].sort(key=lambda e: (abs(tau(P, e, x, y) - tau_0), e.edge_string()))
    N = sum(len(v) for v in S.values())

    def D(t):
        if t >= R: return [e for s in sorted(S) for e in S[s]]
        r, f = int(math.floor(t + TOL)), t - int(math.floor(t + TOL))
        out = [e for s in sorted(S) if s <= r for e in S[s]]
        sh  = S.get(r + 1, [])
        if sh and f > TOL: out += sh[:max(1, math.ceil(f * len(sh) - TOL))]
        return out

    w = {}
    for t in grid:
        v = [tau(P, e, x, y) for e in D(t)]
        w[t] = max(v) - min(v)                           # PRIMARY: effect units, not a ratio

    seq = [e for s in sorted(S) for e in S[s]]           # fractional boundary
    m = next((i for i, e in enumerate(seq) if abs(tau(P, e, x, y) - tau_0) > TOL), N)
    acc, t_val = 0, float(R)
    for s in sorted(S):
        if m < acc + len(S[s]):
            t_val = max(0.0, (s - 1) + (m - acc) / len(S[s])); break
        acc += len(S[s])
    r_val_derived = int(math.floor(t_val)) + 1
    r_val_check = next((r for r in range(1, R + 1)                       # audit only; never on the
                        if any(not is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(G, x, y, Z)  # critical path
                               for G, s in shells_mpdag.items() if s == r)), R + 1)
    assert r_val_derived == r_val_check                  # held 6200/6200; a failure is a genericity flag

    def load_bearing(t):                                 # proposal (4), for free: the ranked list
        keep = {e.edge_string() for e in D(t)}
        out = []
        for G, s in sorted(shells_mpdag.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]):
            if s != math.floor(t) + 1: continue
            for e in reps[G]:
                if e.edge_string() not in keep:
                    out.append((abs(tau(P, e, x, y) - tau_0), atomic_moves(G0, G)))
        return sorted(out, reverse=True)                 # the claims whose revision moves the answer

    return w, t_val, r_val_derived, D, load_bearing
```

refined.guarantee:
THREE STATEMENTS SURVIVE, AND ONE IS DELETED.

G1, exactness at integer budgets. For integer t = r, D(t) is exactly the union of the DAG extensions of the MPDAGs in the ball B_r; nothing is trimmed and the quantifier over the ball is still universal. So if the true DAG lies within r elementary revisions of G0, then tau lies in Psi(r), hence in the reported interval up to sampling. This is the ordinary blanket-IDA guarantee restricted to a ball, and it is a definitional identity rather than a theorem; it is stated as such, and its antecedent is exactly as unverifiable as r_val's was.

G2, zero-cost certificate, proved one direction. If Z is valid in every DAG of D(t) then all those DAGs are consistent with the same P, so tau(e) = beta_{yx.Z} for each and w(t) = 0. Consequently w(t) = 0 for all t <= r_val - 1, and hedging out to r_val - 1 costs nothing. The converse (that the region acquires width exactly at r_val) is NOT proved and must not be asserted: it requires the SEM parameters to be generic. It is reported as a measurement, floor(t_val) + 1 = r_val on 6200 of 6200 rows, together with the fact that the earlier draft's own evidence, P(rho(1) = 0 | r_val = 1) = 0.153, was an artefact of the estimand bug and is 0.000 after the fix.

G3, sandwich at fractional budgets, with an auditable assumption. D(floor t) is contained in D(t), which is contained in D(ceil t), so the intervals nest and w is non-decreasing in t (verified monotone on all 6200 x 61 grid evaluations). At fractional t the guarantee is explicitly conditional: coverage holds if the true DAG belongs to D(t). What makes that honest rather than hidden is that the complement is printed. `load_bearing(t)` returns every excluded DAG of shell ceil(t) with the exact orientation claims it revises, ranked by how far it moves the answer, so the reader sees the finite list of worlds being assumed away. The ordering key uses estimated quantities, so the trimmed set is data-dependent; at integer t the ordering is irrelevant and G1 is ordering-free.

DELETED. "Full soundness, unweakened" cannot be claimed alongside the target metric's calibrate-by-scaling protocol, and it is not claimed here. Measured on this benchmark, the ball intervals overcover at r >= 2 (0.9937) and undercover at r = 1 (0.9021), so scaling to 95 per cent either shrinks a sound region until it is no longer sound or inflates an identification region by a factor with no soundness meaning. The resolution is to calibrate the budget t, which is a set, and never to scale the interval: G1 and G3 then describe precisely the object that is reported. Also not claimed: robustness under an estimated CPDAG (every run uses the true equivalence class), any continuity bound (the relative move is heavy-tailed, max 205.5 times |tau_0| here), and any per-graph averaging of damage.
refined.width_rule:
THE INTERVAL. At budget t report
  CI(t) = [ min_{e in D(t)} (tauhat(e) - z * sehat(e)) , max_{e in D(t)} (tauhat(e) + z * sehat(e)) ],
with tauhat(e) the sample adjusted coefficient on x from regressing y on {x} + O*(e), forced to 0 when y is not a descendant of x in e, sehat(e)^2 = asymptotic_variance(P, x, y, O*(e))/n, and z = 1.96 fixed. The identification part is max Psi(t) - min Psi(t) and the sampling part is the usual OLS term; where damage is absent D(t) is a tau-singleton, the identification part is exactly zero, and the method collapses to the ordinary interval on the elicited set.

CALIBRATION, ONE DIAL, NO SCALING. Split the benchmark. On the calibration half choose t* = the smallest grid value whose empirical coverage reaches 0.95, holding z fixed; report the mean width of CI(t*) on the held-out half. Competitors (DoubleML on the elicited set, TabPFN, CausalPFN, Do-PFN, enumeration of total effects, blanket hedge) get their one scale multiplier fitted on the same calibration half, so the comparison is one free parameter against one. The primary table is the uncalibrated coverage-width curve; the single calibrated width is secondary, because the guarantee and the metric must not be claimed of the same interval.

THE MIXTURE IS AN ASSUMPTION AND IS DECLARED. Choosing a point on the curve requires a distribution over how many elicited claims are false. That constant belongs in the paper as a stated assumption, with the table given per stratum, never fitted silently. Measured (120 problems, 20 SEM draws, j reversed claims, identification width only, calibration in-sample so these are optimistic):

  uniform over j in {0,1,2}: ball r=0 coverage 0.5764 width 0.0530; r=1 0.9021 / 0.6440; r=2 0.9937 / 0.8913; blanket 1.0000 / 0.9443.
    t* = 1.05 (grid 0.05; 1.02 on a 0.02 grid), coverage 0.9836, width 0.7688 -- 18.6 per cent below the blanket and 13.7 per cent below the integer fallback ceil(t*) = 2. Read plainly: the whole one-hop ball plus the single least-damaging DAG of shell 2.
  expert mostly right, P(j) = (.5,.35,.15): t* = 0.70, coverage 0.9531, width 0.6520 -- 30.2 per cent below the blanket, but only 2.2 per cent below the integer r = 1.
  worst stratum, j = 2 only: t* = 1.05, coverage 0.9507, width 0.8011 -- 18.6 per cent below the blanket.

This is the number the audit's third hidden problem was about, and it is now the fix rather than the defect: the integer dial forced r = 2 for a 6.3 per cent saving; the fractional dial reaches 95 per cent between the hops and roughly triples that. Two honest riders. First, the dial's resolution is 1/|S_{r+1}| and the shells are small: mean 2.17 DAGs at hop 1 for k <= 5, still only 4.0 at k = 10 (final_scale.py), so this is a handful of extra steps, not a continuum. Second, the alternative that would be a continuum, interpolating the hull endpoints between consecutive nested sets, was built and measured and is NOT better: width 0.7548 against 0.7688 on the uniform mixture and 0.6664 against 0.6520 on the mostly-right mixture, i.e. inside the noise, while it destroys the "hull of an explicit DAG set" semantics that G1 and G3 rest on. It is rejected on that measurement, not on taste.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Pre-register these four on the full sweep (target n >= 2000 problems, strata j in {0,1,2} declared in advance, corrected IDA estimand, true equivalence class, calibration on a held-out split). Any one failing kills the corresponding piece.

P1, the summary is not the old atom. On the stratum where the integer radius is degenerate (r_val = 1; 68.9 per cent in the original sweep, 81.6 per cent here), t_val takes at least 4 distinct values, and P(t_val > 0 | r_val = 1) >= 0.35 pooled, with >= 0.15 within each false-knowledge stratum j >= 1. Measured here: 5 distinct values, pooled 0.5415, and 0.924 / 0.314 / 0.210 for j = 0 / 1 / 2. FAILS IF pooled P(t_val = 0 | r_val = 1) > 0.65, in which case t_val is r_val with decimals attached and clause (a) is unmet.

P2, the boundary is exactly the old radius, and no more. floor(t_val) + 1 = r_val on every row. Measured 6200/6200. A single violation is either a genericity failure of the SEM draw or a bug, and must be chased rather than averaged away; it is also the standing check that the incomplete back-door criterion is not over-firing (79 of 660 pairs in the audit's harness, zero effect here).

P3, the fractional part carries the signal the integer part cannot. Paired within problem and SEM, moving from j = 0 to j = 2 reversed claims lowers t_val at least twice as often as it raises it, while r_val is unchanged on at least three quarters of the same pairs. Measured: P(down)/P(up) = 0.690/0.169 = 4.08, r_val tie 0.859. FAILS IF the ratio drops below 2 or r_val moves as much as t_val, in which case the new object is a reparametrisation and should be reported as such.

P4, the paper's actual bet, and the one most likely to fail. At the calibrated t*, held-out mean width is at most 0.85 times the blanket width under the declared mixture. Measured in-sample 0.814 (0.7688 against 0.9443) on the uniform mixture, 0.698 on the mostly-right mixture, 0.814 on j = 2 alone. FAILS IF the held-out ratio exceeds 0.90, and it may: the calibration here is in-sample, the saving comes from the shell-2 prefix whose size is 1 DAG in most problems, and the audit's own compute finding runs the other way (k = 10 costs 3.1 s to enumerate the space and 7.1 s for covering_pairs plus neighbour_graph, against a semi-local polynomial blanket IDA). If P4 fails, the honest retreat is written in advance: report the blanket interval as the interval, and sell the ranked load-bearing list (proposal 4) as the contribution, since it is produced by the same computation and needs no coverage claim.

One structural caution that no threshold covers. Locality is real but leaky, so the trimming order must stay tau-based and not become a graph-distance heuristic: measured on 15480 one-hop revisions, a revision touching x or y moves the estimand 73.7 per cent of the time and one touching neither still moves it 27.3 per cent of the time (precision 0.737, recall 0.848 for "touches the query" as a detector). A structural rule would silently drop a quarter of the load-bearing revisions.

All measured on this machine (Python 3.12, numpy/scipy present, CPU only, no SAT solver anywhere in the pipeline).

Main sweep, 120 problems x 3 knowledge strata x 20 SEM draws = 6200 rows, each row a full space enumeration, covering relation, BFS, nearest-first ordering and a 61-point budget grid: 8.3 s wall (final_profile.py). The endpoint-interpolated variant on the same design: 9.2 s (final_interp.py). Analysis is instantaneous from the saved .npz. The audit's own scripts reproduce in 5.68 s (sk_rho_fixed.py) and comparable for sk_cover.py.

Scaling in k, the undirected-edge count, is the binding constraint and it is dominated by the space, not by the estimand (final_scale.py, mean over 2-5 draws per k):
  k = 5 : 53 MPDAGs, 10.4 DAGs, enumerate_space 0.022 s, represented_dags 0.007 s, covering_pairs + neighbour_graph 0.006 s
  k = 8 : 203 MPDAGs, 20.4 DAGs, 0.398 s / 0.077 s / 0.307 s
  k = 10: 726 MPDAGs, 37.5 DAGs, 3.123 s / 0.597 s / 7.117 s
covering_pairs + neighbour_graph is quadratic in |space| and overtakes enumeration around k = 9. Two mitigations, both already in the definition. First, w(t) needs only shells 0..ceil(t)+1, so the neighbour graph can be built lazily to that depth instead of over the whole space; the only thing that ever needed the full class was w(R), the normaliser of rho, and rho is demoted precisely because it buys nothing measurable. Second, restrict the ball rather than the space when k > 10. Without those, k around 10 is the practical ceiling, which excludes most real CPDAGs and is the honest scope statement for the experiments section.

Per-problem storage is negligible (the 6200-row grid archive is 1.2 MB compressed).

refined.name: S(K) — the certified load-bearing support: cascade-footprint hitting screen H with a joint retraction certificate (ℓ demoted to enumeration order)
refined.formal_definition:
SETUP. Ĉ a CPDAG, K a set of elicited orientation claims consistent with Ĉ, G₀ := cl(Ĉ, K) the Meek closure, Z := O*(G₀) the reported adjustment set, (x, y) the query. For J ⊆ K write G_{−J} := cl(Ĉ, K \ J).

CASCADE FOOTPRINT. C(k) := directed_edges(G₀) \ directed_edges(G_{−{k}}). These are the orientations for which k is jointly responsible: the claim itself plus every edge Meek compels on its behalf and that no other claim re-derives. C(k) = ∅ means k is redundant given the rest of K.

ANCHOR. A := {x, y} ∪ Z.

SCREEN. H(k) := 1 iff some edge (u, v) ∈ C(k) has u ∈ A or v ∈ A. (Indicator, not a distance. This is the object the repository already declares as hits_optimal_set at src/bkrobust/knowledge/cascade.py:108; ℓ is the object it declares as cascade_reach at line 99, and ℓ is not used as a screen anywhere below.)

PARTITION. S₀ := {k : H(k) = 1}, K₀ := K \ S₀.

JOINT RETRACTION CERTIFICATE. G⊥ := cl(Ĉ, S₀), i.e. every screened-out claim retracted at once. Cert := is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(G⊥, x, y, Z).

CERTIFIED SUPPORT.
  S(K) := S₀                                              if Cert holds;
  S(K) := S₀ ∪ {k ∈ K₀ : Z invalid in G_{−{k}}}            otherwise (per-claim fallback).
A claim outside S(K) is certified inert: retracting it changes no adjusted estimand.

REPORTED OBJECT (this is what replaces r_val). Not a radius. The pair
  (S(K), Hull_t) with Hull_t := [ min, max ] of β(O*(D)) over D ∈ ⋃_{J ⊆ S(K), |J| ≤ t} ext(cl(Ĉ, S(K) \ J)) ∪ ext(G₀),
where β(·) is the adjusted estimand and t ∈ {1, 2, …} is the analyst-facing dial "how many elicited claims may be wrong". |S(K)| is the integer diagnostic (which claims are load-bearing, direction 4); Hull_t is the interval (direction 1). ℓ(k) = min over the endpoints of k of the skeleton BFS distance to {x, y} survives only as the sort key that orders S(K) for anytime enumeration and as the connected-component test that discards claims in a skeleton component disjoint from A. It has no symbol in the paper and no role in the guarantee.

WHY THE PARTITION IS THE RIGHT ONE. If Z is valid in a DAG D then O*(D) is also valid in D, so β(Z) = β(O*(D)): every extension in which Z survives contributes exactly the point estimate and cannot widen the hull. The hull is therefore supported entirely on the claims whose retraction can invalidate Z, which is what S(K) isolates.

from itertools import combinations
from math import sqrt
from bkrobust.demo.example import dag_to_cpdag, knowledge_to_recover
from bkrobust.demo.meek import apply_orientations, enumerate_dag_extensions
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import (optimal_adjustment_set_dag, optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag,
                                    is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag, adjusted_estimand,
                                    asymptotic_variance)

# ---------- tier 0: cascade footprints, |K| Meek closures, no DAG enumeration ----------
def footprints(cpdag, K, G0):
    fib, C = {}, {}
    for k in sorted(K):
        Gk = apply_orientations(cpdag, set(K) - {k})      # cl(Chat, K \ {k}); None on FAIL
        fib[k] = Gk
        C[k] = None if Gk is None else set(G0.directed_edges) - set(Gk.directed_edges)
    return fib, C

# ---------- the screen, the certificate, the certified support ----------
def certified_support(cpdag, K, x, y):
    G0 = apply_orientations(cpdag, K)
    assert G0 is not None, "elicited knowledge is inconsistent with Chat"
    Z = (optimal_adjustment_set_dag(G0, x, y) if G0.is_dag()
         else optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, x, y))
    assert Z is not None, "O* not identified by G0; report non-identification, not an interval"
    A = {x, y} | set(Z)
    fib, C = footprints(cpdag, K, G0)

    S = [k for k in sorted(K)
         if C[k] is None or any(u in A or v in A for (u, v) in C[k])]   # FAIL -> audit it
    K0 = [k for k in sorted(K) if k not in S]

    Gperp = apply_orientations(cpdag, set(S))                # retract all of K0 at once
    cert = Gperp is not None and is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(Gperp, x, y, Z)
    if not cert:                                             # conservative fallback; never truncate
        for k in list(K0):
            if fib[k] is None or not is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(fib[k], x, y, Z):
                K0.remove(k); S.append(k)
    return Z, sorted(S), K0, fib, cert

# ---------- the hull ----------
def skeleton_bfs(g, sources):                    # ell, used only to order S
    adj = {v: set() for v in g.nodes}
    for a, b in g.skeleton(): adj[a].add(b); adj[b].add(a)
    d, q = {s: 0 for s in sources}, list(sources)
    while q:
        v = q.pop(0)
        for w in adj[v]:
            if w not in d: d[w] = d[v] + 1; q.append(w)
    return d

def hull(cpdag, K, x, y, Z, S, fib, t=1, budget=None):
    beta = None                                   # filled by the caller's estimator; see width_rule
    graphs = ([fib[k] for k in S] if t == 1 else
              [apply_orientations(cpdag, set(S) - set(J))
               for r in range(t + 1) for J in combinations(S, r)])
    lo, hi, spent = +float("inf"), -float("inf"), 0
    for g in graphs:
        if g is None: continue
        exts = enumerate_dag_extensions(g)
        spent += len(exts)
        if budget is not None and spent > budget:
            return None                           # REFUSE: caller falls back to the whole class
        for D in exts:
            b = adjusted_estimand(SEM, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y))
            lo, hi = min(lo, b), max(hi, b)
    return (lo, hi) if lo <= hi else None          # None here means S is empty -> hull collapses

# ---------- one problem, end to end ----------
def audit(cpdag, K, x, y, SEM, n, t=1, c=1.0, budget=None):
    Z, S, K0, fib, cert = certified_support(cpdag, K, x, y)
    S.sort(key=lambda k: min(skeleton_bfs(cpdag, [x, y]).get(v, 10**6) for v in k))  # ell order
    beta = adjusted_estimand(SEM, x, y, Z)
    s = 1.96 * sqrt(asymptotic_variance(SEM, x, y, Z) / n)
    h = hull(cpdag, K, x, y, Z, S, fib, t=t, budget=budget) if S else None
    if h is None and S and budget is not None:
        return whole_class_hedge(cpdag, x, y, SEM, n, c)     # explicit refusal path
    lo = min(h[0], beta - s) if h else beta - s
    hi = max(h[1], beta + s) if h else beta + s
    return (beta - c * (beta - lo), beta + c * (hi - beta)), S, cert
refined.guarantee:
EXACTNESS AT t = 1, CERTIFIED AT RUNTIME (not assumed, not asymptotic).

Lemma (monotonicity). For J ⊆ K₀ we have K \ J ⊇ K \ K₀ = S₀, so cl(Ĉ, K \ J) is at least as oriented as G⊥ = cl(Ĉ, S₀), hence ext(cl(Ĉ, K \ J)) ⊆ ext(G⊥).

Theorem. If Cert holds then for every k ∈ K₀, Z is a valid adjustment set in every DAG extension of G_{−{k}}; therefore β(O*(D)) = β(Z) on that whole fibre and k contributes nothing to the hull. Consequently Hull₁ computed over S(K) alone equals Hull₁ computed over all of K. The reported interval is the exact one-retraction hull, not a lower bound on it.

Corollary (what makes this different from the audited version). The screen is not trusted. When Cert fails the procedure pays |K₀| extra fibre checks and recovers the exact support anyway, so the output is exact on every problem in every regime; the certificate governs compute, never coverage. There is no "anytime lower bound", no patience constant, and no interval that knowingly under-covers.

SOUNDNESS AT t ≥ 2 (over-approximation, still enumerating only over S). For any J ⊆ K with J ∩ S = J_S we have K \ J ⊇ S \ J_S, hence ext(cl(Ĉ, K \ J)) ⊆ ext(cl(Ĉ, S \ J_S)). So the hull over {cl(Ĉ, S \ J_S) : J_S ⊆ S, |J_S| ≤ t} contains the true t-retraction hull. It over-covers, never under-covers. Verified on 150/150 problems (sweep_t2.py, seed 20260914) and tight on 144/150.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No general theorem that H is lossless. The blocking half of the back-door criterion can in principle break through an interior edge of C(k) touching neither x, y nor Z (a flipped edge on a directed route into Z re-opens a collider), and no locality bound is offered to exclude it — such a bound is exactly the continuity-style argument the constraint list forbids. That gap is closed per instance by Cert, not by proof. Measured: 0 misses on 925 load-bearing claims over 1,400 problems (sweep_h.py seeds 20260907/8/9, sweep_h2.py seeds 20260910/11), and the only provable-in-general sub-case is the trivial one, that a claim in a skeleton component disjoint from {x, y} ∪ Z is inert.

NOT CLAIMED, EXPLICITLY. Nothing here holds under an estimated CPDAG; every run uses the true equivalence class. No continuity statement relates footprint size to bias. Nothing is averaged across the queries of one graph: one query is drawn per graph.
refined.width_rule:
Per problem, with n the sample size and z = 1.96:

1. Point estimate β̂ = adjusted_estimand on the elicited Z; statistical half-width s = z · sqrt(asymptotic_variance(SEM, x, y, Z) / n).
2. Structural hull [L, U] = Hull_t over the certified support; if S(K) = ∅ set L = U = β̂.
3. Raw interval I_raw = [min(L, β̂ − s), max(U, β̂ + s)].
4. One global scalar c, fitted on a calibration split, applied about the point estimate:
   I(c) = [β̂ − c·(β̂ − I_raw.lo), β̂ + c·(I_raw.hi − β̂)], c the smallest value giving ≥ 0.95 empirical coverage of the true total effect over the calibration problems.
5. Table entry = mean over test problems of c · (I_raw.hi − I_raw.lo). Every competitor row is calibrated by the same one-scalar rule.

Three properties this rule has and the audited version did not:

(a) Zero structural width where damage is absent. If S(K) = ∅ the hull collapses and I_raw is exactly the statistical interval, so our row equals the oracle-adjustment row up to c. Measured: the hull is a single point on 390/390 undamaged problems across sweep_h2 and sweep_cost. Requirement (c) is met exactly, not approximately.

(b) c is driven by statistical error alone, not by un-hedged structural error. Because the support is certified rather than screened, no load-bearing claim is left out, so the calibration constant does not have to absorb the 128× damage tail on problems the screen missed. This is the entire width argument: an uncertified filter that misses 12–18 per cent of load-bearing claims (measured for ℓ ≤ 0 below) inflates c on every problem, including the undamaged ones.

(c) Refusal instead of truncation. If the enumeration budget is exhausted the method returns the whole-class hedge, never a truncated hull. A knowingly under-covering interval is not cheap under this metric; it is priced at the calibration step.

Measured raw widths, t = 1, saturated elicitation, ours vs the whole-class hedge: mean 0.593 and median 0.846 at n = 8–10 (131 problems with non-zero blanket width), mean 0.545 and median 0.631 at n = 12–16 (95); on damaged problems only, 0.700 and 0.691; replicated at 0.628 and 0.546 in the independent cost sweep. Ours equalled the exact one-retraction hull on 930/930 problems where both were computed.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
The failure mode to test for is r_val's, transposed: mass piling on one value. Three pre-registered predictions, each with the number that kills it, all runnable on this machine in minutes.

P1 — SUPPORT SIZE IS NOT CONCENTRATED. Over ≥ 500 problems, saturated elicitation, n ∈ [8, 22], one query per graph: the fraction with |S(K)| = |K| stays below 0.05, and the fraction with |S(K)| = 0 lies in (0.20, 0.55). Measured in-session: 0.020 and 0.010 for the first (sweep_h2), and 108/300 = 0.360 and 86/200 = 0.430 for the second. FALSIFIED if |S(K)| = |K| on more than 5 per cent of problems, which would mean the object has inherited the collapse it exists to fix, or if |S(K)| = 0 on more than 55 per cent, which would mean it never fires.

P2 — THE OBJECT IS DEGENERATE IN THE MINIMAL-ELICITATION REGIME, AND THAT IS THE HONEST HEADLINE RISK. With K = a minimal recovery set (mean |K| = 2.2 to 2.7), the one-retraction hull already equals the whole-class hull: measured median ours/blanket = 1.000 across all three n-bands (sweep_h, 900 problems). The prediction is directional and falsifiable: the width ratio must fall monotonically as elicitation saturates, reaching ≤ 0.70 in mean by mean |K| ≈ 5 (measured 0.545–0.628) and continuing to fall at mean |K| ≥ 8. FALSIFIED if the mean ratio at mean |K| ≥ 8 exceeds 0.85. The paper must therefore report elicitation size as an experimental axis; a table run only on knowledge_to_recover outputs would show the method tying the blanket hedge and would be reporting the generator, not the method.

P3 — THE ADVANTAGE IS A t = 1 PHENOMENON AND DIES AT t = 2. Measured at t = 2 with mean |K| = 5.00: the S-only hull is sound on 150/150 and tight on 144/150, but its width ratio to the whole-class hedge is mean 1.000 and median 1.000. Prediction: at t = 2 the ratio stays above 0.90 for mean |K| ≤ 6 and drops below 0.80 only once mean |K| ≥ 10. FALSIFIED if t = 2 already beats the blanket at mean |K| ≤ 6, which would be good news and would mean the mechanism is not the one described here.

P4 — THE CERTIFICATE FIRES OFTEN ENOUGH TO BE WORTH HAVING, AND IS CONSERVATIVE WHEN IT DOES NOT. Pass rate ≥ 0.85 at n ≤ 22 (measured 0.890, 0.900, 0.904, 0.917 saturated; 0.998, 0.997, 1.000 minimal), and every failure is a false alarm rather than a real miss (measured: on all 53 failures the per-claim fallback found zero additional load-bearing claims). FALSIFIED if the pass rate falls below 0.60 as n grows, in which case the certificate is always paid and never collected and the screen should be dropped for the plain per-claim exact test.

P5 — THE ORDERING BASELINE, SINCE THE AUDIT ASKED FOR IT. H must dominate the one-bit locality indicator 1[ℓ(k) = 0] on both axes at once. Measured: H missed 0 of 925 load-bearing claims, while ℓ ≤ 0 missed 15/288 = 5.2 per cent, 29/187 = 15.5 per cent and 18/102 = 17.7 per cent in the minimal regime, a miss rate that grows with n rather than shrinking. FALSIFIED if any sweep produces an H miss on a problem whose certificate passed, which would refute the monotonicity lemma and is a unit test rather than an experiment.
refined.cost:
Tier 0 (footprints and the screen): |K| Meek closures plus |K| set differences, no DAG enumeration. Milliseconds; the whole 1,400-problem screen sweep ran in 2.8 s of wall clock at n up to 22.

Tier 1 (certificate): one call to enumerate_dag_extensions on G⊥, which has more undirected edges than any single retraction graph and is therefore the single most expensive fibre in the procedure, bounded above by the whole equivalence class.

Tier 2 (hull): |S(K)| fibre enumerations at t = 1; C(|S|, ≤ t) at higher t, enumerating only over S.

THE COST CLAIM THE ORIGINAL DEFINITION MADE IS REFUTED BY MY OWN MEASUREMENT, and this must be stated rather than buried. Counting DAG extensions actually enumerated, screened versus naive per-claim exact checking: 7.9 vs 8.2 at n = 8–10 (ratio 0.965) and 9.5 vs 8.8 at n = 12–16 (ratio 1.079). The screen saves nothing at these sizes and can cost more, because the certificate's fibre is larger than the per-claim fibres it replaces. Mean |S| was 1.89 and 2.04 against mean |K| of 5.17 and 5.54, so the screen does discard about two thirds of the claims — the saving is simply not where the compute is. The blanket hedge cost 13.7 and 16.3 extensions on the same problems, so the whole procedure remains cheaper than the baseline it is trying to beat on width.

The surviving cost argument is therefore narrow and should be written narrowly: the screen bounds the number of fibres that must be enumerated by |S| + 1 rather than |K|, which matters only when individual fibres are large and |K| is large. No claim is made that this tier survives a graph too large for enumerate_dag_extensions — on such a graph the whole-class hedge and the enumeration-of-total-effects rows of the target table are equally uncomputable, so the metric has no reference there and the scaling story cannot be told at all. Note also that is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag is implemented in this repository by enumerating extensions; a polynomial generalised-adjustment check would make the certificate cheap and would change this paragraph, and that is the implementation to write before claiming any scaling.

refined.name: MDS/CORE — marginal displacement spectrum and the certified inert set (effect-scale direction 4, revised; supersedes SEL_A, id effect-scale-4)
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING. Ĉ is the true CPDAG, K = (k_1,…,k_m) the elicited orientations, consistent in the sense that G_0 := meek_closure(apply_orientations(Ĉ, K)) ≠ None. The analyst's point answer exists only when Z_0 := optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G_0, x, y) ≠ None; θ_0 := adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, Z_0). States where Z_0 is None are a separate fate, not a row (measured here: 50 of 723 single-reversal states, 6.9%; Meek-inconsistent states 29 of 723, 4.0%).

RETRACTION LATTICE. For S ⊆ [m] let G_S := meek_closure(apply_orientations(Ĉ, K∖S)), ext(S) := enumerate_dag_extensions(G_S), τ(D) := adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y)), and

    T_S := [ min_{D∈ext(S)} τ(D) , max_{D∈ext(S)} τ(D) ].

Because Z_0 is identified in G_0, every D ∈ ext(∅) has O*(D) = Z_0, so T_∅ = {θ_0} exactly. S ⊆ S' ⟹ ext(S) ⊆ ext(S') ⟹ T_S ⊆ T_{S'} (verified: 0 violations over the complete lattice of 250 problems, sela2_core.py seed 20260907). T_[m] is the blanket hull over the whole equivalence class.

MARGINAL DISPLACEMENT (the object that replaces the leave-one-out Δ). With exc(A,B) := max(B.lo − A.lo, A.hi − B.hi, 0) the one-sided excess of the larger hull over the smaller,

    μ_i^(j) := max { exc(T_{S∪{i}}, T_S) : S ⊆ [m]∖{i}, |S| ≤ j−1 },     μ_i := μ_i^(m).

μ_i^(1) = exc(T_{{i}}, T_∅) is exactly the audited Δ_i, so the audited screen is this family's first order and nothing is thrown away. The published diagnostic is the ranked spectrum μ_(1) ≥ … ≥ μ_(m) together with the minimal culpable sets: the minimal S with T_S ≠ T_∅.

CERTIFIED INERT SET AND CORE. N^(j)_δ := { i : μ_i^(j) ≤ δ }, C^(j)_δ := [m] ∖ N^(j)_δ. δ is quoted in units of the analyst's own ŝe = sqrt(asymptotic_variance(sem,x,y,Z_0)/n); the default is δ = 0, at which N is a certificate rather than a threshold decision.

INTERVAL (subordinate to the diagnostic, see the width rule). SEL^(j)_δ := conv ∪ { T_S : S ⊆ C^(j)_δ, |S| ≤ min(j, |C|) }, reported as R := conv(SEL^(j)_δ ∪ {θ_0}).

TWO PARAMETERS, BOTH NAMED — this is the audit's fix (2): j is the screening/hedging order and δ the accepted-deficit budget. j = 1, δ = 0 is the audited SEL_A; j = m, δ = 0 is the unconditional member; there is no unindexed "SEL_A".

WITHDRAWN in this revision, per the audit: the sentence "completeness is checkable here rather than assumed" as it was written (replaced by G1 below, which is the checkable statement that is actually true); the statistic median Δ_max/width(RHIG_1) = 1.00 (arithmetically forced by two-element extension classes, an instrument that measures nothing); the 0.651 selective-to-blanket width ratio; and any claim that the selective interval is narrower than the blanket — it is provably not.
refined.pseudocode:
PYTHONPATH=src, all calls are the verified repo API. Reference implementations that produced every number below:
  scratchpad/sela2_core.py (lattice, monotonicity, inert fraction, representation stability)
  scratchpad/sela2_delta.py (identity theorem, δ-width curve)
  scratchpad/sela2_retr.py (μ spectrum, single-reversal retrieval)
  scratchpad/sela2_head.py (μ vs Δ on identical instances)
  scratchpad/sela2_two.py (two simultaneous false claims)
  scratchpad/sela2_cost.py (cost scaling)

from itertools import combinations
from bkrobust.demo.meek import apply_orientations, meek_closure, enumerate_dag_extensions
from bkrobust.demo.evaluate import (optimal_adjustment_set_dag, optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag,
                                    adjusted_estimand, asymptotic_variance)

def hull(sem, cpdag, keep, x, y, cache):                      # T_S, keyed by the KEPT claims
    key = tuple(sorted(keep))
    if key in cache: return cache[key]
    g = apply_orientations(cpdag, list(keep)) if keep else meek_closure(cpdag)
    if g is None: cache[key] = None; return None              # cannot happen for S ⊆ K
    ext = enumerate_dag_extensions(g, limit=8192)
    if not ext: cache[key] = None; return None
    v = [adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, x, y)) for D in ext]
    cache[key] = (min(v), max(v)); return cache[key]

def lattice(sem, cpdag, K, x, y, order=None):                 # order=None -> full 2^m; else |S| <= order
    m, cache, T = len(K), {}, {}
    top = m if order is None else min(order, m)
    for r in range(top + 1):
        for S in combinations(range(m), r):
            T[frozenset(S)] = hull(sem, cpdag, [K[i] for i in range(m) if i not in S], x, y, cache)
    return T

def exc(A, B):                                                # A ⊇ B by monotonicity
    return None if (A is None or B is None) else max(B[0]-A[0], A[1]-B[1], 0.0)

def mds(T, m, j):                                             # μ_i^(j), the ranked spectrum
    mu = []
    for i in range(m):
        best = 0.0
        for S in T:
            if i in S or len(S) > j-1: continue
            if frozenset(S | {i}) not in T: continue
            e = exc(T[S | {i}], T[S])
            if e is not None and e > best: best = e
        mu.append(best)
    return mu                                                 # rank: sorted(range(m), key=-mu[i])

def screen(cpdag, K, sem, x, y, j=None, delta=0.0, n=1000):
    g0 = apply_orientations(cpdag, K)
    if g0 is None: return {"fate": "meek-inconsistent"}
    z0 = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(g0, x, y)
    if z0 is None: return {"fate": "no-optimal-set"}           # analyst has no point answer
    theta0 = adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, z0)
    se = (max(asymptotic_variance(sem, x, y, z0), 1e-12) / n) ** 0.5
    m = len(K); j = m if j is None else j
    T = lattice(sem, cpdag, K, x, y, order=None if j == m else j)
    mu = mds(T, m, j)
    C = [i for i in range(m) if mu[i] > delta * se]
    N = [i for i in range(m) if i not in C]
    lo, hi = theta0, theta0                                   # SEL^(j)_δ, then ∪ {θ_0}
    for r in range(0, min(j, len(C)) + 1):
        for S in combinations(sorted(C), r):
            h = T.get(frozenset(S))
            if h: lo, hi = min(lo, h[0]), max(hi, h[1])
    blk = T[frozenset(range(m))] if j == m else None           # blanket, for the audit column
    return {"fate": "ok", "theta0": theta0, "se": se, "mu": mu,
            "rank": sorted(range(m), key=lambda i: -mu[i]),
            "core": C, "inert": N,
            "minimal_culpable": [S for r in range(1, len(C)+1)
                                 for S in combinations(sorted(C), r)
                                 if T.get(frozenset(S)) not in (None, (theta0, theta0))
                                 and all(T.get(frozenset(S[:k]+S[k+1:])) in (None,(theta0,theta0))
                                         for k in range(len(S)))],
            "interval": (lo, hi),
            "deficit": (0.0 if blk is None else exc(blk, (lo, hi))),   # accepted bias, δ>0 only
            "half_width": lambda lam, z=1.959963985: lam * (0.5*(hi-lo) + z*se)}

Deployment note: pass j < m for large m. The order-j truncation costs Σ_{i≤j} C(m,i) closures and yields exactly the order-j guarantee (G2); it does NOT license the δ=0 irrelevance certificate G1, which quantifies over the whole lattice.
refined.guarantee:
G1 — EXACT IRRELEVANCE (this is the true statement the audit's deleted sentence was reaching for). If μ_i = 0 then T_{S∪{i}} = T_S for every S ⊆ [m]∖{i}; telescoping, T_F = T_{F∩C_0} for every F. Contrapositive: any claim whose retraction could change the achievable answer at any retraction state has μ_i > 0 and is flagged. Completeness here quantifies over SUBSETS OF THE LATTICE, not over which claims happen to be false, so it is decided by the computation and not assumed — which is exactly why the audited version ("Δ_i is computed exactly from the population functional") was a non-sequitur and this one is not. Consequence for retrieval: the honest ground truth is the CULPABLE claims (those whose retraction moves T_F), not the false ones, and recall against culpable claims is 1 by the theorem. Measured (sela2_retr.py, seed 31337, 250 problems, 723 single reversals, 87 consistent-and-biasing): recall 1.000, top-1 by μ 0.885, core 1.52 of 3.07 claims. Head-to-head on identical instances (sela2_head.py, 91 biasing): μ top-1 0.901 / precision 0.832, Δ top-1 0.923 / precision 0.930, recall 1.000 both. Δ is the sharper screen when exactly one claim is false; μ is the one that stays complete when more are. That trade-off is the index j, measured, not argued.

G2 — IDENTITY WITH THE RETRACTION HULL, AND A GUARANTEE UPGRADE AT EQUAL WIDTH. At δ = 0, SEL^(j)_0 = ∪_{|S|≤j} T_S bit-identically at every order (measured 300/300 problems, sela2_delta.py). Selection is therefore width-neutral by theorem, not by luck: inert claims are redundant elements of a monotone family, so removing them cannot shrink a union. What the core buys at that identical width is (a) enumeration over C(|C|,j) subsets instead of C(m,j), and (b) a strictly larger certified class — the same interval covers τ whenever at most j CORE claims are false and arbitrarily many inert claims are false, in place of "at most j claims are false". At j = |C| the qualifier disappears: SEL^(|C|)_0 = T_[m], unconditionally sound given the true CPDAG. Measured under two simultaneous false claims (sela2_two.py, seed 9091, 125 biasing double reversals): SEL^(m)_0 covers τ 1.000, the Δ-active hull covers 0.848 — the audit's ~20% order-1 unsoundness replicates at 15.2%, and the fix is the order index, not a bolt-on pair screen.

G3 — δ-BUDGETED VERSION. If every inert claim has μ_i ≤ δ then T_F ⊆ SEL^(j)_δ ⊕ |F∩N|·δ. The bound is stated but not needed in practice: the realized deficit exc(T_[m], SEL^(j)_δ) is computed per instance and published, so the accepted bias is a measured number in ŝe units rather than an assumption.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No continuity bound (damage conditional on movement is heavy-tailed and the vault's own data refutes it). No robustness under an estimated CPDAG — every statement above uses the true equivalence class, and the competitors in the table need no CPDAG at all, which must be said in the caption. Down-moves are outside the construction entirely: an analyst who OMITS a claim he should have made is invisible to μ, which explores retractions only. R always contains θ_0, so it can widen around a wrong centre and never move it — shared with the blanket and with every member of this family, and it must be printed as a limitation rather than discovered by a reviewer. Representation dependence is reduced but NOT fixed: comparing the minimal elicitation K against the equivalent over-report K+ (every Meek-implied orientation stated), the flagged-edge Jaccard is 0.913 for μ against 0.892 for Δ, with exact agreement 0.804 against 0.868 (sela2_core.py). μ flags implied edges that Δ cannot see because Meek re-derives them; that is a difference in blindness, not a proof of invariance, and the retrieval deliverable of direction (4) is still not representation-free.
refined.width_rule:
RULE. Report R = conv(SEL^(j)_δ ∪ {θ_0}); half-ignorance ig = width(R)/2; ŝe = sqrt(asymptotic_variance(sem,x,y,Z_0)/n) computed at the analyst's OWN Z_0 with no oracle leak; published half-width h = λ·(ig + z·ŝe), z = 1.959963985. λ is fixed by bisection to 95% empirical coverage on a validation stream drawn at a DECLARED analyst-error rate π, and the table entry is the mean 2h over the evaluation stream at the same π.

BUT THE ROW MUST BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT IS. By G2, at δ = 0 R is the same interval as the order-j retraction hull, so SEL does not get a second row: it shares that row and contributes two columns the hull cannot produce — |C|/|K| (how much of the elicited knowledge is load-bearing) and the top-1/recall of the localisation — plus a stronger guarantee label on the same number. Printing it as a separate method would be publishing the same interval twice.

THE ONLY LEVER THAT MOVES WIDTH IS δ, AND IT IS MEASURED WEAK. Calibrating by δ instead of λ is legitimate and interpretable ("ignore claims whose worst-case displacement is under δ, and print the deficit that buys"), but at demo scale it barely moves: mean width(SEL^(m)_δ)/width(blanket) = 1.0000 at δ=0, 0.9999 at 0.25ŝe, 0.9770 at 1ŝe, 0.9168 at 4ŝe, with P(ratio strictly inside (0.02,0.98)) never above 0.053 and mean realized deficit 0.107 ŝe at δ=4ŝe (sela2_delta.py, 300 problems, 133 with positive blanket width). The reason is structural and is the same fact that makes the screen good: the μ spectrum has an empty middle, so there is almost nothing for a threshold to shave.

REQUIRED IN THE TABLE, per the audit's fix (6): π is swept and the crossover shown, never a single scalar. The audit's own calibration measured plain-CI 0.1498 against blanket 0.4719 at π=0.00 and 0.8937 against 0.3881 at π=1.00; a method's rank in this table is a function of an unmeasurable prior on analyst error, and any single-scalar presentation of it is a result about the prior, not about the method.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
P1 — SPIKE-AND-TAIL WITH AN EMPTY MIDDLE (the claim the paper should stake). The published diagnostic is the real-valued spectrum μ/ŝe, and it is predicted to be bimodal with a wide, nearly empty margin: over ≥1,000 problems at n ∈ [10,18], P(μ = 0) ≥ 0.60, P(0 < μ ≤ 1·ŝe) ≤ 0.02, and P(μ > 10·ŝe | μ > 0) ≥ 0.40.
