Measured baseline at n ∈ [7,9] (2,004 claim-instances, sela2_retr.py): 0.7804 / 0.0010 / 0.572, non-zero μ/ŝe median 11.19, q10 4.09, max 49.7. KILL: if the (0, 1·ŝe] band carries more than 5% of claim-instances, the screen is threshold-sensitive, δ = 0 stops being a certificate, and the whole entry falls back to a calibrated-δ method with a coverage penalty.

P2 — THE INTERVAL HALF IS DEGENERATE BY THEOREM AND MUST NOT BE RAISED AGAIN. SEL^(j)_0 = ∪_{|S|≤j} T_S on 100% of instances at every j and every graph size; the width ratio to the blanket is exactly 1 at δ = 0. Measured 300/300. This predicts a null: a single instance with width(SEL^(j)_0) < width(∪_{|S|≤j} T_S) means the monotonicity or telescoping argument is wrong, and only then may the width claim be reopened. This is the prediction that retires the audited object's headline rather than repairing it.

P3 — THE LOCALISATION MUST STAY SELECTIVE AS THE ELICITED SET GROWS (the effect-scale form of the paper's own locality fact, 0.1376 at hop 0 against 0.000423 at hop ≥ 2). Predicted: mean |C|/|K| falls with graph size at fixed query, staying at or below 0.30 with mean |C| ≤ 2.0 at n ∈ [14,18] and |K| ≥ 6. Measured baseline at n ∈ [7,9]: inert fraction 0.731 (sd 0.332), so |C|/|K| = 0.269 with mean |C| = 0.67 in the null regime, and mean |C| = 1.43 of 3.05 under one false claim. KILL: if mean |C|/|K| ≥ 0.5 at n ≥ 14, the screen names half the elicited knowledge, gives the analyst nothing to act on, and this entry becomes a negative-results entry with revive_if = "a screen that keeps |C| small when |K| is large".

P4 — THE DISCRIMINATING PREDICTION FOR THE TARGET TABLE, STATED AGAINST OUR OWN INTEREST. The δ-lever never wins: mean calibrated width of SEL^(j)_{δ*} divided by the calibrated blanket width is predicted to stay at or above 0.85 for every π ≤ 0.5 at n ≥ 1000. If it comes in below 0.85 at any π, the row is worth publishing as a method after all and P2's demotion should be revisited. Uncalibrated baseline at the most generous threshold tried: 0.9168 at δ = 4·ŝe.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THE WHOLE ENTRY A NEGATIVE RESULT: P1 fails (no margin, so no certificate) or P3 fails (no selectivity, so no localisation). P2 and P4 failing in our favour would be good news; P2 and P4 confirming, which is what the current measurements say, leaves a diagnostic section with a theorem, not a table row.
refined.cost:
Per problem, exact (j = m): 2^m Meek closures, each followed by enumerate_dag_extensions, which brute-forces 2^u orientations of the u undirected edges of the retracted graph — so 2^m · 2^u DAG constructions, each costing one optimal_adjustment_set_dag plus one adjusted_estimand, with hulls cached by the kept-claim key. No space enumeration, no covering relation, no BFS distances, no SAT.

MEASURED on this machine (sela2_cost.py, seed 5, 25 problems per band, full lattice plus the μ spectrum): n ∈ [7,9], mean |K| = 3.28, mean u = 4.28 → mean 4.3 ms, max 11.9 ms per problem; n ∈ [10,13], mean |K| = 3.36, u = 4.92 → mean 13.9 ms, max 109.2 ms; n ∈ [14,18], mean |K| = 3.80, u = 5.24 → mean 85.9 ms, max 1,430.9 ms. Whole sweeps: 250 problems with the full lattice and the over-report lattice in 2.5 s; 250 problems × up to 5 single reversals, 723 lattices, in 4.1 s; 300 problems with the full δ-curve in 1.6 s.

TRUNCATED (j < m): Σ_{i≤j} C(m,i) closures; j = 1 is m closures and is exactly the audited Δ screen. The order-j truncation carries the order-j guarantee (G2) but NOT the δ=0 irrelevance certificate (G1), which needs the whole lattice.

HONEST LIMIT, carried over from the audit and not repaired: the cost is exponential in u, and on the graph sizes where TabPFN, CausalPFN and Do-PFN are the competitors the chordal component is large and enumerate_dag_extensions is not affordable at all. The exact core is a demo-scale instrument; what ships on large graphs is order-j with the order-j guarantee, and the table caption must say so rather than let the 4.3 ms be read as a statement about the competitors' regime.

refined.name: Certified reversal hull (CRH) — direction (1)'s ball, plus a free-admission certificate, with a split-calibrated budget
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING. Ĉ is the CPDAG of the TRUE Markov equivalence class (nothing below is claimed under an estimated Ĉ). K = (k_1..k_M) are elicited orientations of edges of Ĉ's skeleton, each with exactly two states. G0 = cl_Meek(Ĉ ⊕ K), Z0 = O*(G0), θ̂0 = the Z0-adjusted estimand. D* is the true DAG, τ* = θ_{D*}, E ⊆ [M] the indices false in D*.

REVERSAL FIBRE. For σ ⊆ [M], K[σ] reverses exactly the claims in σ. G[σ] := cl_Meek(Ĉ ⊕ K[σ]) if Meek admits it, else ⊥ ("data-refuted": the reversed knowledge set is inconsistent with Ĉ, and this is caught for free). Θ(G[σ]) := {θ_D : D ∈ [G[σ]]}.

RETRACTION COST. c: [M] → [0,∞) is the analyst's per-claim retraction cost, and c(σ) := |σ| + Σ_{k∈σ} c(k). Setting c ≡ 0 gives c(σ) = |σ|, so the construction REDUCES EXACTLY to direction (1)'s ball of radius ρ. Default when no confidences are elicited: c(k) = BFS hop distance from {X,Y} to k's endpoints (the locality law).

INERT CERTIFICATE. σ is certified inert iff G[σ] ≠ ⊥ and is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(G[σ], X, Y, Z0).
  LEMMA (verified, not asserted). Certified inert ⇒ Θ(G[σ]) = {θ̂0}. Proof: Z0 valid in the MPDAG sense means Z0 is a valid adjustment set in every D ∈ [G[σ]], so θ_D = adjusted_estimand(Z0) = θ̂0 for all such D. Checked on 439 certified-inert σ over 182 problems: 0 violations. It is sufficient, not necessary — 58.2% of non-certified σ also had zero width — so the certificate is conservative in the safe direction.
  COROLLARY (the whole point). Adding a certified-inert σ to any admitted family leaves the hull unchanged. Harmless claims can therefore be admitted at literally zero width.

ADMITTED FAMILY. Â(ρ) := {σ : |σ| ≤ b, G[σ] ≠ ⊥, c(σ) ≤ ρ} ∪ {σ : |σ| ≤ b, σ certified inert} ∪ {∅}.
  b is a DECLARED enumeration cap fixed in advance, not a tuned knob. ρ is the single calibrated knob.

CRH. I(ρ) := [ min_{σ∈Â(ρ)} min Θ(G[σ]) , max_{σ∈Â(ρ)} max Θ(G[σ]) ], widened by the estimator's sampling term at finite n.

WHAT CHANGED FROM witness-6, AND WHY. The retrieval framing is withdrawn as the licensing story. The ranked list ranks LOAD-BEARINGNESS (observable); the theorem wanted FALSENESS (unobservable); measurement says the gap between them is where the method actually lives, and the certificate — not the ranking — is what closes it.
refined.guarantee:
Three statements, graded honestly. The first is deliberately NOT called a theorem.

(R1) REMARK (deterministic, one line). If E ∈ Â(ρ) then τ* ∈ I(ρ). The only non-trivial ingredient is Meek soundness (a Meek closure never excludes a DAG satisfying the constraints), which is cited, not proved. This is a tautology of the union and is labelled as such; calling it a Theorem invites the one-line review.

(R2) THE EVENT THAT ACTUALLY LICENSES THE INTERVAL. Coverage equals P(A_cov(ρ)) where A_cov(ρ) := {∃σ ∈ Â(ρ) : τ* ∈ Θ(G[σ])}. The recall event {E ∈ Â(ρ)} is strictly stronger and is not what coverage needs. Both frequencies are reported side by side. This is where the certificate earns its place: because the harmless false claims are exactly the certified-inert ones, admitting them free raises P(E ∈ Â) from 0.889 (paid admission only) to 0.998 at ρ=3, and from 0.471 to 0.878 at ρ=0 — at zero width, measured over 452 problems. That +0.108 to +0.407 is the paper's mechanism, not the ranking.

(R3) THE DISTRIBUTION-LEVEL GUARANTEE, which needs no unobservable precondition. I(ρ) is nested increasing in ρ. Given m calibration problems exchangeable with the test problem, set ρ̂ = min{ρ : #miscovered ≤ ⌊α(m+1)⌋ − 1}. Then P(τ* ∈ I(ρ̂)) ≥ 1 − α over the joint draw of calibration and test problems. This converts the three unjustified constants of witness-6 into one selection procedure with a guarantee at the level the target metric is computed at. Measured over 200 random half-splits: ρ̂ mode 3, held-out damaged-stratum coverage 0.989 (5th percentile 0.862), mean width 0.2967.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. No continuity bound anywhere: nothing says a small perturbation causes a small change, and nothing bounds bias as a function of distance. The heavy tail costs the statement nothing, because the hull contains the tail's endpoint by construction rather than by a bound.

SCOPE WRITTEN INTO THE STATEMENT, not an appendix. (a) True CPDAG only; the guarantee is silent under an estimated Ĉ. (b) Claims must be edge orientations with a binary alternative — "no edge between A and B" and "W is not a confounder" have no reversal state space and are out of scope. (c) One query per graph enters calibration; with several queries per graph the problem's unit is the worst case over them, never the average. (d) Every benchmark row is conditioned on G0 being valid: Meek refused the corrupted knowledge set outright in 121 of 371 corrupted draws, so the framing "no existing check flags that" holds only for the surviving majority, and the refusal rate must be printed.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Four predictions. P1 is a lemma check, P2 is predicted to FAIL as specified, and that failure is the finding.

P1 (implementation, must hold exactly). Adding any certified-inert σ changes |I| by < 1e-9. ALREADY MEASURED: 439 certified-inert σ over 182 problems, 0 violations. If this ever fires, the certificate or the code is wrong, and it fires loudly rather than as a quiet loss of coverage.

P2 (THE DEGENERACY BET, AND IT IS PREDICTED TO FAIL). At ρ̂ calibrated to 95% on the damaged stratum, the mass of the width distribution strictly between 0 and the ball width, on the damaged stratum, is ≥ 0.20. MEASURED: 0.000 at ρ*=3. The profile is 0.245 interior at ρ=1 and 0.082 at ρ=2, but damaged coverage there is only 0.796 and 0.918. So at the only honest operating point the CRH is exactly two-valued on the damaged stratum, {0, ball width}, with mass 1.000 at the ball. That is the r_val disease relocated, and it is worse than r_val's own 0.689. On the FULL population the object is genuinely continuous (182 distinct widths at ρ=3, 60.0% at zero, 39.8% at the ball, 0.2% interior), so the honest statement is: the CRH is non-degenerate as a population summary and degenerate as a conditional one, and the paper must say which it is reporting.

P3 (THE SELECTION INCREMENT, the prediction that decides whether the ranked list survives at all). The saving of CRH over direction (1)'s ball at honest damaged-conditional 95% is zero whenever the expert's error model is exchangeable across claims, and positive only to the extent c is informative about E. MEASURED by varying the error model over ~300 problems each: +0.31% under uniform errors, +7.79% when errors concentrate near the query and c = hop is matched, +0.00% when errors concentrate far and c is anti-matched. PREDICTION: no cost function raises this above roughly 10% on an exchangeable-error benchmark. The paper must therefore either ship a non-exchangeable elicitation error model with evidence that real experts err that way, or report the selection increment as a measured null and rest the contribution on the certificate. Either is publishable; claiming the selective width without this row is not.

P4 (base-rate honesty control). |marginal coverage − damaged-stratum coverage| at ρ̂ must be < 0.10. MEASURED: 0.182 at ρ=1 (0.978 vs 0.796) — fails; 0.000 at ρ=3 — passes, but only at ball width. Calibrating on the damaged stratum closes this gap by construction, which is precisely why it must be the headline.
refined.cost:
Per problem: Σ_{s≤b} C(M,s) calls to apply_orientations, and for each surviving fibre one is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag plus one enumerate_dag_extensions with an optimal_adjustment_set_dag + adjusted_estimand per extension. At M≈4, b=2 that is 9.1 fibres per problem measured.

Measured throughput: 452 problems in about 3 minutes single-core; the three-condition error-model sweep (925 problems total) in about 12 minutes. Everything is CPU, minutes not hours, no SAT solver, no encoding.

Meek does 39.7% of the work for free: 1633 of 4112 fibres were refused outright by apply_orientations before any enumeration.

Honest note on the certificate's cost: is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag is only 1.8× cheaper than enumerate_dag_extensions + adjusted_estimand at this scale (0.03s vs 0.05s over 810 fibres), so the certificate is a PROOF DEVICE that makes free admission licensable, not a speedup. Do not sell it as one.

Calibration adds one pass over the grid (16 values of ρ) on cached per-fibre ranges, which is free; 200 half-splits ran in under a second.

refined.name: Elicitation survival profile σ^K(j), with safe mass ν_Z(q)
refined.formal_definition:
SETUP. Query (x,y); estimated CPDAG Ĉ; elicited claims K = (k_1,…,k_m), each k_i an orientation of an undirected edge of Ĉ; G_0 = apply_orientations(Ĉ, K) ≠ ⊥; Z = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G_0, x, y).

CENTRE GATE (mandatory, a third outcome, not a fold into r_val = 1). Report NOT IDENTIFIED AT THE CENTRE if Z is None, and NOT CERTIFIED AT THE CENTRE if is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(G_0,x,y,Z) is False. optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag returns O when all extensions agree on O, which is weaker than O being valid in all of them; on graphs of 5–8 nodes this fired on 37/300 = 12.3% of problems (fin3_sweep.py, seed 20260907) and on 6–12 nodes on 690/3690 = 18.7% (fin3_sound.py, seed 999). No profile, no radius and no interval is defined on that cell.

CORRUPTION ALPHABET. A pattern is c ∈ {keep, rev, ret}^m; j(c) = #{i : c_i ≠ keep}. Its state is G_c = apply_orientations(Ĉ, K_c) where K_c reverses the rev claims and drops the ret ones. c is ADMISSIBLE iff G_c ≠ ⊥, i.e. Meek does not refute it; inadmissibility is data-visible and costs the analyst nothing.

DEFINITION (survival profile). For j = 0,…,m,
  σ^K_Z(j) := |{admissible c, j(c)=j : is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(G_c, x, y, Z)}| / |{admissible c, j(c)=j}|,
reported together with its denominator. σ^K_Z(0) is the centre gate itself. Write σ^{K,rev} for the restriction to c ∈ {keep, rev}^m, the paper's own threat (a claim that is false yet data-consistent).

DEFINITION (safe mass). At an elicited per-claim error rate q,
  ν_Z(q) := Σ_{j=0..m} C(m,j) q^j (1−q)^{m−j} σ^K_Z(j),
the probability that Z stays back-door valid when each claim is independently wrong with probability q.

DERIVED, FREE. j_val := min{ j ≥ 1 : σ^K_Z(j) < 1 }, the breakdown number of CLAIMS; and the load-bearing list L := { k_i : some admissible single corruption of k_i decertifies Z }, with φ^K(1) = |L|/m = 1 − σ^K(1). L is direction (4) at |K|·|alphabet| calls.

WHY THIS INDEX AND NOT HOPS. A single-claim reversal is never one covering step away. Over 263 centre-valid problems the minimum hop distance of any single reversal was 2 in 163 cases, 3 in 70, 4 in 18, 5 in 10, 6 in 2, and 1 in zero (fin3_sweep.py). B_1(G_0) contains only retractions and refinements, so the hop-indexed σ(1) cannot see the event that produces the paper's own damage numbers, and the hop at which it lives varies from 2 to 6 per problem, so σ_hop(1) is not comparable across problems. Re-indexing also removes the counting artifact the audit found: among fragile centre-valid problems, Spearman(σ_hop(1), |undirected(Ĉ)|) = +0.247 (p = 3.3e-4, n = 207) while fragility itself rises with size (Spearman(φ^K(1), n_undir) = +0.188), i.e. σ_hop drifts safe as the graph grows; the claim-indexed σ^K(1) gives +0.054 (p = 0.44) and ν(0.2) gives −0.219, the conservative direction, negative within every m-stratum with n ≥ 49 (m=1 −0.255, m=2 −0.370, m=3 −0.115).

NON-DEGENERACY, MEASURED (fin3_sweep.py, seed 20260907, 300 problems, 11 s). Inside the stratum where r_val = 1 and therefore carries no information (172 of 263 centre-valid problems, 65.4%): ν(0.2) takes 22 distinct values on [0.512, 0.827], IQR 0.160, modal share 0.349, with no atom at 0 or 1; ν(0.1) takes 21 values on [0.729, 0.907]; σ^K(1) takes 10 values with a real atom at 0 (37.2%: every single claim is load-bearing). The audited hop version in the same stratum: 9 values, IQR 0.083, 77% of mass on two values.

THE RUNNING EXAMPLE NOW EXERCISES IT (fin3_demo.py, 8-variable demo, 48 MPDAGs). Scenarios A, B, C have r_val = 3, 3, 2 and hop σ(1) = 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, so the audited gate flags nothing. The claim-indexed profile separates them: A σ^K = (1, 1, 0, 0), ν(0.2) = 0.8960; B σ^K = (1, 1, .5, .5, 0), ν(0.2) = 0.9088; C σ^K = (1, .5, .5, 0), ν(0.2) = 0.7520.
refined.guarantee:
G1, THE CERTIFICATE (validity, never magnitude). If σ^K_Z(i) = 1 for every i ≤ J, then Z satisfies the back-door criterion for (x,y) in every DAG consistent with every knowledge state obtained by revising at most J of the elicited claims, reversal or retraction. It is exact rather than bounded: is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag quantifies over all of enumerate_dag_extensions, the corruption set is finitely and exhaustively enumerated, and inadmissible patterns are excluded because Meek already refutes them on the data. Nothing is asserted about the size of the bias when σ < 1, which is required, since damage conditional on Z moving is heavy-tailed; measured here, |point error| / se on instances where Z is invalid in the true DAG had median 11.4, p90 26.7, max 78.6 (n = 218, fin3_width.py, n_samples = 1000).

VERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED (fin3_sound.py, seed 999, 3,000 centre-valid problems, 16 s, expert error rate 0.35). Let w be the expert's actual number of wrong claims. On the 2,398 problems where σ^K(i) = 1 for all i ≤ w, Z was valid in the true DAG 2,398 times: zero violations. On the 602 where the certificate failed, Z was actually invalid 232 times, 38.5%. The warning is therefore ONE-SIDED and not tight, and the paper must say so: σ^K measures loss of CERTIFICATION, not damage. Second measurement of the same gap: in the cell where no elicited claim touches x or y, Z was invalid in the true DAG in 0 of 1,256 instances, while φ^{K,rev}(1) > 0 on 11.6% and ν(0.35) < 0.95 on 19.9% of them (fin3_scale.py, q = 0.35).

G2, COVERAGE TRANSFER (what makes it a row in the table rather than a diagnostic). Assume the CPDAG is correct and each claim is independently wrong with probability at most q. Then P(Z back-door valid) ≥ ν_Z(q), so a nominal 1−α interval computed on the elicited set has unconditional coverage at least (1−α)·ν_Z(q), and the ν-interval of the pseudocode has coverage at least 1−α, because every component is a valid 1−α interval in the world that carries its weight. Both are validity statements conditional on a declared error model. Neither is a continuity claim, and neither survives a misspecified CPDAG, which is why the sweeps use the true equivalence class throughout.

G3, WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No statement about an estimated CPDAG. No bound relating distance to bias. No aggregation of damage across the queries of one graph: σ^K and ν are defined at a fixed (x,y), and every average in the evidence above is over corruptions at a fixed query or over problems in a population, never over queries within a graph.
refined.width_rule:
RULE. Report the α/2 and 1−α/2 quantiles of the mixture Σ_c w_c N(τ̂_{Z(c)}, se²_{Z(c)}) over admissible corruption patterns, w_c ∝ q^{j(c)}(1−q)^{m−j(c)}, with Z(c) = Z on every pattern where Z stays certified and Z(c) = the candidate sets of G_c otherwise. Only the unsafe mass 1 − ν_Z(q) can move the interval, so ν = 1 gives back exactly the nominal CI on the elicited set: property (c) holds exactly, not approximately, and it fired on 21.3% to 30.6% of problems depending on q. The free constant is q, a per-claim error rate an analyst can be asked about, not a threshold t on a counting measure.

MEASURED (fin3_scale.py, seed 271828 + 350, 3,000 instances from 1,500 problems, 6–12 nodes, up to 10 undirected edges, n = 1,000 sampled rows per instance, expert error rate 0.35, P(Z invalid in truth) = 0.073). The repository has no sampler, so one was added: rows drawn from N(0, sem.covariance()), OLS from the sample second moments, so every width below carries sampling noise. One global multiplier per method calibrated so that coverage is 95% in BOTH the damaged and undamaged sub-populations, worst case not average:

  point on the elicited set (DoubleML-style)      2.6909
  blanket hedge over the whole class              0.3848
  corruption-class envelope                       0.3848
  claim-level gate φ^K(1) > 0                     0.3703
  ν-MIXTURE (ours)                                0.3677
  free locality gate (a claim touches x or y)     0.3597

Cluster bootstrap over problems, 300 replicates (fin3_boot.py): ours minus blanket is negative, ours minus the free locality gate is +0.0102 [−0.0004, +0.0245] at q = 0.35 and +0.0176 [−0.0040, +0.0427] at q = 0.20. So the object beats every hedge in the table and does NOT beat the free indicator. That is the audit's bar and it is not cleared. The reason is measurable and belongs in the paper rather than being hidden: the corruption class and the whole equivalence class produced the SAME set of candidate optimal adjustment sets on 100.0% of instances (mean 1.4713 distinct sets each), so there is almost no selectivity to buy at this scale. The advantage over the blanket does grow with the class, ratio 0.973, 0.953, 0.921 as |undirected(Ĉ)| goes 2–3, 4–5, 6–10 at q = 0.35 (1.015, 0.978, 0.908 at q = 0.20), which is where a real CPDAG lives.

THE METRIC ITSELF HAS A DEGENERACY, AND IT MUST BE REPORTED WITH THE TABLE. Pooled calibration, same generator, sweeping the expert error rate (fin3_table.py, 2,500 instances each): at q = 0.05 the break rate is 0.010 and the unhedged point estimate wins the pooled table at width 0.1511; at 0.10, break 0.027, point 0.1662; at 0.20, break 0.048, point 0.1949; at 0.35, break 0.106, point 0.9245 and last. Whenever P(Z invalid) < α = 0.05 the single global multiplier repairs only the noise misses and "do nothing" wins by construction. So the table is informative only if the paper prints the realised break rate beside it, or calibrates per stratum as above, which multiplies the point row by 13.6 to 20.1.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
Four predictions, each with a number and a decision rule, all checkable on an independent seed and generator before the table is written.

P1, RESOLUTION INSIDE THE DEAD STRATUM. On ≥ 1,000 centre-valid problems, restricted to the r_val = 1 stratum, ν_Z(0.2) will take ≥ 15 distinct values, have interquartile range ≥ 0.10, and put ≤ 40% of its mass on any single value. Measured on seed 20260907, n = 172: 22 values, IQR 0.160, modal share 0.349. FALSIFIED if any of the three fails, in which case the re-index bought resolution only on this generator.

P2, THE DRIFT DOES NOT COME BACK. In every stratum of fixed m with n ≥ 50, the Spearman correlation of ν_Z(q) with the number of undirected edges of Ĉ will be ≤ 0, while the same correlation for the hop-indexed σ(1) will be > 0 among fragile problems. Measured: ν at m = 1, 2, 3 gives −0.255, −0.370, −0.115; σ_hop gives +0.247 overall among fragile problems (p = 3.3e-4). FALSIFIED by a single significantly positive ν correlation, which would mean the counting measure is still rewarding irrelevant structure and the gaming path is open again.

P3, THE CERTIFICATE IS ONE-SIDED AND LOOSE, AND WILL STAY SO. On ≥ 2,000 problems with a declared error rate, zero violations of G1 will be observed, and the precision of the warning will stay between 0.25 and 0.55, i.e. when the certificate fails Z will actually be invalid in the true DAG between a quarter and a half of the time. Measured: 0 violations in 2,398 certificate-held problems, precision 0.385 in 602 failures. A violation kills the guarantee outright. A precision above 0.55 would mean the object is tighter than claimed and the paper is understating it; below 0.25 it is an alarm not worth acting on and the width rule should hedge on a narrower event.

P4, THE BET FAILS UNLESS THE CLASS IS BIGGER THAN THE CLAIM SET, AND THIS IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO KILL THE PAPER. Compute, per problem, |{O*(d) : d in ext(Ĉ)}| against |{O*(G_c) : c admissible}|. Prediction: the calibrated width advantage of any selective method over the blanket hedge is bounded by the fraction of instances where these two sets differ, so on any generator where they coincide on more than 90% of instances no selector, ν included, can beat the blanket by more than about 10%, and the free indicator "does an elicited claim touch x or y" will not be beaten. Measured: coincidence 100.0%, mean 1.4713 sets, ours beats blanket by 4.4% and loses to the free indicator by 0.0102 [−0.0004, +0.0245]. FALSIFIED, and the paper's bet vindicated, only if a generator whose classes are genuinely richer (target: coincidence below 60%, mean distinct sets above 3) shows the ν-interval beating the free indicator by more than 5% with a bootstrap interval excluding zero. If that experiment comes back tied again, the selective-widening claim must be dropped and the object shipped as the diagnostic and certificate it is, not as a row in the width table.
refined.cost:
Per query: at most 3^m apply_orientations plus one is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag per distinct resulting graph, with memoisation on MPDAG.key(); 2^m for the reversal-only profile that the width rule uses; 2|K| for the load-bearing list. Independent of |space|, so nothing is paid for the parts of Ĉ the expert never spoke about, which is the opposite of the hop-indexed object.

MEASURED. 8-variable demo, |space| = 48, 96 covering pairs: profile 1.0 to 1.8 ms per scenario against 25 ms for enumerate_space plus covering_pairs plus BFS, so the whole certificate is roughly a twentieth of the machinery it replaces (fin3_demo.py). Sweep of 300 problems including the hop machinery for comparison: 11 s (fin3_sweep.py). Larger regime, 1,500 problems on 6 to 12 nodes with up to 10 undirected edges, where enumerate_space would have had to sieve 3^10 = 59,049 candidates and was not run at all: 1.8 s of profile time in total, 1.2 ms per problem, inside a 13 s run that also drew the SEMs, sampled 3,000 datasets of 1,000 rows and evaluated all six methods (fin3_scale.py). Soundness check, 3,000 problems, 16 s (fin3_sound.py). Full sweep of the error rate, four values, 2,500 instances each: 22 to 26 s per value (fin3_table.py). Everything CPU, numpy plus scipy.stats.norm only, minutes not hours.

refined.name: Certified core size c (canonicalised, reversal-complete)
refined.formal_definition:
SETTING. C is the CPDAG of the TRUE equivalence class (never an estimated one — the hat is deleted, per the paper's constraint). K is the elicited set of orientation claims, each an ordered pair (t,h) whose endpoints are joined by an undirected edge of C. G0 := apply_orientations(C, K) is required non-None; Z := optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, x, y) is required non-None and valid in G0.

STEP 1 — CANONICALISE. K* := a subset-minimal K' ⊆ K with apply_orientations(C, K').directed_edges == G0.directed_edges, found greedily by deleting claims in a fixed order (≤|K| closure calls). K* generates the same G0 and hence the same Z. Write m := |K*|. Convention for the no-knowledge row of the table: K = ∅ ⇒ m = 0, c := 0, κ := 1. Every quantity below is defined on K*, never on raw K. This step is not cosmetic: it is what makes the scalar immune to padding with Meek-implied claims (see the prediction).

STEP 2 — CORRUPTION MODEL (REVERSAL ONLY). For J ⊆ K*, W(J) := apply_orientations(C, {reverse(k) if k ∈ J else k}). J is admissible iff W(J) ≠ None. Ranging J over 2^{K*} enumerates every direction assignment to the edges of K*, so the model is world-complete: every DAG D of the equivalence class extends W(J_D) where J_D is the set of claims of K* that D contradicts, and J_D is admissible. The proposal's retraction arm is DELETED. Lemma (retraction redundancy): ext(apply_orientations(C, K*∖J)) = ⋃_{J'⊆J} ext(W(J')), so retraction-safe(J) ⟺ safe(J') for all J' ⊆ J. Measured here: the retraction arm changed the verdict on 0 of 800 problems while doubling the cost. Deleting it also deletes the "in either direction" overclaim, because the reversal arm already IS every direction.

STEP 3 — SAFE, FREE. safe(J) := (W(J) is None) or is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(W(J), x, y, Z). The None case is a sound free pass: an inadmissible reversal names no DAG in the class, so there is no world to certify against. T ⊆ K* is FREE iff safe(J) for every J ⊆ T. Freeness is downward closed, hence T is free iff T contains no minimal unsafe subset; let U be the antichain of minimal unsafe subsets.

STEP 4 — THE SCALAR. c := m − max{|T| : T free}. Equivalently c is the minimum hitting-set number of U (a maximum free set is a maximum independent set in U). REPORT c, an integer. κ := 1 − c/m only where a table needs a normalised number, and only on K*.

STEP 5 — THE SETS. core := K* ∖ T* for a maximum free set T*: a minimum-CARDINALITY SUFFICIENT set, not a necessary one. Report a named core only when the minimum hitting set is unique (measured unique on 1.000 / 0.955 / 1.000 at mean m = 1.64 / 5.12 / 6.08). The object to publish as the retrieval target for the author's direction (4) is the NECESSARY CORE N := ⋂ over all minimum hitting sets, the claims that lie in every core; scoring an arbitrary maximiser against a ground-truth false-claim list scores badly by construction.

PROVENANCE OF EVERY NUMBER BELOW. My sweeps against ~/bkrobust, archived with the raw JSON at /Users/josecosta/mugango/output/2026-09-07_radius-redef/certified-core/ (core.py, width.py, falsek.py, padtest.py, bigsweep.py, decomp.py). Sampler: random DAG on n ∈ [7,10) with edge_prob ∈ [0.22,0.40] (n ∈ [9,13), p ∈ [0.14,0.26] for the m ≈ 6 sweep), true CPDAG via dag_to_cpdag, K a random subset of the true orientations of C's undirected edges (optionally with a fraction reversed to make claims FALSE), (x,y) a random ordered pair with y a descendant of x, Z = O*(G0) filtered valid in G0. This is NOT the paper's 2,087-problem sweep; the magnitudes are mine and do not transfer. The proposal's own "7 distinct values" and "Spearman −0.981" do not reproduce and must not enter the paper.
refined.guarantee:
THEOREM 1 (conditional joint certificate). Let T* be a maximum free set. For every J ⊆ T* with W(J) ≠ None, Z is a valid back-door adjustment set in EVERY DAG extension of W(J). So all 2^{|T*|} joint direction assignments to the free claims leave Z valid, simultaneously and in either direction, CONDITIONAL on the core claims standing as elicited. This is checked exhaustively per problem, not extrapolated from single-claim checks.

THEOREM 2 (c = 0, the endpoint worth foregrounding). If c = 0 then T* = K*, so J = K* is among the certified subsets. Every DAG D of the equivalence class contradicts some J_D ⊆ K*, D extends W(J_D), and W(J_D) is certified; therefore Z is a valid back-door adjustment set in D. Two consequences an analyst can act on: Z is valid in the true DAG NO MATTER WHICH ELICITED CLAIMS ARE FALSE, and the point estimate is licensed with no structural widening and no tuned constant behind it. MEASURED HERE: with a truthful K, Z valid in the bare CPDAG on 291/291 c = 0 problems; with a deliberately corrupted K (mean 0.45–0.90 reversed claims per problem, so that Z is invalid in the truth on 8.5%–12.4% of all problems), Z valid in the TRUE DAG on 439/439 c = 0 problems across three sweeps. Zero counterexamples in 730 checks.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, and must be written down rather than glossed. (a) Freeness is CONDITIONAL on the core, not joint with it: nothing is claimed about a world where a core claim and a free claim are both wrong. Measured here, such a world exists on 0.000 of problems at mean m = 1.64, 0.045 at m = 5.12, 0.000 at m = 6.08. The width rule closes that hole by construction — those worlds touch the core, so they are enumerated — so the conditionality costs the interval no soundness; it costs only the strength of the English sentence. Do not repair it by quantifying freeness over core corruptions as well: that quantifies over all of 2^{K*} and forces c into {0, m}, which is the degeneracy this definition exists to escape. (b) The core is a minimum-cardinality SUFFICIENT set, not "the minimal set of claims that must be right"; a claim in one core is free in another. (c) c is a validity certificate, not a bias bound: nothing here is a continuity statement, and none is implied. (d) Everything is stated on the true equivalence class; no robustness claim is made under an estimated CPDAG.

HONEST REDUNDANCY. After canonicalisation the core is almost always just the set of individually load-bearing claims: c equals the count of claims whose single reversal breaks Z on 1.000 / 0.955 / 1.000 of problems at mean m = 1.64 / 5.12 / 6.08, and a minimal unsafe subset of size ≥ 2 occurs on 0.000 / 0.045 / 0.000. The exhaustive 2^m verification is therefore confirmatory rather than discriminative at these sizes, and the paper should say so instead of selling the certificate as a discovery procedure. What it buys is the joint guarantee, which m singleton checks do not license.
refined.width_rule:
M := {J ⊆ K* : W(J) ≠ None and (J = ∅ or J ∩ core ≠ ∅)} — the admissible worlds that TOUCH the core, not the 2^{|core|} subsets of it. For J ∈ M let Θ_J := {adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(d, x, y)) : d ∈ enumerate_dag_extensions(W(J))}, and Θ := {θ̂(Z)} ∪ ⋃_{J∈M} Θ_J. Report Î := [min Θ − q·ŝe, max Θ + q·ŝe], with q the single scalar the protocol calibrates to 95% empirical coverage for every row alike. When c = 0, M = {∅} and Î = θ̂(Z) ± q·ŝe: pure statistical width, no structural widening at all.

SOUNDNESS OF THE INTERVAL. θ_true ∈ Θ always. The true DAG's contradiction set J* is either disjoint from the core, in which case J* is certified free, Z is valid in the truth and θ̂(Z) = θ_true; or it touches the core, in which case J* ∈ M and θ_true ∈ Θ_{J*}. MEASURED HERE on 950 problems with corrupted K: structural coverage 1.0000, against 0.9920–0.9967 for the radius-1 (r_val = 1) hedge, which is therefore unsound, and 0.876–0.915 for the bare point estimate.

THE SAVING IS IN SUPPORT, NOT IN WIDTH, AND THE PAPER MUST SAY SO. Support shrinks: |W| → |M| by 1.94x, 1.95x, 2.02x, 2.05x, 2.62x, 3.27x, 3.30x, 5.56x across eight sweeps, growing with m — against the 2.37x–14.0x the proposal's 2^m/2^c arithmetic claims. Width does not shrink at all. MEASURED HERE: the certified-core interval has EXACTLY the blanket-enumeration structural width on 1.0000 of 1,650 problems (700 with truthful K, 950 with corrupted K). The mechanism, measured on 1.0000 of problems that have at least one non-trivial free world: every estimand a free world yields equals θ̂(Z), which is already in Θ. So free worlds contribute nothing to a range that already contains the point estimate, and any selective-widening scheme built on "which worlds break Z" inherits the blanket width. This is the finding that matters most and it is negative for the paper's bet as instantiated here.

WHAT THE ROW CAN HONESTLY CLAIM. A tie with the blanket-hedge and enumeration-of-total-effects rows on width, at 1.94x–5.56x fewer worlds enumerated and with a certificate that decides the zero-width case in m validity checks instead of the whole class. A win over every point row (DoubleML on the elicited set, TabPFN, CausalPFN, Do-PFN), which is where the width metric is actually decided: those must be inflated uniformly to cover the 8.5%–12.4% of problems where Z is invalid in the truth with heavy-tailed bias, while this rule pays zero structural width on the c = 0 stratum (measured 0.000 width on 471/471 c = 0 problems) and pays it only where a core exists. Do NOT write a width-saving claim against the blanket row. Note also that c is conservative for width: P(structural width = 0 | c > 0) = 0.392–0.573, and Spearman(c, blanket width) = 0.589–0.742, so a positive core flags fragility on many problems that carry no bias.
refined.degeneracy_prediction:
All thresholds fixed in advance, all checkable on the paper's own 2,087-problem sweep with c computed on the canonicalised K*.

P1 — NOT DEGENERATE (the claim r_val fails). c takes ≥ 4 distinct values and no single value carries more than 0.70 of the mass, at every mean |K*| ≥ 1.5. Measured here: 4 values / modal mass 0.460 at m = 1.64; 6 values / 0.465 at m = 5.12; 5 values / 0.647 at m = 6.08. Compare the defect being fixed: r_val = 1 on 0.689. Falsified if any stratum puts > 0.70 on one value, or if P(c = |K*|) > 0.10 at mean |K*| ≥ 4 (measured 0.015 and 0.000).

P2 — A USABLE ZERO STRATUM. P(c = 0) ∈ [0.05, 0.65]. Measured 0.460 / 0.075 / 0.113 with truthful K and 0.543 / 0.156 / 0.610 with corrupted K. Falsified below 0.05, which would mean the licence never fires and the width rule never pays.

P3 — PADDING IMMUNITY (the gaming attack). Pad every problem with the Meek-implied claims G0 re-derives, leaving G0 and Z bit-identical, then recompute. ZERO padded variants change c, |K*| or κ after canonicalisation, while ≥ 70% raise the uncanonicalised κ and none lowers it. Measured on 400 padded problems: 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.0000 changed after canonicalisation; raw κ rose on 0.765 (and on 0.781 and 0.914 in two other sweeps), fell on 0.0000, mean +0.267, max +0.833. A single c that moves under canonicalised padding falsifies the fix and sends the scalar back to being an interview-length artefact.

P4 — THE SOUNDNESS ENDPOINT. P(Z valid in the true DAG | c = 0) = 1.000 exactly. Measured 439/439 with corrupted K and 291/291 bare-CPDAG validity with truthful K. One counterexample falsifies Theorem 2 and the width rule with it; this is the single check to run first.

P5 — THE RISKY ONE, PREDICTING THE BET FAILS. The certified-core interval and the blanket enumeration have the same structural width on ≥ 0.99 of problems, i.e. mean width ratio 1.00 ± 0.01. Measured 1.0000 on 1,650 problems. If the paper's sweep instead returns a mean ratio ≥ 1.10, the free-world law breaks at their graph sizes and this becomes a genuine width method — that outcome would be good news and it is the one result that would raise the score.

P6 — THE REDUNDANCY IT MUST ADMIT. c equals the count of individually load-bearing claims on ≥ 0.95 of problems for mean |K*| ≤ 6 (measured 1.000 / 0.955 / 1.000), so the exhaustive certificate is confirmatory. If that holds, the paper reports the m-check computation with verification and does not sell 2^m as necessary. The audit's contrary reading — that the collinearity is a small-|K| artefact that dissolves by |K| ≈ 5 — is falsified here at m = 6.08 after canonicalisation, and canonicalisation is the likely reason.

KILL CONDITION, decided before the width table is written. If the calibrated width row does not beat the point rows, or if P(c = 0) < 0.05 at the paper's elicitation sizes, file a negative-results entry with revive_if: minimal unsafe subsets of size ≥ 2 exceed 0.15 of problems at mean |K*| ≥ 8, which is the only regime where the exact hitting-set computation buys anything over the m singleton checks.
refined.cost:
Exact, CPU-only, no SAT solver, no enumeration of G_Chat. Canonicalisation: ≤ |K| calls to apply_orientations. The certificate: memoise safe(J) (it does not depend on T) and enumerate subsets in increasing size, skipping any J that already contains a known minimal unsafe subset — worst case 2^m calls to is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag, not the 3^m the proposal asserted, and the retraction arm's factor of two is gone with the arm. MEASURED validity checks per problem: 2.12 (max 15) at mean m = 1.64, 16.14 (max 34) at m = 5.12, 34.48 (max 127) at m = 6.08 — against 2^m = 3.8 / 36.0 / 69.1 and 3^m = 11.1 / 306.2 / 845.6. The greedy lower bound the proposal offered "beyond m ≈ 8" is unnecessary; run the fast path (m singleton checks, then verify the complement) and fall back to the exact loop only when verification fails, which measured here is 0%–4.5% of problems. Minimum hitting set over the antichain of minimal unsafe subsets is enumerated by increasing size over the union of its elements, negligible at these antichain sizes.

Wall clock on this machine, whole pipeline including rejection sampling: 400 problems at m ≈ 1.7 in 0.9 s; 600 problems at m ≈ 1.6 in 1.7 s; 200 problems at m ≈ 5.1 in 43.5 s; 150 problems at m ≈ 6.1 in 18.1 s; the padding study, 400 problems with three core computations each, in 2.9 s. The interval adds enumerate_dag_extensions once per must-hedge world; that dominates at large m and is bounded by |M|, measured 1.58–12.41 worlds per problem against 2.64–29.47 for the blanket. Everything above runs in minutes, and the archived scripts reproduce it: /Users/josecosta/mugango/output/2026-09-07_radius-redef/certified-core/{core.py,width.py,falsek.py,padtest.py,bigsweep.py,decomp.py} with PYTHONPATH=/Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src.

designs.name: MASKSWEEP — one enumeration per problem, eighteen read-offs
designs.question: Which of C1–C18 report a quantity whose distribution is genuinely spread, and which have merely relocated r_val's point mass onto a new value? r_val died of an atom (0.689 at the value 1). Almost every surviving candidate is a hull over a family of DAG subsets, so the atom's natural new home is ν = 1, "my hull is the blanket hedge". The experiment asks one question per definition — where does the mass sit — plus the question that decides whether an atom at the OTHER end is benign: when a definition reports zero width, is it right? It deliberately does NOT decide the width table (that needs DoubleML/TabPFN/CausalPFN/Do-PFN rows and calibration); it decides degeneracy, which is the precondition for that table being worth building.
designs.population: One problem = (D*, Ĉ, one query (x,y), one elicited claim set K, one SEM). Draws: D* a random DAG on n ∈ [7,14) nodes in a random topological order, edge prob p ∈ [0.14, 0.35]; Ĉ = dag_to_cpdag(D*), the TRUE equivalence class in every run (no estimated CPDAG anywhere); keep only |undirected(Ĉ)| ∈ [3,7] so ext(Ĉ) is enumerable. Exactly ONE query per graph, drawn uniformly from ordered pairs with y ∈ descendants(x) — no damage is ever averaged across the queries of one graph. Factorial design, 3×3 cells: planted false-claim count j_true ∈ {0,1,2} × elicitation size |K| ∈ {≤2, ≤4, ≤6}. |K| is a declared axis and not a nuisance, because C1-P3, C2-P2, C11-P3 and C14-P2 each stake their non-degeneracy on the win growing with |K|; a sweep at one |K| would report the generator. Target 1,500 kept problems per cell (13,500 total), two seeds. All statistics are reported on the INFORMATIVE STRATUM, blanket width > 0, with its share printed (pilot: 0.760; C2 measured 0.328 and C11 0.213 on their own generators, so the share is generator-dependent and never suppressed).
designs.what_is_generated:
Per problem, ONE cache, and it is the whole cost of the experiment: ext = enumerate_dag_extensions(Ĉ) (pilot mean 10.7 DAGs, max 48); per extension D_i, τ_i, the Z0-validity bit, and the agreement bitvector A[i,c] = 1{claim c holds in D_i}; the index of D* in ext; the skeleton-BFS hop of each claim from {x,y}; max asymptotic_variance over ext.

K is sampled so the truth is known by construction: pick m = min(m_max, |und|) undirected edges of Ĉ at random, orient each TRUTHFULLY from D*, then reverse exactly j_true of them. So D* ∈ ext(Ĉ) at a known index, τ* = τ(D*), and the set of false claims is exactly the flipped index set — no oracle beyond the generator. Draws where K is Meek-inconsistent with Ĉ (empty mask) are rejected as not analyst states, and the rejection rate is reported (pilot 62%; C16 measured 121/371 on its own).

The cost collapse that makes 18 definitions cost the same as one, VERIFIED not assumed: ext(cl(Ĉ, K')) = {D ∈ ext(Ĉ) : D ⊨ K'}, and apply_orientations returns None exactly when that set is empty. Measured 0 violations over 4,860 pattern checks (60 problems × all 3^4 keep/reverse/retract patterns), and the shared cache is 19.3× cheaper than re-closing per pattern. Every retraction fibre, reversal fibre, certificate and hull of every candidate is therefore a numpy bitmask over one list — zero further Meek closures, zero further enumerations, and enumerate_space / covering_pairs / bfs_distances are never called except in the one anchor arm below.

τ uses the IDA convention C7 and C13 both insist on: τ(D) = 0 when y ∉ de_D(x), else adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D,x,y)) — otherwise optimal_adjustment_set_dag returns ∅ for two different reasons and the raw confounded coefficient is silently reported.
designs.what_is_measured:
Every definition is forced to emit ONE per-problem statistic in [0,1], so a single rule applies to all eighteen. Four families:

H (hull-valued: C1 RHIG_j, C2 CRH_j, C5 H(Sel), C6 flip hull, C7 R_b, C8 I^∪/I^∩, C9 LRH(h,b), C10 H_m, C11 U_b, C12 order-≤2 on L, C13 D(t), C14 Hull_t, C15 SEL, C16 CRH ball, C18 core-touching worlds) → ν = structural width / blanket width.
S (set-valued: C5 |Sel|, C6 |{λ_k>0}|, C11 |U_2|, C12 |L|, C14 |S(K)|, C15 |C|, C17 φ^K(1), C18 c) → |set|/|K|.
R (per-claim score: C1 ℓ, C5 λ(e), C6 λ_k, C7 λ, C8 λ, C15 μ) → λ/blanket, distributed over claim-instances.
I (index-valued: r_val baseline, C2 j_sat, C10 ladder rung, C13 t_val, C17 j_val) → index/m.

Per problem per definition also recorded: contains_truth = 1{τ* ∈ reported hull}; zero_and_wrong = 1{ν = 0 and τ* ∉ hull}; and, free of any data sampling, the finite-n dilution w(n) = (z·ŝe + h)/(z·ŝe + h_blanket) evaluated on a grid n ∈ {1e2…1e6} — the sampling half enters additively, so the whole n-axis is analytic and costs one asymptotic_variance pass. For family R, the score is paired with the ground-truth label 1{this claim is one of the j_true flipped ones}, giving precision@j against the chance rate j/|K|.
designs.primary_outcome: Per definition, per cell: the empirical distribution of its [0,1] statistic on the informative stratum, summarised as (P(=0), P(=1), interior mass, distinct-value count, largest atom at 3-decimal resolution and where it sits) — reported as an ECDF, not a mean. Beside it, two scalars: P(τ* ∈ hull) and the count of zero-and-wrong reports. The r_val baseline runs in the same table as row zero, so every candidate is read against the defect it claims to fix rather than against an absolute standard.
designs.decision_rule_fixed_in_advance:
Fixed now, before the full sweep. On the informative stratum, with ≥ 500 problems in the cell:

DEGENERATE if the largest atom ≥ 0.60, or interior mass < 0.10. The 0.60 is calibrated on r_val's own 0.689, so a candidate is convicted only by the disease it was built to cure.
NON-DEGENERATE if the largest atom ≤ 0.40 AND interior mass ≥ 0.20 AND ≥ 8 distinct values.
BORDERLINE otherwise, and resolved by one pre-declared tiebreak only: the atom must fall monotonically across the three |K| strata, each with n ≥ 200. Nothing else may promote a borderline row.

Overriding both, and checked first: the CERTIFICATE RULE. If a definition reports zero width on a problem where τ* is outside its interval even once at matched budget j = j_true, its atom at 0 is a silent failure, not a certificate, and the definition is marked UNSOUND regardless of its spread. C1-P1, C6-P2/G3, C10-P2, C13-G2 and C18-P4 each stake themselves on exactly this being 0; one counterexample falsifies the theorem, not the forecast.

RELOCATION TEST, decided on the 300-problem lattice anchor: if P(ν = 1 | r_val = 1) ≥ 0.95 and the two marginal atoms agree within 0.05, the definition is marked RELOCATED — the mass moved from the value 1 to the value 1, and the paper has renamed the defect. C2-P3 and C12-P2 predict this of themselves in advance and are graded as having predicted it, not as having escaped it.

The pilot already puts hull-at-budget-1 at atom 0.696 (|K|≤4) and 0.880 (|K|≤2) — i.e. the whole retraction family is presently on the DEGENERATE side of a rule fixed before the sweep, which is why the rule is written down now rather than after.
controls_and_sanity_checks: MASK IDENTITY, the foundation: on a random 2% subsample, ext(cl(Ĉ,K')) recomputed the slow way via apply_orientations + enumerate_dag_extensions must equal the bitmask, and apply_orientations is None exactly when the mask is empty. Measured 0/4,860 violations in the pilot. Any violation voids every read-off and the run is discarded.

τ CONVENTION: τ(D*) must equal sem.true_total_effect(x,y) on 100% of problems. Measured 400/400 in the pilot. This is the check that catches the O*(D)=∅ ambiguity C13 documented with a witness (truth x<-c->y with x->y reports -1.2482 where the total effect is 0).

MONOTONE NESTING: ν must be non-decreasing in the budget on every problem for every hull definition. Measured 0 violations over 400 problems × the full budget ladder. A violation is a bug in the mask construction, not a finding.

BLANKET ENDPOINT: every hull definition at its maximal budget must equal the blanket hull exactly (ν = 1.000). Measured 0/400 failures. This is the identity C2 verified at 160/160 and C7 at 160/160, re-verified here as a harness test rather than a result.

RETRACTION DOMINATES REVERSAL: the reversal hull must never exceed the retraction hull at matched budget (C8 Lemma, C18's measured 0/800). Measured 0/400 violations, and the two coincided exactly at b=1 and b=2 in the pilot — which also means C6's and C16's reversal families cannot escape a degeneracy that convicts the retraction family.

PERMUTATION CONTROL for family R: precision@j of the score ranking against a uniformly random claim permutation on the same instances. C1-P5 measured 0.310 vs 0.293 (no lift) while C5-P1 and C6-P4 claim large lift; they cannot both be right and the control settles it in the same pass.
SEED REPLICATION: two seeds, and every reported atom mass must agree within ±0.05 or the cell is reported as unstable and not graded.

GENERATOR PROVENANCE: r_val is recomputed on a 300-problem subsample via enumerate_space/covering_pairs/neighbour_graph/bfs_distances (39 ms/problem, 23× the cache — hence a subsample, not the sweep). Its atom must land near the paper's own 0.689; if this generator does not reproduce the defect, no verdict on this generator transfers to the paper's 2,087-problem sweep and the run is reported as off-distribution.

REJECTION AND STRATUM SHARES printed with every table: the Meek-inconsistent rejection rate (pilot 62%) and the informative share (pilot 0.760). C2 measured 0.328 informative and C11 0.213; a candidate that looks non-degenerate only because 80% of its rows are zeros must be visible as such.
ONE QUERY PER GRAPH is enforced in the generator, so no within-graph averaging can occur anywhere, and the constraint is a property of the data structure rather than a discipline in the analysis.
designs.what_would_falsify_the_whole_idea:
Three ways this experiment is worthless rather than merely negative.

(1) The mask identity fails anywhere. Then fibres are not subsets of ext(Ĉ), the cache is invalid, all eighteen read-offs are wrong, and the cheapness argument collapses back to per-pattern Meek closure (19× slower, still runnable, but the design's whole claim is gone). Pilot says 0/4,860; one violation and the run is void.

(2) The experiment does not discriminate: every definition lands in the same class, with atom masses within 0.05 of each other on every cell. Then the eighteen candidates are one candidate wearing eighteen names, the degeneracy question was never about the definition, and the correct output is a negative-results entry (letter C, an instrument that measured nothing) with revive_if tied to a generator whose equivalence classes are genuinely richer — C17 already measured the corruption class and the whole class yielding identical candidate adjustment sets on 100.0% of instances, which is exactly the regime where no selector can differ from another.

(3) The informative stratum is too small to carry a distribution — under ~150 problems per cell after filtering. Then every ECDF is over a handful of problems and no atom mass is estimable; the generator must be rebuilt for load-bearing knowledge before any verdict is issued. C2's own width rule says this in the same words, and its 32.8% informative share is the warning.

And the finding that would falsify the paper rather than the experiment: if ν = 1 for every definition at every budget on the informative stratum, the selective-widening bet is dead — the hull IS the blanket hedge, damage being local does not cash out as hedging being cheap, and the honest headline is that Meek closure cascades so retracting one claim reopens most of the class. The pilot's 0.696 and 0.956 atoms at budgets 1 and 2 say this is the live outcome, not the safe one.
designs.runtime_estimate:
Measured on this machine, not extrapolated from a guess. Pilot: 180 problems with a five-definition read-off in 0.3 s (1.6 ms/problem); 400 problems with the full budget ladder for both retraction and reversal plus all four control checks in 0.76 s (1.9 ms/problem); the larger cell (|K|≤6, 9–14 nodes) at 3.4 ms/kept-problem. The cache is 88% of the time and the read-offs are 12%, so going from five definitions to eighteen adds far less than it looks — the marginal cost of a definition is a numpy bitmask over ~11 rows.

Full sweep: 9 cells × 1,500 kept problems = 13,500 at ~2–3.5 ms including rejection sampling ≈ 30–50 s; with all eighteen read-offs, call it 60–90 s. The n-axis is free (analytic, one asymptotic_variance pass). The r_val lattice anchor is the only expensive arm at 39 ms/problem, so it is capped at 300 problems ≈ 12 s. Two seeds doubles it. TOTAL: under 4 minutes single-core, CPU only, numpy alone, no SAT solver and none needed.

For contrast, the naive design — each definition running its own closures and enumerations — costs 19.3× the cache on the fibres alone and would put the same sweep near an hour, which is how eighteen separate audit scripts came to exist in the output directory instead of one table.
designs.implementation_sketch:
Two files under /Users/josecosta/mugango/output/2026-09-07_radius-redef/masksweep/, run with PYTHONPATH=/Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src. Working prototypes verifying every claim above are at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josecosta-mugango/1cbd3bff-6ceb-4991-8a2a-b20d5a3f01d3/scratchpad/{verify_mask.py,proto.py,scale.py,controls.py}.

cache.py — the only file that touches the repository.

    def make_cache(rng, j_true, m_max, n_lo, n_hi, p_lo, p_hi):
        D  = random_dag(rng, n, p)                        # random topological order
        C  = dag_to_cpdag(D)                              # the TRUE class
        if not 3 <= len(C.undirected_edges) <= 7: return None
        ext = enumerate_dag_extensions(C)                 # <-- the one expensive call
        x, y = a uniform ordered pair with y in D.descendants(x)
        K = truthful orientations of m random undirected edges, then flip j_true of them
        A = np.array([[(u,v) in Dp.directed_edges for (u,v) in K] for Dp in ext])
        if not A.all(axis=1).any(): return None           # Meek-inconsistent K, rejected
        sem = random_sem(D, rng)
        tau = [0.0 if y not in Dp.descendants(x)
               else adjusted_estimand(sem, x, y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(Dp,x,y))
               for Dp in ext]                             # IDA convention, C7/C13's fix
        Z   = the common O* over the G0-extensions, else None (non-amenable, KEPT not dropped)
        valid = [is_valid_adjustment_set_dag(Dp,x,y,Z) for Dp in ext] if Z else None
        star  = index of D in ext ; hopK = skeleton BFS in C from {x,y}
        se2   = max(asymptotic_variance(sem,x,y,O*(Dp)) for Dp in ext)

Fibres are then pure numpy, and this is the entire mechanism:

    retract(A,S)  = AND over columns not in S of A[:,c]
    reverse(A,sig)= AND over columns of (~A[:,c] if c in sig else A[:,c])
    width(mask)   = tau[mask].max() - tau[mask].min()  (0 if empty)

readoffs.py — eighteen functions, each taking the cache and returning (statistic, contains_truth). Illustrative, all one-liners over the masks: C1/C7/C10 = union of retract(A,S) over |S| ≤ j; C6/C16 = union of reverse(A,σ) over |σ| ≤ b (C16 additionally filtering by cost c(σ) ≤ ρ using hopK); C2 = the same over minimal generating subsets of dir(G0)\dir(Ĉ); C9 = the mask {i : dis(i) ⊆ T_h and |dis(i)| ≤ b} read straight off A and hopK with no closure at all; C13's t_val = the first index in the κ-ordering at which tau leaves the singleton; C17's σ^K(j) and ν_Z(q) = counts of admissible patterns whose mask keeps `valid` all-true; C12/C14/C18's certified sets = which single-column retractions break `valid`; family R's λ(k) = width(retract(A,{k})) − width(g0). Nothing here calls the repository.

driver.py — loops the 3×3 cells and two seeds, runs the five controls inline (asserting, not printing), writes one tidy parquet/npz of (problem_id, cell, seed, definition, family, statistic, contains_truth, zero_and_wrong, m, |ext|, informative), then emits the ECDF table and the atom/interior summary. The r_val anchor is a separate 300-problem loop that additionally calls enumerate_space → represented_dags → covering_pairs → neighbour_graph → bfs_distances, joined on problem_id for the relocation test.

The single design decision worth restating: because ext(cl(Ĉ,K')) is a subset of ext(Ĉ) selected by claim agreement — verified at 0/4,860 — the eighteen definitions are eighteen bitmasks over one enumeration, so the experiment costs what ONE definition costs, and adding a nineteenth candidate is a function, not a run.

designs.name: SIT — the selection-increment test: does selective widening buy width because of *which* claims are hedged, or because of *how many* and *how often the class reopens*?
designs.question: Every surviving definition converges on the same family — a hull over the DAGs reachable by retracting at most j elicited claims — and every one of them reports a mean calibrated width below the blanket hedge over the whole equivalence class. The paper is judged on exactly that number. But three of the candidates' own audits already say the mean is a mixture: C8 measured a median selective/blanket ratio of exactly 1.000 with 52.8% exact ties, C2 measured 0.955, C18 measured the certified-core interval at exactly the blanket structural width on 100% of problems, and C12 measured that at order 1 hedging over the load-bearing set and over all of K give the identical interval on 300/300. So the headline saving may be produced by three things that have nothing to do with the method: (a) the base rate of problems where the equivalence class carries no ignorance at all, (b) the *cardinality* of the hedged set rather than its identity, and (c) the fraction of problems on which retracting one claim happens not to reopen the chordal component that sets the blanket width. The experiment asks one question and pre-commits to the answer: at honest 95% coverage, on the stratum where background knowledge can matter at all, and against a cardinality-matched random selection, is any selective row narrower than the blanket hedge — and is it narrower than the one-line free baseline "hedge the claims incident to X or Y"? Three pilots I ran this session against ~/bkrobust say the likely answer is no on both counts, which is precisely why the pre-registration is worth having.
designs.population:
The unit is a PROBLEM: one true DAG D*, its true CPDAG Ĉ = dag_to_cpdag(D*), exactly one query (X,Y), one linear-Gaussian SEM, one elicited claim set K. One query per graph, so problem = graph and no damage is ever averaged across the queries of a single graph; the bootstrap clusters on the problem.

Problems are drawn into a BALANCED FACTORIAL over the four confounds the brief names, with the levels crossed and the cells filled to equal size by rejection sampling:
  F1 graph size n ∈ {8, 12}
  F2 class width u = |undirected(Ĉ)| ∈ {narrow: 3–4, wide: 6–7}
  F3 elicitation saturation s = |K| / u ∈ {1/3, 2/3, 1}, so elicitation length is expressed relative to the ambiguity it addresses and is not confounded with F2
  F4 locality of the elicitation: NEAR (every claim has an endpoint at skeleton-hop 0 from {X,Y}), FAR (every claim has both endpoints at hop ≥ 2), MIXED (at least one of each)
Edge probability p ∈ {0.18, 0.26, 0.34} is drawn within cell and recorded as a covariate, so density varies inside every cell rather than tracking it.

Two cells are declared UNFILLABLE IN ADVANCE from a fillability pilot I ran before any outcome was computed (seed 7, 8,000 draws): (n=8, wide, saturated, FAR) occurred 0 times and (n=12, wide, saturated, FAR) 14 times. The structural reason is reportable as a finding rather than a nuisance — an analyst who speaks about every ambiguous edge of a wide class cannot avoid touching the query neighbourhood. The factorial is therefore 34 cells; the two are reported as unfillable with their attempt counts, never quietly reweighted.

Target 150 problems per cell → 5,100 problems. Each problem is then run at five ELICITATION-ERROR ARMS sharing the same graph, CPDAG, SEM, query and true claim set (a within-problem paired design): b_true = 0; b_true = 1 with the false claim drawn uniformly from K (exchangeable); b_true = 1 with it drawn preferentially from the query-adjacent claims (concentrated); b_true = 2 exchangeable; b_true = 2 concentrated. The exchangeable arm is the pre-registered primary and the concentrated arm the declared sensitivity, fixed this way in advance because C16 measured the selection increment moving from +0.31% to +7.79% exactly when the error model is matched to the screen.

Exclusions are counted per cell and reported, never silently dropped. Measured rates in my pilot (seed 31337, 200 kept of 599 attempts): apply_orientations(Ĉ, K_asserted) returns None — Meek refuses the corrupted elicitation outright — on 9.3% of attempts, which is a data-visible check the analyst gets for free and bounds the scope of the paper's "no existing check flags that"; the centre gate (optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0,X,Y) is None, or the returned set is not valid in G0) excludes 11.7%, consistent with C17's 12.3%. Problems whose blanket hull has zero width (the equivalence class already identifies the effect) are KEPT, counted, and excluded from the primary by pre-specification; my pilot measured that stratum at 43–46%, which is why a pooled mean over it would be an average over zeros.
designs.what_is_generated:
TRUE DAG. D* = _random_dag(rng, n, p) — the eight-line helper from tests/demo/test_evaluate.py, copied verbatim: nodes n0…n{n-1}, a random topological order, each forward pair included with probability p. Acyclicity is by construction.

TRUE EQUIVALENCE CLASS. Ĉ = dag_to_cpdag(D*). This is the TRUE CPDAG in every run, never an estimate; the paper writes C, not Ĉ-hat, and no robustness claim under an estimated CPDAG is made anywhere in this experiment. Accept the draw only if u = |Ĉ.undirected_edges| falls in the cell's band.

QUERY. Enumerate the ordered pairs (X,Y) with Y ∈ D*.descendants(X), Y ≠ X, and draw one uniformly. Amenability is thus guaranteed for the true DAG (so O*(D*) is a valid adjustment set in D*, which the sanity checks verify), while rival DAGs in the class may have Y ∉ de(X) and are priced by the IDA convention below.

ELICITED CLAIMS. For each undirected edge {a,b} of Ĉ its TRUE orientation is read off D* (D*.is_directed_edge(a,b) decides), giving the true-orientation list T. Skeleton-hop distances from {X,Y} are computed by one BFS over Ĉ.skeleton(). Set m = max(1, round(s·u)); sample m claims from T restricted to the locality level's admissible sublist (near / far / mixed), uniformly without replacement. K_true is that sample.

PLANTED ERROR. Draw the false set E ⊆ K_true of size b_true (uniformly, or weighted toward hop-0 claims in the concentrated arm) and reverse exactly those claims: K_asserted = K_true with each k ∈ E replaced by its flip. THE TRUTH IS KNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION — E is the set of false claims, D* is the true DAG, and no inference is involved. G0 = apply_orientations(Ĉ, K_asserted); a None is the Meek-refusal exclusion. Z0 = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, X, Y), gated as above.

SEM AND DATA. sem = random_sem(D*, rng) (coefficients bounded away from zero, random sign, edges visited in sorted order so the draw does not depend on PYTHONHASHSEED). τ* = sem.true_total_effect(X, Y). The population arm uses adjusted_estimand and asymptotic_variance directly. The finite-sample arm — which the target metric requires and which the repository has no sampler for — draws n_obs rows from N(0, sem.covariance()) with rng.multivariate_normal, forms the sample second-moment matrix once, and computes every OLS coefficient and standard error from it by the same normal-equation solve the repository uses in _regress_coeffs, with ŝe² = σ̂²_{y|x,z}·(A⁻¹)₀₀ / n_obs. n_obs ∈ {250, 1000, 10000}; 1000 is the pre-registered primary.

RNG DISCIPLINE. One numpy Generator per problem, seeded by SHA-256 of (cell id, replicate index), so any single problem is reproducible in isolation and cells can be run in any order or in parallel without changing a number.
designs.what_is_measured:
Per problem, the retraction fibre for a claim subset is Θ(S) = { τ(D) : D ∈ enumerate_dag_extensions(apply_orientations(Ĉ, K_asserted \ S)) }, memoised on frozenset(K_asserted \ S) — my pilot measured a mean of 4.9 distinct fibres per problem, so the cache does most of the work. The estimand uses the IDA convention fixed once: τ(D) = 0 if Y ∉ D.descendants(X), else the coefficient from adjusting on optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, X, Y). This is not cosmetic — optimal_adjustment_set_dag returns the empty set both when no adjustment is needed and when Y is not a descendant of X, and C13 measured 19.8% of class DAGs per problem mis-priced by the naive path.

ROWS, each emitting a per-problem interval:
  PLAIN — the analyst's own answer, [θ̂(Z0) ± z·ŝe], zero ignorance half. Stands in for DoubleML / TabPFN / CausalPFN / Do-PFN on the elicited set, all of which emit a point plus a sampling half and differ only in the estimator.
  BLANKET — hull of τ over enumerate_dag_extensions(Ĉ); the whole-class hedge, also the enumeration-of-total-effects row.
  BUD(j) — the budget-j retraction hull ∪_{|S| ≤ j} Θ(S) over all of K, j ∈ {1,2}. Retraction only: C2, C7, C8, C10 and C15 all establish that the reversal fibre is a subset of the retraction fibre, so reversal can never widen the hull, and dropping it halves the closure count.
  SEL — BUD(1) restricted to the load-bearing screen L = { k : apply_orientations(Ĉ, K\{k}) ≠ None and Z0 is not valid in it }. This is the row every candidate wants to publish (C12's L, C14's S(K), C5's screen).
  LOC — BUD(1) restricted to the claims with an endpoint at hop 0 from {X,Y}. The free one-line baseline; it costs one BFS and evaluates no estimand.
  PERM — BUD(1) restricted to a uniformly random subset of K of the SAME CARDINALITY as L. The negative control; B = 200 independent draws per problem give an exact within-problem randomisation distribution, and re-selecting indices over already-cached fibres makes it nearly free.
  PLACEBO — BUD(1) restricted to claims lying in a chordal component of Ĉ vertex-disjoint from {X,Y} ∪ Z0 ∪ every O*(D) enumerated. Must have width identically zero.

CALIBRATION TO HONEST 95%. Split the problems once, by cell, into a calibration half and an evaluation half. Rule (ii), the primary: rows with an ignorance half keep z = 1.96 fixed on the sampling half and scale the ignorance half about its midpoint by λ ≥ 1, the floor being C1's fix for the audit finding that λ* = 0.90 published a band strictly inside the interval the theorem covers. Rule (i): rows with no ignorance half (PLAIN) scale the sampling half by c ≥ 1. The two knobs are never mixed within a row. A row that reaches 0.95 at no multiplier is reported UNCALIBRATABLE with no width — and that is a result, not an accident: scaling cannot inflate a zero-width report, so a row whose zero-ignorance reports are sometimes wrong has a coverage ceiling below 0.95. My pilot (seed 424242, 400 problems, n_obs = 1000, one planted reversal) measured exactly this: PERM saturates at coverage 0.885 on the non-trivial stratum and cannot be calibrated at all, while SEL, LOC and BLANKET all calibrate at λ* = 1.00.

PER-PROBLEM QUANTITIES RECORDED: the raw hull endpoints of every row, θ̂(Z0), ŝe, τ*, the blanket width, |L|, |LOC|, |K|, u, n, p, the hop profile of K, the exclusion reason if any, and the per-problem ratio width(row)/width(BLANKET). The ratio's distribution is recorded, not only its mean, because the pilot says it is two-atom: on the non-trivial stratum (seed 90210, 300 problems) the ratio for SEL was exactly 1 on 70.3%, exactly 0 on 21.2%, mean 0.7529, median 1.0000.
designs.primary_outcome:
ρ* = W95(SEL) / W95(BLANKET), where W95 is the mean calibrated width at honest 95% empirical coverage of τ*, computed on the held-out evaluation half, restricted to the NON-TRIVIAL STRATUM (blanket ignorance width > 0), pooled across the 34 fillable factorial cells with EQUAL CELL WEIGHTS, at the reference arm b_true = 1, exchangeable error model, n_obs = 1000, adjustment map Z_opt, IDA estimand convention. Lower is better; ρ* = 1 means selective widening buys nothing over hedging the entire equivalence class.

Reported inseparably from ρ*, and pre-specified so neither can be dropped after seeing the other:
  Δ_sel = W95(PERM) − W95(SEL), the SELECTION INCREMENT at matched cardinality, with its within-problem permutation p-value from the B = 200 draws. If PERM is UNCALIBRATABLE, Δ_sel is reported as such — a stronger outcome than any number, since it says a cardinality-matched random selection cannot be made honest at any width.
  Δ_loc = W95(LOC) − W95(SEL), the increment over the free hop-0 baseline. Signed; the pilot suggests it is negative.
  The mixture decomposition of the per-problem ratio: P(ratio = 1), P(ratio = 0), and the conditional mean on the open interior, published in the same table cell as ρ*.
  The median ratio, beside the mean, always.

Uncertainty: BCa bootstrap over problems (B = 2000), clustered on the problem, stratified by cell so the equal-weight pooling is respected. No ordering is claimed that the intervals do not separate.
designs.decision_rule_fixed_in_advance:
SELECTIVE WIDENING IS DECLARED A WIDTH METHOD only if all four hold on the evaluation half:
  (1) ρ* ≤ 0.85 with a BCa upper end below 0.95.
  (2) Δ_sel > 0 with permutation p < 0.01, AND Δ_sel ≥ 0.25 · (W95(BLANKET) − W95(SEL)) — at least a quarter of the saving over the blanket is attributable to WHICH claims were hedged rather than to how many. (If PERM is uncalibratable, (2) is satisfied by that fact alone and is recorded as "selection is necessary, not merely helpful".)
  (3) Δ_loc > 0 with a bootstrap interval excluding 0 — the screen beats the one-line free baseline. A screen that loses to one BFS is not a contribution.
  (4) The ordering of PLAIN, LOC, SEL, BUD(1), BUD(2), BLANKET is unchanged across n_obs ∈ {250, 1000, 10000}, across the two calibration rules (ii) and (ii′: λ = 1 fixed on the ignorance half, sampling half scaled by c ≥ 1), and across both adjustment maps. A table whose ordering moves with the sample size or the calibration convention is reporting the convention, not the method.

BRANCHES, all written before the run:
  (1) holds, (2) fails → the saving is a base-rate-and-cardinality effect. The paper reports the blanket hedge as the method in the width table, and SEL survives as a diagnostic with a theorem (the budget-j containment statement) and no width claim. This is the outcome three candidates' own audits already point at and it is publishable as stated.
  (1) holds but P(ratio = 1) ≥ 0.60 and the median ratio ≥ 0.99 → the mean is a two-atom mixture. The paper must print the median and the atom masses in the same cell as the mean and may not state a general width claim; the honest sentence is that the win is carried by the minority of problems where one retraction does not reopen the chordal component that sets the blanket width.
  (3) fails → the contribution is the locality law, not the screen. LOC becomes the method row, SEL is withdrawn from the table, and the ranked-list framing of direction (4) is dropped.
  (1) fails → selective widening is dead as a width method. File a negative-results entry, letter C (an instrument that measured nothing), revive_if: a generator or a real-CPDAG corpus on which P(BUD(1) = BLANKET | blanket width > 0) falls below 0.40, since that is the only regime where a selective hull has room to be narrower.
  Any sanity check below 100% → the run is VOID and nothing is reported until the bug is found. A failed sanity check is never reinterpreted as a finding.

No knob is chosen on the evaluation half: j, the budget ladder, the screens, the strata, the locality definition, n_obs, the calibration rule and the error model are all fixed above. λ and c are fitted on the calibration half only, and the calibration/evaluation halves are swapped once as a check, not as a second chance.
controls_and_sanity_checks: CONFOUND CONTROL — balanced factorial. Graph size, class width, elicitation saturation and elicitation locality are crossed factors with equal cell counts, not covariates in a regression. Density varies inside every cell rather than tracking any factor. The pooled primary weights cells equally, so a cell that is merely easier to fill cannot drive the headline.

CONFOUND CONTROL — class width is conditioned directly. u = |undirected(Ĉ)| is the quantity that drives both the blanket width and the enumeration cost, so it is a design factor rather than something density is hoped to proxy. Measured this session (seed 20260907, 318 problems): mean |ext(Ĉ)| is 4.6 at u ∈ [2,3], 9.8 at u ∈ [4,5], 18.0 at u ∈ [6,8].

CONFOUND CONTROL — elicitation length as a fraction of ambiguity. |K| enters as s = |K|/u, so 'the analyst said more' is not confounded with 'the class was wider'. This is the axis C14's P2 predicts the whole effect lives on, and C11's P3 nominates as the decisive experiment.

CONFOUND CONTROL — one query per graph. No damage is aggregated across the queries of a single graph, the constraint the brief imposes; the bootstrap and the permutation test both cluster on the problem.

CONFOUND CONTROL — within-problem pairing. b_true ∈ {0,1,2} and the two error models are run on the SAME D*, Ĉ, SEM, query and K_true, so graph-level variance is differenced out of every budget and error-model contrast.

CONFOUND CONTROL — the trivial stratum is never pooled into the primary. Problems whose blanket hull has zero width are kept, counted (43–46% in my pilots) and reported as their own line. A mean taken over them is an average over zeros and rewards the null method.

CONFOUND CONTROL — mixture decomposition published with the mean. P(ratio = 1), P(ratio = 0) and the interior conditional mean sit in the same cell as ρ*, because the pilot says the distribution is two-atom (70.3% at exactly 1, 21.2% at exactly 0, median 1.000, mean 0.753 — seed 90210, 300 problems) and a lone mean hides exactly that.
CONFOUND CONTROL — cardinality matching. PERM hedges a random subset of K of the same size as L, so the selective row cannot win merely by enumerating fewer fibres.

CONFOUND CONTROL — the free baseline is a mandatory row. LOC is one BFS over Ĉ.skeleton() and no estimand evaluation. C17 measured its object losing to this indicator and C16 measured a 1.2% margin over direction (1)'s plain ball; if SEL does not beat it, the contribution is the locality law.

CONFOUND CONTROL — calibration-rule sensitivity. Everything is recomputed under rule (ii′) (λ = 1, sampling half scaled) as well as rule (ii) (λ ≥ 1 on the ignorance half, z fixed). The method ordering must be identical under both, or the table is reporting the calibration convention.

CONFOUND CONTROL — sample size. n_obs ∈ {250, 1000, 10000} on the same problems. If the ordering flips with n_obs the table is reporting sample size rather than knowledge (C3's P2), and the width table is replaced by the population-only ignorance table.

CONFOUND CONTROL — adjustment map. The whole primary is recomputed with Z_pa(D) = pa_D(X) in place of Z_opt(D) = optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D,X,Y). C1 measured the levels differing by about 30% across maps while the ordering was preserved within each; no number is quoted without its map, and cross-map comparisons are void.

CONFOUND CONTROL — estimand convention. The primary uses the IDA convention τ(D) = 0 when Y ∉ D.descendants(X); the naive path (adjusting on optimal_adjustment_set_dag, which returns ∅ in that case and yields a confounded coefficient) is run alongside and the difference reported, so no reviewer can attribute the result to the convention. C13 measured 19.8% of class DAGs per problem mis-priced by the naive path and the repository's own audit_rw_0_ostar_edge_case.py records the trap.

CONFOUND CONTROL — exclusion accounting. Meek refusal of the corrupted elicitation (9.3% of attempts in my pilot), the centre gate (11.7%), and the two unfillable factorial cells (0/8000 and 14/8000 at seed 7) are counted per cell and printed. Nothing is dropped silently, and the Meek-refusal rate bounds the paper's premise that no existing check flags a false-but-data-consistent K.

NEGATIVE CONTROL A (the randomisation null, and the headline one) — PERM. Under the null that the load-bearing screen carries no information beyond its cardinality, PERM and SEL have the same calibrated width AND the same coverage; the B = 200 within-problem draws give the exact null distribution. It has power: in my pilot (seed 90210) PERM's raw hull was zero-width-and-WRONG on 17/300 problems against 0/300 for SEL, and in the finite-sample pilot (seed 424242) PERM could not be calibrated to 95% at any λ, saturating at coverage 0.885 on the non-trivial stratum.

NEGATIVE CONTROL B (should show exactly nothing) — the inert-component placebo. Hedging over claims lying in a chordal component of Ĉ vertex-disjoint from {X,Y} ∪ Z0 ∪ every enumerated O* must produce a hull of width < 1e-12 on 100% of problems, and appending such claims to K must leave ρ* bit-identical. A non-zero width is either a bug or a refutation of the locality premise the whole paper rests on; a shift in ρ* is the padding/gaming attack C18's P3 tests.

NEGATIVE CONTROL C (the honest analyst) — the b_true = 0 arm. With no false claim there is nothing for a selective hedge to repair, so PLAIN must already reach 95% and SEL's excess width over PLAIN is pure cost. If ρ* at b_true = 0 equals ρ* at b_true = 1, the number is a property of the generator's equivalence classes and not a response to damage, and the 'selective widening answers a false claim' story is unsupported.

SANITY 1 (estimand identity) — for every problem, |adjusted_estimand(sem, X, Y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D*, X, Y)) − sem.true_total_effect(X, Y)| < 1e-9. This single assertion exercises O*, the SEM covariance, the normal-equation solve and the amenability filter at once. Measured this session: max deviation 3.997e-15 on 318/318 problems (seed 20260907). A failure is an implementation bug, never a finding.

SANITY 2 (τ-convention guard) — for every enumerated DAG D, assert is_valid_adjustment_set_dag(D, X, Y, optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D, X, Y)) whenever Y ∈ D.descendants(X), and force τ(D) = 0 otherwise. This is the check that would have caught the documented O*-returns-∅ trap before it reached a coverage number.

SANITY 3 (ladder endpoints) — the hull at j = |K| must be bit-identical to the hull over enumerate_dag_extensions(Ĉ), and the hull at j = 0 identical to Θ(G0).
