Measured 300/300 this session (seed 90210). A mismatch means apply_orientations or the retraction indexing is wrong and every soundness statement in the paper is void.
SANITY 4 (nesting) — hull_j ⊆ hull_{j+1} on 100% of problems, and Θ(S) ⊆ Θ(S′) for S ⊆ S′. Measured 300/300 (seed 90210). A violation is a fibre-cache bug, since monotonicity is definitional.

SANITY 5 (membership certificate) — is_consistent_extension(D*, apply_orientations(Ĉ, K_asserted \ E)) must be True for E the planted false set, on 100% of problems. Measured 300/300 (seed 90210). This is the containment the budget-j theorem rests on; one failure and the theorem is misstated or Meek closure is broken.

SANITY 6 (zero-ignorance certificate) — in the population arm, whenever the matched-budget hull has zero width, |θ̂(Z0) − τ*| < 1e-9. It discriminates: measured 0/300 violations for SEL against 17/300 for PERM (seed 90210), so it is a live check and not a tautology.

SANITY 7 (equivalence-class round-trip) — dag_to_cpdag(D) == Ĉ for every D ∈ enumerate_dag_extensions(Ĉ), and is_valid_mpdag(G0). Catches a v-structure or Meek bug that would silently change what 'the class' means.

SANITY 8 (determinism) — one cell is rerun with the same seed under two different PYTHONHASHSEED values and must reproduce every number bit-identically. The repository's own random_sem docstring records why: iterating a frozenset of edges consumes the RNG in a hash-order-dependent sequence, and this experiment iterates edge sets constantly.

SANITY 9 (calibration hygiene) — ŝe is computed on the analyst's OWN Z0 and never on optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D*, ·), which would leak the truth into the width; and the primary is recomputed with the calibration and evaluation halves swapped, the two agreeing within the bootstrap interval. Both leaks are the ones C1's audit closed.

SANITY 10 (population/finite-sample agreement) — on a 50-problem subsample at n_obs = 1e6 the finite-sample hull endpoints must match the population ones to < 0.01. Catches a wrong sample second-moment matrix or a mis-specified standard error, which would otherwise show up as a plausible-looking width.
designs.what_would_falsify_the_whole_idea:
The idea under test is the paper's bet: damage is local, so a selective widening should cost less width than a uniform one. It is falsified, and the selective row must be withdrawn, if any of the following comes back from the evaluation half.

ρ* > 0.85, or a BCa upper end at or above 0.95. The selective hull is the blanket hedge with extra steps, and the family's only surviving contribution is the budget-j containment theorem, which is a diagnostic and not a row in a width table. My three pilots put ρ* near 0.75 on the non-trivial stratum, so this threshold is genuinely at risk in both directions.

Δ_sel ≤ 0, or Δ_sel positive but below a quarter of the saving over the blanket, with PERM calibratable. The saving is then produced by cardinality and by the base rate of problems where the class carries no ignorance, and the paper may not describe it as selection. This is the branch three of the candidates' own audits already point at: C12 measured hedging over L and over all of K giving the identical interval on 300/300 problems at order 1, and I replicated the no-op three times this session — SEL and BUD(1) agreed to four decimal places in raw width (0.7529 vs 0.7529, seed 90210) and in calibrated width (0.4983 vs 0.4983, seed 424242).

Δ_loc ≤ 0. The one-line hop-0 baseline is not beaten, so the measured locality law is doing all the work and the screen is decoration. My finite-sample pilot has LOC at 0.7721 against SEL at 0.7845 on the non-trivial stratum, i.e. currently losing, which is the same sign C17 and C16 measured.

P(BUD(1) = BLANKET | blanket width > 0) ≥ 0.60 together with a median ratio of 1.000. The mean is then a two-atom mixture and the r_val degeneracy has been relocated rather than removed: a minimum over a ball collapsing to 1 on 68.9% of problems is replaced by a hull collapsing to the blanket on a comparable majority. Measured 70.3% in my pilot, so this is the most likely single outcome and the paper must be written to survive it.

The ordering of the rows changing with n_obs, with the calibration rule, or with the adjustment map. The table is then reporting a convention and no method claim can be read off it.

Any sanity check below 100%. That does not falsify the idea; it voids the run. The distinction is kept sharp on purpose, because an implementation bug that produces a plausible width is the failure mode this whole design exists to make impossible to mistake for a finding.

What would NOT falsify it, and must not be used as a defence: a large ρ* saving on the pooled stratum that includes zero-blanket-width problems, a raw-width comparison at unequal coverage (PERM is narrower than SEL on raw width and dishonest — measured 0.331 against 0.753 — so raw width is meaningless here), or a win in the concentrated error arm alone, which is the arm whose error model was chosen to match the screen.
designs.runtime_estimate:
Measured this session on this machine, CPU only, PYTHONPATH=/Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src, no SAT solver and none needed. Three pilots: 200 problems with generation, rejection sampling, blanket hull, budget-1 hull and both screens in 0.82 s (4.1 ms per kept problem, seed 31337); 300 problems with the same plus all three sanity checks and the permutation arm in 1.6 s (5.4 ms, seed 90210); 400 problems with the full finite-sample arm — a 1000-row multivariate-normal draw, the sample second-moment matrix, every OLS and standard error, all six rows and the calibration — in 1.4 s (3.5 ms, seed 424242). Fillability probe: 8,000 candidate draws in 1.3 s.

Design volume: 34 fillable cells × 150 problems = 5,100 problems, each at 5 elicitation-error arms ≈ 25,500 hull computations. At 4–6 ms that is 2–3 minutes of core compute. The three n_obs levels reuse the same fibres and re-solve only the OLS, adding well under a minute. The B = 200 permutations per problem re-select index subsets over already-cached fibres and cost seconds in total; my pilot measured a mean of 4.9 distinct fibres cached per problem, which is what makes this cheap. The BCa bootstrap at B = 2000 runs over 5,100 cached per-problem widths and is seconds. The population arm, the second adjustment map and the naive-estimand arm each re-run the hull loop, roughly tripling the core.

The dominant cost is rejection sampling in the hard cells, not the hulls: pooled the acceptance rate is about 1 in 3, but (n=12, narrow, saturated, FAR) filled 63 times in 8,000 draws, so a 150-problem cell there needs on the order of 20,000 accepted-candidate draws. Cap attempts at 200,000 per cell and report any cell that fails to fill.

Total: under 45 minutes single-core, and under 10 with the 34 cells distributed across cores, since cells share no state and each problem is seeded independently from SHA-256 of (cell id, replicate). The only scaling risk is enumerate_dag_extensions, exponential in the size of the chordal components, which is why u is capped at 7 by design and why the cap is a declared scope statement rather than a hidden one; the blanket and enumeration-of-total-effects rows pay the same cost, so the comparison stays fair.
designs.implementation_sketch:
Layout under /Users/josecosta/mugango/output/2026-09-07_radius-redef/sit/: gen.py (generator and factorial), rows.py (the six rows plus the placebo), calib.py (the two calibration rules and the bootstrap), sanity.py (S1–S10 as assertions), run.py (the cell loop), analyse.py (primary, decomposition, permutation test, tables). Results to results.parquet, one row per (problem, error arm, method, n_obs, map, convention); every table is regenerated from it so no number is ever typed by hand.

Imports, all from the verified surface: MPDAG from bkrobust.demo.graph; dag_to_cpdag from bkrobust.demo.example; apply_orientations, enumerate_dag_extensions, is_consistent_extension, is_valid_mpdag from bkrobust.demo.meek; optimal_adjustment_set_dag, optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag, is_valid_adjustment_set_dag, is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag, random_sem, adjusted_estimand, asymptotic_variance from bkrobust.demo.evaluate. _random_dag is copied from tests/demo/test_evaluate.py. Nothing from bkrobust.demo.space is imported: enumerate_space, covering_pairs, neighbour_graph, bfs_distances, atomic_moves and check_metric_axioms are all deleted from the critical path along with the hop currency r, so no problem is ever discarded for space size.

Per-problem core, about sixty lines:

  rng = default_rng(int.from_bytes(sha256(f"{cell}:{rep}".encode()).digest()[:8], "big"))
  D = random_dag(rng, n, p); C = dag_to_cpdag(D)
  accept only if cell's u band holds; draw (X,Y) from the amenable ordered pairs
  hopd = BFS over C.skeleton() from {X,Y}                     # one deque, ten lines
  T = [(a,b) if D.is_directed_edge(a,b) else (b,a) for (a,b) in sorted(C.undirected_edges)]
  K_true = sample m from T restricted by the locality level; E = planted false subset
  K_ass  = K_true with each k in E flipped
  G0 = apply_orientations(C, K_ass);  skip-and-count if None
  Z0 = optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag(G0, X, Y); skip-and-count if None or not valid in G0
  sem = random_sem(D, rng); S = rng.multivariate_normal(0, sem.covariance(), n_obs); Shat = S.T@S/n_obs
  ols(z) -> (coef, se) by one solve on Shat, exactly the repository's normal-equation form
  fib(S_retracted) memoised on frozenset: apply_orientations then enumerate_dag_extensions,
      tau(D') = 0.0 if Y not in D'.descendants(X) else ols(optimal_adjustment_set_dag(D',X,Y))[0]
  L   = [i for i,k in enumerate(K_ass) if (G:=apply_orientations(C, K_ass minus i)) is not None
                                       and not is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(G, X, Y, Z0)]
  LOC = [i for i,k in enumerate(K_ass) if min(hopd[k[0]], hopd[k[1]]) == 0]
  PERM_b = rng.permutation(len(K_ass))[:len(L)] for b in range(200)
  rows = {name: (min,max) over fib over the selected singleton retractions, unioned with fib(K_ass)}

Sorted iteration everywhere an edge set is traversed, mirroring the discipline random_sem already documents, so PYTHONHASHSEED cannot move a number; S8 asserts it.

Calibration and analysis: bisect λ (rule ii) or c (rule i) on the calibration half to the smallest multiplier reaching 0.95 empirical coverage of τ*, declare UNCALIBRATABLE if the coverage ceiling is below 0.95 at the grid's top, freeze it, and evaluate on the held-out half. ρ* is the equal-cell-weight mean of W95(SEL) over that of W95(BLANKET) on the non-trivial stratum; the BCa bootstrap resamples problems within cell. The permutation test is paired and exact within problem: for each problem compare W95(SEL) against the 200 PERM draws, then combine across problems by the standard cluster-permutation statistic.

The four checks that must run and pass before analyse.py will emit a table, wired as assertions rather than prose: S1 the estimand identity, S3 the ladder endpoints, S4 nesting, S5 the membership certificate. All four are already measured clean this session (318/318, 300/300, 300/300, 300/300), so a failure means the new code broke something rather than that the repository is unsound.

fatal: THE SOUNDNESS ARM CANNOT FIRE. The CERTIFICATE RULE is evaluated 'at matched budget j = j_true', but every union-of-fibres hull contains D* at that budget by construction: D* disagrees with K exactly on the planted flip set S_flip, |S_flip| = j_true, and the union over |S| <= j_true includes S = S_flip, so retract(A,S_flip) contains D*. Measured 0/573 failures (AUDIT_masksweep.py). So contains_truth == 1 and zero_and_wrong == 0 identically for C1, C2, C5, C6, C7, C8, C10, C11, C13, C14, C15, and the verdict UNSOUND is unreachable for exactly the candidates that stake themselves on it (C1-P1, C6-P2/G3, C10-P2, C13-G2). The rule only has teeth for the filtered hulls (C9, C16, C18) that can exclude D* -- and there it fires for a generator reason, not a theorem reason (see the hop-placement item). FIX: evaluate soundness at a budget the analyst could actually choose without knowing j_true (a fixed b, or a b picked by a declared data-free heuristic), and report the coverage curve over b rather than a single matched-budget bit.

THE RETRACTION HULL AND THE REVERSAL HULL ARE THE SAME SET AT EVERY BUDGET, not merely ordered. retract(A,S) = disjoint union over sigma subset of S of reverse(A,sigma), hence union_{|S|<=b} retract(S) = union_{|sigma|<=b} reverse(sigma) exactly. Measured 0 differences over 573 problems x b in {1,2} (AUDIT_masksweep.py). Consequences: (a) the control 'RETRACTION DOMINATES REVERSAL' is an identity that can only catch a typo, and the pilot's 'the two coincided exactly at b=1 and b=2' is the theorem, not evidence; (b) C6's flip hull is C1/C10's retraction hull under a second name, so two of the eighteen rows are one row and the falsification path 'every definition lands in the same class' is partly pre-purchased by arithmetic; (c) only C16 escapes, and only because its cost filter c(sigma) <= rho breaks the union. FIX: state the identity as a lemma, drop C6 as a distinct row or redefine it as an EXACT-sigma (not <= b) family, and replace that control with one that can fail.

FAMILY R IS SCORED AGAINST A LABEL IT IS PROVABLY BLIND TO, AND THE DECLARED PERMUTATION CONTROL CERTIFIES A SPURIOUS LIFT. lambda(k) = width(retract(A,{k})) - width(g0) drops column k, so lambda(k) is invariant to whether claim k was the flipped one: measured 0 violations over 400 problems x every column (AUDIT2.py, re-flipping column k and recomputing). Yet precision@1 at j_true=1 measures 0.494 against the design's chance rate 1/m = 0.352 -- and a data-free baseline that ranks claims by how many extensions of Chat disagree with them (pure reversibility, never touches tau, the SEM, or the query) scores 0.660, BEATING lambda (AUDIT3.py, n=500). The whole lift is the Meek-consistency rejection sampler: only a claim whose reversal stays consistent can be the planted false one. The declared control (a uniform permutation on the same instances) reproduces 0.352 and would therefore report lambda's 0.494 as 'large lift'. Deeper: under the paper's own premise (K is consistent with the data), false claims are unidentifiable within the MEC in principle, so direction (4) cannot be graded as false-claim retrieval at all. FIX: add the reversibility baseline as the null (not a uniform permutation), and regrade family R against a LOAD-BEARING label (does retracting k change Z's validity or move tau) rather than the falsity label -- and say in the paper that falsity retrieval is impossible by construction, which is itself the honest finding.

THE PRIMARY OUTCOME IS NOT THE QUESTION, AND EITHER READING OF IT IS WRONG. The paper is judged on mean width at 95 per cent calibrated coverage; the experiment grades the SHAPE of the nu ECDF and pre-declares atom >= 0.60 as DEGENERATE. The coverage column the design omits settles it, from the same cache, in one pass: measured on 900 problems, |K|<=6, j_true ~ U{0,1,2} (AUDIT5.py) -- budget 0: coverage 0.618 at 0.002x blanket width; budget 1: coverage 0.840 at 0.699x; budget 2: coverage 1.000 at 0.936x; budget 3+: 1.000 at 0.99x. So the first budget reaching 95 per cent coverage costs 93.6 per cent of the blanket width -- a 6.4 per cent saving, and that is the paper's answer. The pre-declared rule instead reports budget 1's atom of 0.653 as DEGENERATE, while budget 1's mean nu of 0.704 could be sold to a reader as a 30 per cent win. Both readings are wrong for the same missing column. An atom is not r_val's disease: r_val died of being a MINIMUM, not of having a mode; importing the 0.689 threshold onto a bounded width ratio convicts candidates that win the metric. FIX: make (coverage, mean width / mean blanket width) over budgets a CO-PRIMARY outcome computed on the full population, and demote the ECDF/atom summary to a diagnostic. It costs nothing extra -- the same masks.

THE |K| AXIS IS CONFOUNDED WITH THE BASELINE, AND THE ONLY TIEBREAK READS THE CONFOUND. |und(Chat)| is capped at 7 while m = min(m_max,|und|), so m/|und| measures 0.510 / 0.908 / 0.993 across the |K| <= 2/4/6 cells, and the budget-0 (G0) width share of the blanket falls 0.339 / 0.087 / 0.000 -- in the |K|<=6 cell G0 has essentially no free edges and is a single DAG (P(width(G0)=0) = 1.000, AUDIT2.py, n=95). The plain retraction hull's atom then falls 0.842 -> 0.674 -> 0.653 across those cells (AUDIT_masksweep.py) purely because the baseline shrank. The pre-declared BORDERLINE tiebreak is 'the atom must fall monotonically across the three |K| strata', which every hull definition satisfies mechanically. So the one rule allowed to promote a borderline row is a rule that cannot fail. FIX: report nu relative to the G0 baseline, (width(hull) - width(G0)) / (blanket - width(G0)); decouple m from |und| by sampling m independently and reporting the free-edge count as a covariate; and replace the tiebreak with monotonicity at fixed (|und|, free-edge count).
serious: THE nu=1 ATOM IS MOSTLY THE IDA tau=0 CONVENTION, NOT MEEK CASCADE. Measured: of the ~414 informative problems with nu(b=1) = 1, 305 (73.7 per cent) have a hull containing a world where y is not a descendant of x, i.e. a world whose tau was set to 0 by the convention (AUDIT_masksweep.py). Blanket width then spans the 0-vs-tau* jump and nu saturates the moment one direction-reversing world enters the hull. The headline statistic is therefore largely measuring 'does one retraction admit a world where x does not cause y' -- a different question from the one asked. FIX: stratify every ECDF on whether the hull contains a non-descendant world, report a second nu over direction-preserving worlds only, and say explicitly whether the paper's estimand is the IDA multiset (0 included) or the effect conditional on causal order.

MEEK-CONSISTENCY REJECTION IS j_true-DEPENDENT, SO THE THREE CELLS ARE DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. Measured acceptance 56.7 / 46.4 / 32.5 per cent at j_true = 0/1/2 (rejections 206/312/560 for 270 kept each; Meek-inconsistency alone 0 / 76 / 184, AUDIT_masksweep.py). Two flips survive only when both reversals are structurally harmless, so the j=2 cell is selected toward benign perturbations -- which biases the whole design toward finding damage smaller and definitions less degenerate than they are. FIX: paired design. Fix (D*, Chat, query, K-support, SEM), enumerate the admissible flip sets of each size on that one problem, and grade j_true WITHIN graph. That is not within-graph averaging of damage (still one query per graph), it is a matched comparison, and it removes the selection entirely.

TRUTHINESS BUG IN THE IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH: 'valid = [...] if Z else None'. The empty set is falsy. Measured Z = O*(G0) = empty on 352/810 problems, 43.5 per cent (AUDIT_masksweep.py). Every validity-based read-off (C12, C14, C15, C17, C18, the certificate rule, and r_val itself) would silently lose those rows, and the loss is correlated with the outcome -- Z = empty means no confounding under G0. proto.py has it right ('if Z is not None'); the sketch in the design does not. FIX: 'if Z is not None', and print the count of Z = empty problems as a first-line number since 43 per cent of the population has a trivial adjustment set.

Z IS DECLARED IDENTIFIED WHERE THE WORLDS ARE QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT, AND THE r_val = 0 CASE IS UNNAMED. Measured 42/810 problems (5.2 per cent) where the G0-extensions disagree about whether y is a descendant of x yet O* agrees (both empty) -- the exact empty-set ambiguity C13 documented, surviving the tau fix because the fix was applied to tau and not to the Z-identification step. Separately, in the lattice arm the analyst's own Z is already invalid inside G0's own extensions on 7/50 problems (14 per cent, AUDIT4.py), so r_val = 0 and the radius is undefined; the design never mentions this case and the relocation test would silently include it. FIX: identify Z only over the G0-extensions with y in de(x); report P(Z invalid at G0) and P(O* not identified) (measured 4.4 per cent) on the front page of every table.

THE RELOCATION TEST COMPARES TWO DIFFERENT METRICS. r_val counts BFS hops on the covering relation, but covering is model inclusion and a single covering step can retract several edges at once -- space.py's own docstring says the one-edge characterisation is false because of Meek propagation. The sweep's nu is indexed by CLAIM budget. Measured on 50 lattice problems (AUDIT4.py): r_val equals the claim budget j_val on 60 per cent, and P(j_val = 1 | r_val = 1) = 0.788, below the 0.95 relocation threshold for a units reason rather than a property of any definition. FIX: for each fibre, also compute the lattice distance from G0 of the MPDAG cl(Chat, K') that generates it, and run the relocation test on one common scale; or define both quantities on the claim scale and say so.

THE GENERATOR-PROVENANCE CHECK HAS NO DENOMINATOR AND NO TOLERANCE. 'Its atom must land near the paper's own 0.689.' Measured P(r_val = 1) = 33/50 = 0.660 including right-censored problems (12/50 never break) and 33/38 = 0.868 excluding them (AUDIT4.py). The paper's 0.689 sits between the two conventions, so the run passes or fails on an undeclared choice -- and the paper's 0.689 is over all problems while every other statistic here is on the informative stratum. FIX: declare the censoring convention, the conditioning set, and a numeric tolerance before the sweep.

THREE OF THE FIVE CONTROLS ARE THEOREMS ABOUT THE NUMPY, AND THE FOURTH IS VACUOUS. MONOTONE NESTING cannot fail (the hull is a union over a family growing in b, so max-min is monotone by construction). BLANKET ENDPOINT cannot fail (S = all claims is a member of the union at maximal budget, giving the all-ones mask). RETRACTION DOMINATES REVERSAL is an equality (fatal item 2). The tau CONVENTION check is vacuous as sited: the query is drawn with y in de_{D*}(x), so tau(D*) = true_total_effect is forced and the check can never see the O* = empty ambiguity it claims to catch -- that ambiguity lives in D_i not equal to D*. Only MASK IDENTITY is a real test, and it holds (verify_mask.py reproduced). FIX: move the tau check onto every extension (assert tau_i = 0 exactly when y not in de_{D_i}(x); assert O*(D_i) is a valid adjustment set in D_i); add a control that no reported hull is ever empty; add the reversibility baseline from fatal item 3.

HOP-LOCALISED DEFINITIONS ARE GRADED AGAINST AN UNDECLARED FALSE-CLAIM PLACEMENT, WHICH IS THE ONE ASSUMPTION THE 'DAMAGE IS LOCAL' BET RESTS ON. The generator flips claims uniformly over the m sampled edges. Measured hop of the planted false claim: 270/102/49/19/2 at hops 0-4, plus 58 (11.6 per cent) whose endpoints are not connected to {x,y} in the skeleton at all (AUDIT3.py, n=500). A C9-style hop-0/budget-1 hull then covers the truth on 0.540 of problems and is flagged zero-and-wrong on 59/500 -- a verdict that is a readout of the flip placement, not of the definition. FIX: make false-claim placement a declared axis (uniform / hop-concentrated / far-concentrated) and report every hop-localised candidate against all three. Separately, the 11.6 per cent of claims that cannot touch the query inflate every |set|/|K| denominator in family S; report |K| restricted to the query's skeleton component.

THE THRESHOLDS ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS FAMILIES AND FAMILY I CAN NEVER PASS. |K| <= 2 forces m = 2 (measured, AUDIT2.py), so index/m has support {0, 0.5, 1} and the NON-DEGENERATE criterion '>= 8 distinct values' is unreachable in that cell; |K| <= 4 gives m in {3,4}, at most 5 values. So family I (the r_val baseline, C2's j_sat, C10's ladder rung, C13's t_val, C17's j_val) is convicted in six of nine cells by support size alone. Meanwhile a bounded ratio in [0,1] carries a structural atom at exactly 1.000 that an integer index does not, so applying r_val's 0.689-calibrated 0.60 to both is a coincidence of numbers rather than a calibration. FIX: per-family thresholds on a support-normalised spread (normalised entropy or Simpson index over the achievable support), declared per cell.

THE CACHE AS SKETCHED CANNOT SERVE C2 OR C17. A is built over the m ELICITED claims, but C2 ranges over minimal generating subsets of dir(G0) minus dir(Chat) -- the Meek-IMPLIED orientations, which are not columns of A -- and C17's admissible-pattern counts have the same shape. FIX (cheap, and it preserves the whole cost argument): build A over all of und(Chat) (at most 7 columns) rather than only K's m, and keep a K -> column map. Every derived orientation is then a column and every fibre stays a bitmask.

THE n-AXIS IS A REPARAMETRISATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. w(n) = (z*se + h)/(z*se + h_blanket) uses the SAME se (max asymptotic_variance over ext) for every definition, so w(n) is a monotone function of nu and one per-problem scalar and adds no ordering information -- as n grows it converges to nu, as n shrinks to 1. It is also an additive construction while the target metric calibrates by SCALING an interval, so it computes a quantity the width table will never use. FIX: drop it, or compute se inside each definition's own hull and measure width-at-coverage at finite n by simulation on one cell only.

INFORMATIVE-STRATUM-ONLY REPORTING, AND A SEED CHECK THAT CANNOT FIRE. Measured informative share 0.707-0.722, close to the claimed 0.760. But dropping the ~29 per cent of problems with blanket width 0 removes about 30 per cent of the DENOMINATOR of the metric the paper is judged on (mean width), and the share is generator-dependent (the design itself cites 0.328 for C2 and 0.213 for C11), so cross-candidate atom comparisons sit on different populations. Separately, +/- 0.05 across two seeds is about 4 standard errors at n = 1500 (SE ~ 0.012), so the stability check will essentially never fire; and a seed change redraws graph, query, K and SEM together, so it isolates nothing. FIX: report the full-population mean width alongside the stratum ECDF, per definition with its own N; replicate on a structural knob (the |und| window, the p range) instead of the seed; and add a SEM-only redraw arm on fixed graphs (free -- no re-enumeration) to report how much of nu's variance is the SEM draw.

THE CLASS IS SMALL BY CONSTRUCTION AND THE 'NO DISCRIMINATION' NULL IS PARTLY PRE-PURCHASED. |und| in [3,7] gives measured mean |ext(Chat)| = 11.0 (modes 8, 6, 12; max 24 in this run) and mean |enumerate_space| = 32.5. C17's result that the whole class yields identical candidate adjustment sets on 100.0 per cent of instances is exactly what a class this small predicts, and falsification path (2) names that regime itself. FIX: add a cell with |und| in [8,12] capped on |ext| (say <= 512) instead of on |und|; the cache is linear in |ext| and the measured 2.5 ms/kept problem leaves ample budget.

THE QUERY IS DRAWN WITH ORACLE KNOWLEDGE. Pairs are sampled uniformly from {(x,y) : y in de_{D*}(x)}, which an analyst cannot do; they choose a query from Chat. This selects against precisely the queries whose causal order is in dispute -- the regime that produces the tau = 0 jump above -- and excludes null effects, where the IDA convention is benign. FIX: draw the query from ordered pairs connected in Chat regardless of the truth, and report the effect-is-zero-in-truth stratum separately.

MINOR, MEASURED NON-ISSUES worth recording so nobody re-litigates them. (a) The mask identity holds: verify_mask.py reproduced, and 0 violations over 573 problems x b in {1,2} in an independent implementation. (b) The back-door implementation is sufficient-only and could in principle over-report invalidity, but measured 0 of 1475 back-door-invalid instances are valid under the generalized adjustment criterion (AUDIT2.py) -- at these graph sizes it is not a source of bias. (c) width(empty mask) = 0.0 is a live trap for the filtered hulls (C9, C16, C18), which can be empty where the union families cannot; it did not fire in 500 draws of the C9 hull but it would fabricate a zero-width 'certificate' and then an UNSOUND verdict. Make an empty hull NaN, not 0.
dAudits.fixes:
"PRIORITISED, ALL CHEAP ON THE EXISTING CACHE.

1. Add the coverage column and make it co-primary. For every definition and every budget, report (coverage of tau*, mean width / mean blanket width) on the FULL population, plus the smallest budget reaching 95 per cent coverage and its width ratio. That single table is the paper's question; the pilot answer on this generator is budget 2, coverage 1.000, width 0.936x blanket -- a 6.4 per cent saving. Keep the ECDF/atom summary as a diagnostic and stop letting it issue verdicts.

2. Move the certificate rule off the matched budget. Grade soundness at a budget chosen without j_true (fixed b, or a declared data-free rule), and report coverage as a curve. At matched budget the rule is a tautology for twelve of the eighteen candidates (measured 0/573).

3. Prove and then drop the retraction/reversal duplication. State union_{|S|<=b} retract(S) = union_{|sigma|<=b} reverse(sigma) as a lemma, delete C6 as a distinct row or redefine it on exact-sigma fibres, and replace the dominance control with something that can fail.

4. Regrade family R. Score against a load-bearing label (retraction changes Z-validity or moves tau), not against falsity, and use the reversibility baseline (rank by column disagreement count in A) as the null instead of a uniform permutation. Measured: lambda 0.494 vs reversibility 0.660 vs uniform 0.352. State in the paper that within-MEC false-claim retrieval is impossible under the paper's own premise -- that is a result, not a gap.

5. Kill the |K| confound. Report nu relative to the G0 baseline, (width(hull) - width(G0)) / (blanket - width(G0)); sample m independently of |und|; record the free-edge count as a covariate; and rewrite the tiebreak as monotonicity at fixed (|und|, free edges). As written the tiebreak promotes on an artefact (baseline width share 0.339 -> 0.087 -> 0.000).

6. Paired j_true. Fix (D*, Chat, query, K-support, SEM) and vary only the flip set, enumerating admissible flip sets per size. Removes the 56.7 / 46.4 / 32.5 per cent acceptance gradient without touching the one-query-per-graph rule.

7. Declare false-claim placement as an axis (uniform / hop-concentrated / far-concentrated). Every hop-localised candidate (C9, C16, C18) is currently graded by an undeclared uniform prior; its measured coverage of 0.540 is a property of that prior.

8. Cache fixes: A over all of und(Chat), not only K's m columns (C2, C17 need the Meek-implied orientations); 'if Z is not None' not 'if Z' (43.5 per cent of problems have Z = empty); empty hull -> NaN, never width 0.0; identify Z only over G0-extensions with y in de(x); relative not absolute threshold on the informative filter.

9. Stratify on the tau = 0 mechanism. Report nu split by whether the hull swallows a world with y not in de(x); 73.7 per cent of the nu = 1 atom is that, and it is the mechanism, not a nuisance.

10. Declare the r_val provenance convention (censoring, conditioning set, numeric tolerance) before the run; 0.660 vs 0.868 on the same 50 problems depending on how censored problems are counted.

11. Per-family, support-normalised degeneracy thresholds. The '>= 8 distinct values' rule is unreachable for family I in the |K| <= 2 and |K| <= 4 cells (support size 3 and 5).

12. Add a larger-class cell (|und| in [8,12], cap on |ext| not on |und|), a SEM-only redraw arm on fixed graphs, and replicate on a structural knob rather than the seed. Drop the analytic n-axis or recompute se per hull.

13. Fix the vacuous controls: assert the tau convention on every extension (not only D*), assert O*(D_i) valid in D_i, assert no hull is empty. Keep the mask-identity control -- it is the only one that could ever fail, and it holds."
dAudits.verdict: "REVISE BEFORE RUNNING. The cost argument is sound and reproduces (mask identity 0 violations; 2.5 ms per kept problem measured on this machine; mean |ext| = 11.0), so the one-cache/eighteen-read-offs mechanism is real and worth keeping. The grading is not. As specified the experiment cannot fail in the directions it claims to test and cannot answer the question it is a precondition for: the certificate rule is a tautology at matched budget for twelve of eighteen candidates (0/573 measured); the retraction and reversal families are literally the same set at every budget, so one of the two 'controls' is an equality theorem; the retrieval arm scores a statistic that is provably blind to its label, and its declared permutation control certifies a lift that a data-free reversibility baseline beats (0.660 vs 0.494 vs 0.352 chance); the only rule allowed to promote a borderline candidate is satisfied mechanically by the |K| axis, because the G0 baseline width share falls 0.339 -> 0.087 -> 0.000 across the three cells while m/|und| rises 0.51 -> 0.91 -> 0.99. And 73.7 per cent of the nu = 1 atom the whole design is built to interrogate is manufactured by the IDA tau = 0 convention swallowing a direction-reversed world, not by Meek cascade. Most damaging: the target metric needs a coverage column the design deliberately omits. Adding it costs nothing and already answers the paper's question on this generator -- coverage 0.618 / 0.840 / 1.000 at budgets 0 / 1 / 2 with widths 0.002 / 0.699 / 0.936 of the blanket, so the first budget reaching 95 per cent coverage saves 6.4 per cent of width. Read without that column, budget 1's mean nu of 0.704 looks like a 30 per cent win and its atom of 0.653 looks like a DEGENERATE verdict; both are wrong. Land fixes 1-5 (coverage co-primary, unmatched-budget certificate, retraction/reversal lemma, load-bearing relabelling of family R, baseline-relative nu with a de-confounded tiebreak) and the sweep becomes worth its four minutes -- and it will most likely report that the selective-widening bet is dead on this generator, which is a publishable negative if it is stated with the coverage column beside it and a declared prior over how many claims the expert got wrong. That prior, currently a factorial nuisance uniform on {0,1,2}, is the single parameter that determines the headline number and needs defending in the paper, not stratifying in the appendix."

fatal: THE CENTRAL CONTRAST IS A THEOREM, NOT A MEASUREMENT: SEL is identically BUD(1). Under the centre gate, Z0 is valid in every extension of G0, so Theta(empty) is a *single point* (= theta-hat(Z0)), not a set. For any claim k outside L, Z0 is valid in every extension of apply_orientations(C, K\{k}); back-door validity means every such DAG's tau equals the same population coefficient on Z0 (including the IDA tau=0 cases, where validity forces the coefficient to be 0 too). So Theta({k}) = Theta(empty) for every k not in L, and the union over L equals the union over all of K. Verified on this machine: SEL width == BUD(1) width on 250/250 problems and 152/152 non-trivial ones (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josecosta-mugango/1cbd3bff-6ceb-4991-8a2a-b20d5a3f01d3/scratchpad/audit_sit.py, seed 20260907, mean ratio 0.7905, median 1.0000, 75.7% exact ties, 17.8% exact zeros). The design's own pilots (raw 0.7529 vs 0.7529; calibrated 0.4983 vs 0.4983; C12's 300/300) are this identity re-measured three times. FIX: prove it as a one-paragraph lemma, delete the SEL-vs-BUD(1) comparison, and re-aim the experiment at the only live axis, the budget ladder j = 0,1,2,|K| against BLANKET. The lemma is a *positive* result to keep: the screen returns the same interval as the full budget-1 hull while enumerating |L| fibres instead of |K|, so SEL is a cost method, not a width method.

THE PRIMARY OUTCOME CANNOT RESPOND TO THE TREATMENT. With the lambda >= 1 floor and every ignorance row already covering at lambda = 1 (the pilot's own lambda* = 1.00 for SEL, LOC, BLANKET), W95 is just the mean *raw* hull width. Raw hull width is a deterministic function of (C-hat, K_asserted, Sigma); it does not depend on whether any claim is true. Measured: SEL's raw width is bit-identical between b_true = 0 and b_true = 1 on 85/110 paired problems, and rho* at b_true = 0 is 0.76 -- already under the 0.85 decision threshold with no damage anywhere in the design (audit_sit2.py, seed 4242, 250 paired problems). So decision rule (1) is satisfiable by the honest-analyst arm, and Negative Control C is guaranteed to fire. The experiment as written measures how often the equivalence class reopens, which is question (c) of its own three-way decomposition, and calls the answer a width method. FIX: couple width to coverage by calibrating every row to *exactly* 0.95 (allow lambda < 1, or add an additive pad so a zero-width report can be inflated), and pre-register the primary as rho*(b=1) - rho*(b=0), the damage-induced increment, not rho*(b=1).

DECISION RULE (2) IS PRE-SATISFIED, AND BY AN ARTIFACT OF THE KNOB. The rule says an uncalibratable PERM satisfies it 'by that fact alone', and the pilot already measured PERM uncalibratable -- so the condition is met before the run. The uncalibratability is mechanical, not evidential: the knob multiplies only the ignorance half, and a random subset that misses the load-bearing claim has ignorance half exactly 0, which no multiplier can move. The paper's own target metric scales the *whole* interval, and PERM's interval always has width >= 2*1.96*se-hat > 0, so under the metric as stated PERM is always calibratable and Delta_sel is a real number. This is not PERM-specific: SEL's own ignorance half is exactly zero on 60/120 problems (audit_sit4.py, seed 777), so under a generator where SEL's marginal coverage dipped below 0.95 the same knob would condemn SEL as uncalibratable. FIX: make the primary calibration the target metric's own procedure -- one scalar multiplying the whole interval -- keep the two-knob split as a sensitivity, and delete the 'uncalibratable implies (2) is satisfied' clause. Then Delta_sel is a width comparison at equal coverage, which is what it claims to be.

DECISION RULE (3) CANNOT BE MET ON WIDTH: Delta_loc <= 0 by construction. Hull width is monotone in the hedged set and every claim outside L contributes a fibre equal to the base point, so W(LOC) <= W(L) for every problem regardless of hop structure. Measured: LOC < SEL on 23/152 non-trivial problems, LOC > SEL on 0/152 (audit_sit.py). Worse, the F4 factor's own definition fixes the baseline's content: in NEAR cells every claim is incident to X or Y so LOC = K = BUD(1) = SEL and Delta_loc = 0 exactly; in FAR cells LOC is empty (measured: LOC empty on 90/250 problems) so LOC is a zero-ignorance row; only MIXED can separate them, and only through the calibration knob. Pooling Delta_loc with equal cell weights over F4 therefore measures the level mix of a factor the experimenter chose. FIX: replace the three-level locality factor with a graded covariate (fraction of claims incident to {X,Y}, or mean skeleton-hop of K), define Delta_loc only where LOC is neither empty nor all of K, and state plainly that any positive Delta_loc is a coverage statement about LOC's misses, never a width statement.

THE CENTRE GATE IS A COLLIDER ON THE PHENOMENON BEING MEASURED, AND MOST OF IT IS THE O*-RETURNS-EMPTY TRAP THE DESIGN BELIEVES IT FIXED. Measured (audit_sit3.py, seed 99, 400 gate-eligible problems): P(residual ambiguity of G0 within one hop of X or Y) = 0.664 among gate-excluded problems against 0.254 among kept ones -- the gate removes near-query ambiguity at 2.6x the rate, and near-query ambiguity is precisely where the paper's own hop law puts the damage (0.1376 at hop 0 vs 0.000423 at hop >= 2). And 95 of the 128 exclusions came from the *second* half of the gate (Z0 not None yet not valid in G0), which fires when optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag reports spurious agreement because optimal_adjustment_set_dag returns the empty set in every extension where Y is not a descendant of X. So the gate silently drops the non-amenable stratum -- the one where the blanket hedge is widest and the selective story is most interesting -- under the label 'the analyst's own indecision', and the design's IDA fix protects tau but not Z0. FIX: split and report the two gate branches; define Z0 by a convention that exists on every G0 (an MPDAG-level optimal set, or the minimal element of all_valid_adjustment_sets_mpdag(G0,X,Y), plus an explicit amenability test on G0); and run the primary on the excluded stratum with the Z_pa map, which is defined everywhere.

THE 'WITHIN-PROBLEM PAIRED DESIGN' IS BROKEN BY POST-TREATMENT EXCLUSION. Both exclusion gates read K_asserted, so both are caused by the planted error. Measured (audit_sit2.py, 250 problems run at b_true = 0 and b_true = 1 on the same D*, C-hat, SEM, query and K_true): the Meek-refusal verdict differs between the two arms on 50/250 problems, the centre-gate verdict on 48/250, and only 110/250 (44%) are usable in both arms. If cells are refilled to 150 *kept* problems per arm -- which is what 'target 150 problems per cell' implies -- the five arms run on five different populations selected on a post-treatment variable, and Negative Control C, the b=2 contrast and every 'graph-level variance is differenced out' claim are between-population comparisons. FIX: draw until 150 problems pass Meek and the centre gate in *all five* arms, keep that intersection as the analysis set, and report the per-arm refusal rates separately as the scope statement they are meant to be (they bound 'no existing check flags that', which is a genuine and useful number).
serious: rho* <= 0.85 is a statement about `_random_dag`, not about the method. The per-problem ratio is two-atom, so the mean is approximately 1 - P(ratio = 0): measured 75.7% at exactly 1, 17.8% at exactly 0, median 1.0000, mean 0.7905, closely reproducing the design's own pilot (70.3 / 21.2 / 1.000 / 0.7529). The threshold therefore reduces to 'at least ~15% of drawn problems carry a chordal component that supplies the blanket width and touches nothing near the query', a property of the Erdos-Renyi-plus-random-topological-order generator at n in {8,12}. FIX: report rho* per configuration with the atom masses in the same cell (the design already commits to this -- make it the primary, not a companion), add a generator-family sensitivity (other p regimes, a block or scale-free generator, and a real-CPDAG corpus if one can be had), and say in the paper that rho* is not transportable.

rho* is a ratio of means and is therefore weighted by |tau*|, an exogenous SEM draw. The IDA convention places a hull endpoint at exactly 0 whenever some extension has Y not a descendant of X: measured on 59.3% of non-trivial problems, and there the blanket width runs at the scale of the effect itself (mean width 0.9604 vs mean |tau*| 0.8982; overall corr(width, |tau*|) = 0.506 -- audit_sit5.py, seed 31337, 300 problems). So the paper's headline 'mean width required for honest 95% coverage' is denominated in random_sem's Uniform(0.3,1.5) weights and the generator's path-length distribution, and is not commensurable with any width DoubleML or a PFN would report on real data. FIX: publish the median ratio and a scale-free width (width / |tau*|, or width in se-hat units) beside the mean, and report the fraction of hull endpoints supplied by the tau = 0 convention as a first-class number rather than a footnote to the naive-vs-IDA arm.

Marginal calibration plus stratified reporting leaks coverage. lambda is fit on the calibration half, but the primary is reported only on the non-trivial stratum, while 43-46% of problems are trivial and covered by every row. A row can reach 0.95 marginally while covering about 0.91 conditionally on the stratum that is actually reported, and the leak favours precisely the narrow rows whose failures live in that stratum. FIX: calibrate on the same stratum that is reported, and print per-stratum and per-cell empirical coverage next to every width so a reader can see which rows over- or under-cover.

Two of the five arms do not exist in part of the factorial. m = max(1, round(s*u)) equals 1 in the (narrow, s = 1/3) cells, so b_true = 2 is undefined there; and in every FAR cell no claim is at hop 0, so the 'concentrated' error model is identical to the exchangeable one, which silently voids the declared sensitivity arm in a third of the design and means C16's +0.31% -> +7.79% swing can only be reproduced on NEAR and MIXED cells. FIX: pre-specify the cell subset on which each arm is defined and report each arm only there, with the equal-weight pooling restricted to that subset.

Negative Control B is not guaranteed to be zero and is defined from the outcome. 'Vertex-disjoint from {X,Y} + Z0 + every enumerated O*(D)' does not exclude the causal nodes cn(X,Y) = de(X) intersect (an(Y) + {Y}), which lie in neither Z0 nor any O* (since O* = pa(cn) \ cn); reorienting inside such a component changes de(X) and hence tau. Measured: 1 of 70 placebo-eligible components contained a node that is causal in some extension (audit_sit2.py). Under the stated rule a hit voids the run or is read as a refutation of the locality premise, so this is a false-alarm generator wired to the strongest branch in the decision tree. FIX: construct the placebo instead of discovering it -- append a synthetic component structurally disconnected from D* and assert bit-identity of every number -- and drop the outcome-defined variant.

The L screen conflates two different failures. is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag returns False both when Z0 is invalid in some extension and when enumerate_dag_extensions(g) comes back empty ('conservatively returns False'), so a retracted graph with no extension would be scored load-bearing. FIX: assert a non-empty extension set for every retracted graph, count any empty case separately, and derive validity and the fibre from one shared enumerate_dag_extensions call rather than three (is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag, optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag and the fibre each re-enumerate today).

Three of the ten sanity checks cannot fail. S4 (nesting) is definitional given retraction monotonicity; S3 (ladder endpoints) is definitional because retracting all of K returns C-hat; S5 (the membership certificate) follows from Meek soundness whenever every remaining claim was read off D*, which the generator guarantees. Their 300/300 pass rates certify the cache and the indexing, which is worth having, but they are not evidence for the budget-j theorem and must not be presented as such. FIX: relabel them regression assertions and add a check that can actually fail -- that ext(G0) is a subset of ext(C-hat) on every problem, and that no extension of G0 carries a v-structure absent from C-hat.

p is not balanced within cells, contrary to the design's claim. Rejection sampling on the u band selects p: (n = 8, wide) will accept almost only p = 0.34 and (n = 8, narrow) almost only p = 0.18, so 'density varies inside every cell rather than tracking any factor' is false and density stays confounded with F2, which is the factor the design most wants clean. FIX: record the realised p distribution per cell and post-stratify to a common one, or fix p per cell and let u be an outcome with its conditional distribution reported.

The two unfillable cells are reported as an epistemic finding when they are a generator property. '(n=8, wide, saturated, FAR) occurred 0 times' follows from drawing the query uniformly among ordered pairs with Y in de(X) *after* the graph: in a wide class the ambiguous component is large and likely to touch a randomly chosen causal pair. It says nothing about what analysts can avoid. FIX: report it with the attempt counts as a property of the generator plus the query-sampling rule, and drop the sentence about analysts.

The permutation test's null and its resolution are underspecified. B = 200 gives a smallest attainable p of 1/201 = 0.005 against a threshold of p < 0.01, and combining across problems requires the same permutation index b in every problem for the joint null to exist; it is also unstated whether lambda is refit per draw b or once for the PERM row. FIX: raise B to at least 1000, fix a shared permutation index across problems, and write the calibration rule for PERM explicitly (one lambda per draw b, statistic = mean over b, p-value from the distribution over b).

Currency mismatch with the object the paper defines, plus an unexamined fourth mechanism for the ratio-1 atom. The paper's space is BFS hop count on the covering relation of G_Chat; the experiment measures hulls over *claim-retraction budgets*, and one retraction can un-orient many Meek-implied edges. Separately, retracting a claim whose orientation the remaining claims re-derive through Meek is a no-op, which produces ratio-1 problems for a reason none of the design's three named causes (a), (b), (c) covers -- and it makes the cardinality-matched PERM unfair in an unexamined direction, since a random claim is more often redundant than a load-bearing one. FIX: state the currency change as a redefinition and prove the containment theorem in the currency actually measured; match PERM on the number of *effective* retractions (claims whose retraction strictly enlarges the extension set), not on |L|.

Implementation details worth fixing before the run. (i) RNG: the sketch draws the planted error E from the same stream before random_sem, so the SEM is not in fact shared across arms as the pairing claims; spawn named substreams via SeedSequence for graph / query / claims / error / SEM / data, and note that S8 (PYTHONHASHSEED determinism) will not catch this. (ii) Node labels n0..n11 sort as strings, so for n = 12 MPDAG.nodes orders them n0, n1, n10, n11, n2, ...; harmless inside the repository because every index map is built from dag.nodes, but a landmine for the hand-written OLS layer -- use zero-padded labels. (iii) The finite-sample OLS uses the uncentered second-moment matrix with divisor n, consistent only because the SEM has mean zero; say so or centre, and use n - p in sigma-hat squared. (iv) CHECKED AND CLEAN, so do not spend design effort on it: the worry that the finite-sample hull is a max-statistic over unequal numbers of extensions (mean 3.7 for SEL vs 8.9 for BLANKET) and would inflate BLANKET more is not material at n = 1000 -- measured inflation +0.0002 for SEL and -0.0023 for BLANKET, rho* population 0.6898 vs finite 0.6896 (audit_sit4.py). Most extensions share the same O*, so their sample coefficients are literally identical.
dAudits.fixes:
"Priority order, and the first three change what the experiment is rather than how it is run.

1. Replace the SEL-vs-everything contrast with a lemma plus a budget ladder. Prove that under the centre gate Theta(empty) is a single point and Theta({k}) = Theta(empty) for every k outside L, so SEL = BUD(1) identically (250/250 here). The surviving empirical question is the ladder j = 0, 1, 2, |K| against BLANKET, with the two-atom decomposition attached to every cell. SEL then enters the paper as a computational result -- the same interval from |L| fibres instead of |K| -- which is defensible and is exactly what C12's 300/300 no-op already measured.

2. Make coverage the outcome and width the cost, in that order. The measured facts that survive every confound above are coverage facts: 0.720 with one reversed claim, 0.568 with two, 0.884 hedging over one revision, 0.9306 over the class. Width is a structural quantity that does not move with damage (raw SEL width identical across arms on 85/110 problems). So report: coverage by b_true and by row, then the width each row needs once every row is calibrated to exactly 0.95, with the atom masses and the median beside every mean. Pre-register rho*(b=1) - rho*(b=0) as the primary; rho*(b=1) alone is a generator statistic.

3. Fix the calibration knob, which currently manufactures two of the four decision-rule verdicts. Use the target metric's own procedure -- one scalar on the whole interval -- so no row is structurally uncalibratable, delete the 'uncalibratable implies rule (2) is satisfied' clause, and keep the ignorance-only two-knob version as a sensitivity with the lambda >= 1 soundness floor disclosed.

4. Repair the population. Keep only problems that pass Meek and the centre gate in all five arms (44% here, so budget for it); split and report the gate's two branches; give Z0 a convention that exists on every G0 so the near-query-ambiguity stratum is not thinned 2.6-fold; run the primary a second time on the gate-excluded stratum under Z_pa.

5. Repair the factorial. Locality becomes a graded covariate rather than a three-level factor whose extremes force LOC = K or LOC = empty; p is post-stratified to a common distribution within each u band; each arm is reported only on the cells where it is defined (b = 2 needs |K| >= 2, the concentrated model needs a hop-0 claim).

6. Repair the controls. Build the placebo by appending a disconnected synthetic component instead of discovering one from Z0 and the enumerated O*; match PERM on effective retractions rather than on |L|; raise B to 1000 with a shared permutation index; relabel S3, S4, S5 as regression assertions and add ext(G0) subset ext(C-hat) as a check that can fail.

7. Report scale honestly. Publish the fraction of hull endpoints supplied by the IDA tau = 0 convention (59.3% of non-trivial problems here) and a scale-free width, because the absolute widths are denominated in random_sem's weight draw and cannot be compared to a real-data competitor's.

Probe scripts, all runnable with PYTHONPATH=/Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src and each under two seconds: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josecosta-mugango/1cbd3bff-6ceb-4991-8a2a-b20d5a3f01d3/scratchpad/audit_sit.py (SEL = BUD identity, atom masses, LOC vs SEL), audit_sit2.py (arm-dependent exclusions, b=0 vs b=1 width, placebo eligibility), audit_sit3.py (gate collider, gate-branch split), audit_sit4.py (finite-sample inflation, zero-ignorance rate), audit_sit5.py (tau = 0 convention and width scale)."
dAudits.verdict: "Do not run it as written. The design is unusually disciplined -- its pilots reproduce on this machine (mean ratio 0.79 vs their 0.7529, ties 75.7% vs 70.3%, zeros 17.8% vs 21.2%), its exclusion accounting is honest, and its branch structure is written before the data. But the question it asks has already been settled analytically and the pre-registration would spend forty-five minutes of compute and a paper section confirming a theorem. SEL is identically BUD(1) (250/250, 152/152 non-trivial), so the selection contrast is vacuous; the primary outcome is the mean raw hull width, which is a deterministic function of structure and does not move with the planted error (identical across arms on 85/110 paired problems, and rho* = 0.76 in the arm with no damage at all, already under the 0.85 threshold); rule (2) is pre-satisfied by an artifact of scaling only the ignorance half, which no multiplier can lift off zero; rule (3) is unmeetable on width because the hull is monotone in the hedged set (LOC never wider than SEL, 0/152); and both exclusion gates read the treatment, leaving 44% of problems usable in all arms while the centre gate strips near-query ambiguity at 2.6 times the rate, which is exactly where the paper's own hop law puts the damage. The r_val degeneracy has been relocated, not removed: a minimum over a ball collapsing to 1 on 68.9% of problems has become a hull collapsing to the blanket on 75.7%, and the design's own fourth branch anticipates this. The honest and still-publishable experiment is the one hiding inside this one: prove the SEL = BUD(1) lemma, measure the budget ladder with the two-atom decomposition, make coverage the outcome and width its price at exactly 95%, and report the selective screen as a cost result -- the same interval from fewer enumerations -- rather than a width result."
